````ts
// The console descriptor registry (src/consoles.ts) held to the answers the shell gave before the descriptors existed:
// the classification table and the battery table are the ones recorded in ./recorded.ts from detectPlatform and
// romHasBattery, and the system-node field and stream tables are the ones recorded from buildGraph's SETTING_FIELDS,
// CONSTRUCT_FIELDS, CONFIG_PARAMS and streamsOf. Moving where a console's data lives must not move what it answers, so
// the recorded tables are the oracle here and the registry's own code paths are what is measured against them: the knob
// rows go through systemKnobs and droppedKnobs, the streams through the perChannel shape buildGraph wires, and the
// classification table through classifyRom's tiered reader.
//
// The rest of the file is what the descriptor's own shape has to hold: the registered platform and core sets
// projectConfig validates against, the splits' tap modes, a console that misdeclares itself, and the contributions the
// generated list builds.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { classifyRom } from "../../src/systemsStore";
import {
  CONSOLE_DESCRIPTORS,
  consoleFor,
  detectPlatform,
  detectorAnswer,
  platformEntry,
  registeredCores,
  registeredPlatforms,
  realCartOf,
  romHasBattery,
  sniffLengths,
} from "../../src/consoles";
import {
  buildGraph,
  droppedKnobs,
  exportModeOf,
  systemKnobs,
  type GraphModel,
  type GraphSystem,
} from "../../src/graph/buildGraph";
import { defaultCoreFor, systemNodeTypeFor } from "../../src/platform";
import type { ConsoleDescriptor } from "../../src/consoles";
import type { HostBackend } from "../../src/backend";
import { coreSchema, parseConfig, platformSchema } from "../../src/projectConfig";
import { BATTERY_CASES, CLASSIFY_CASES, FOREIGN_FIELDS, KNOB_TYPES, KNOB_VALUES, OWN_FIELDS } from "./cases";
import { RECORDED_BATTERY, RECORDED_CLASSIFY, RECORDED_KNOBS, RECORDED_STREAMS } from "./recorded";

// The recorded answers are JSON text ("-" for absent), so a value round-trips by that spelling.
const ABSENT = "-";
const spell = (v: unknown): string => (v === undefined ? "undefined" : JSON.stringify(v));
const decode = (s: string): unknown => (s === "undefined" ? undefined : JSON.parse(s));

test("a ROM classifies through the tiered reader, with the answers and the reads the old classifyRom made", () => {
  const wrong: string[] = [];
  const readWrong: string[] = [];
  // A reader that records what it was asked for: classifyRom is the one place ROM bytes enter TS, so its reads are the
  // registry's.
  const reads: number[] = [];
  const bytes = new Map<string, Uint8Array>();
  const reader = {
    readFilePrefix: (path: string, length: number) => {
      reads.push(length);
      return (bytes.get(path) ?? new Uint8Array()).subarray(0, length);
    },
  } as unknown as HostBackend;
  CLASSIFY_CASES.forEach((c, i) => {
    const path = `/x${c.ext ?? ""}`;
    bytes.set(path, c.bytes);
    reads.length = 0;
    const got = classifyRom(reader, path);
    const where = `${c.name}${c.ext === undefined ? "" : ` ${c.ext}`}`;
    if (got !== RECORDED_CLASSIFY[i]) wrong.push(`${where}: ${String(got)} (recorded ${RECORDED_CLASSIFY[i]})`);
    // The cheap tier is the 0x134 detectors over the file's first 0x134 bytes: a file one of them claims costs that one
    // read, and anything else pays the deep read too (the Sega header sits at a bank's end).
    const cheap = detectPlatform(c.bytes.subarray(0, 0x134), undefined);
    const want = cheap === "unknown" ? [0x134, 0x8200] : [0x134];
    if (JSON.stringify(reads) !== JSON.stringify(want)) {
      readWrong.push(`${where}: the reads ${reads.join(",")} (want ${want.join(",")})`);
    }
    if (cheap !== "unknown" && got !== cheap) {
      wrong.push(`${where}: answered ${String(got)} at the deep tier, the cheap one said ${cheap}`);
    }
  });
  if (wrong.length) console.log(`# classification differs:\n#   ${wrong.join("\n#   ")}`);
  if (readWrong.length) console.log(`# reads differ:\n#   ${readWrong.join("\n#   ")}`);
  expect(wrong).toEqual([]);
  expect(readWrong).toEqual([]);
});

test("the battery rule gives the answers the pre-descriptor rule gave", () => {
  const wrong: string[] = [];
  BATTERY_CASES.forEach((c, i) => {
    const got = romHasBattery(c.header, c.platform);
    if (got !== RECORDED_BATTERY[i]) wrong.push(`${c.name}: ${got} (recorded ${RECORDED_BATTERY[i]})`);
  });
  if (wrong.length) console.log(`# battery differs:\n#   ${wrong.join("\n#   ")}`);
  expect(wrong).toEqual([]);
});

test("a ROM is read in two tiers, the cheap one first, and the deep one only when the first declines", () => {
  // A reader that records what it was asked for: classifyRom is the one place ROM bytes enter TS, so its reads are the
  // registry's reads.
  const reads: number[] = [];
  const bytes: Record<string, Uint8Array> = {};
  const reader = {
    readFilePrefix: (path: string, length: number) => {
      reads.push(length);
      const whole = bytes[path] ?? new Uint8Array();
      return whole.subarray(0, Math.min(length, whole.length));
    },
  } as unknown as HostBackend;
  const load = (path: string, b: Uint8Array) => {
    bytes[path] = b;
    reads.length = 0;
    return classifyRom(reader, path);
  };

  // A Nintendo header answers in the first read and pays nothing more, whatever its extension says.
  expect(load("/roms/cart.gb", bytesOf(gbLike(), 0x8000))).toBe("gb");
  expect(reads).toEqual([0x134]);
  // A Sega header sits at the end of a bank, so a file the cheap tier declines costs the deep read.
  expect(load("/roms/cart.sms", bytesOf(segaLike(), 0x20000))).toBe("sms");
  expect(reads).toEqual([0x134, 0x8200]);
  // And a file carrying nothing at all is the second read's extension fallback.
  expect(load("/roms/cart.gg", new Uint8Array(0x8000))).toBe("gg");
  expect(reads).toEqual([0x134, 0x8200]);
  // The registry's tiers are the descriptors' distinct prefix lengths, ascending.
  expect(sniffLengths()).toEqual([0x134, 0x8200]);
});

test("each system node's setting, construct-time and param fields are the ones the old tables kept", () => {
  const wrong: string[] = [];
  for (const [type, field, spelledValue, settings, construct, params, dropped] of RECORDED_KNOBS) {
    if (!consoleFor(type)) {
      wrong.push(`${type}: no descriptor`);
      continue;
    }
    const config = { [field]: decode(spelledValue) };
    // The row is what the shell's own code answers: systemKnobs for the node's settings, construct fields and params,
    // and droppedKnobs for what the document leaves out.
    const answers = systemKnobs({ type, coreConfig: config });
    const has = (o: Record<string, unknown>) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o, field);
    const got = {
      settings: has(answers.settings) ? spell(answers.settings[field]) : ABSENT,
      construct: has(answers.construct) ? spell(answers.construct[field]) : ABSENT,
      params: has(answers.params) ? spell(answers.params[field]) : ABSENT,
      dropped: droppedKnobs(type, config).length > 0,
    };
    const want = [settings, construct, params, dropped] as const;
    const have = [got.settings, got.construct, got.params, got.dropped] as const;
    if (want.join("|") !== have.join("|")) {
      wrong.push(`${type} ${field} ${spelledValue}: ${have.join(" ")} (recorded ${want.join(" ")})`);
    }
  }
  if (wrong.length) console.log(`# fields differ:\n#   ${wrong.slice(0, 40).join("\n#   ")}`);
  expect(wrong).toEqual([]);
});

test("every stream layout the old streamsOf reported is the one buildGraph wires", () => {
  // The recorder read the streams through the one shape that prints them: a lone system in the perChannel shape wires
  // stream k to its own output bus, so the out node's `buses` and the ports the wires leave say which streams a mode
  // reports - and exportModeOf is measured on the way, since it is what the shape chooses the mode by.
  const wrong: string[] = [];
  const labels = ["mix", "stereoModPins", "pinsPlusRef", "individualMono"];
  for (const [type, mode, buses, ports] of RECORDED_STREAMS) {
    // Reach each mode the way a store does: the pins and channels splits by the routing (the engine's arm), the pin
    // reference layout by the stored export label. Only a NES reads either.
    const split = type === "rp.mesen.nes" && (mode === 1 || mode === 3);
    const routing = split ? (mode === 1 ? "pinSplit" : "channelSplit") : "onePerInstance";
    const system = {
      id: 1,
      platform: PLATFORM_OF[type],
      type,
      linkGroup: 0,
      exportMode: exportModeOf(type, { channelExportMode: labels[mode] }),
      resources: { rom: 1 },
      romName: "rom1",
      pipeline: [],
      coreConfig: { channelExportMode: labels[mode] },
    } as unknown as GraphSystem;
    const built = buildGraph({
      systems: [system],
      routing: routing as GraphModel["routing"],
      shape: { kind: "perChannel" },
    });
    const out = built.document.nodes.find((node) => node.id === "out")!;
    const wired = built.document.wires
      .filter((wire) => wire.to.startsWith("out.out."))
      .map((wire) => ({
        at: Number(wire.to.slice("out.out.".length).split("-")[0]),
        port: wire.from.slice("sys-1.".length),
      }))
      .sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at)
      .map((wire) => wire.port);
    if (JSON.stringify([out.settings?.buses, wired]) !== JSON.stringify([buses, ports])) {
      const got = JSON.stringify([out.settings?.buses, wired]);
      wrong.push(`${type} mode ${mode}: ${got} (recorded ${JSON.stringify([buses, ports])})`);
    }
  }
  if (wrong.length) console.log(`# streams differ:\n#   ${wrong.join("\n#   ")}`);
  expect(wrong).toEqual([]);
});

// The platform each recorded node type runs, as the store places it: the model only needs one a console registers.
const PLATFORM_OF: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  "rp.sameboy.gb": "gb",
  "rp.mesen.nes": "nes",
  "rp.mesen.gba": "gba",
  "rp.mesen.sms": "sms",
};

test("the fields cases.ts probes are the ones the descriptors hold, and a field another node owns is on none", () => {
  const wrong: string[] = [];
  for (const type of KNOB_TYPES) {
    const descriptor = consoleFor(type);
    if (!descriptor) {
      wrong.push(`${type}: no descriptor`);
      continue;
    }
    const fields = [
      ...Object.keys(descriptor.settingFields ?? {}),
      ...Object.keys(descriptor.constructFields ?? {}),
      ...(descriptor.configParams ?? []),
    ];
    // Every field the record probed as this type's own is one the descriptor carries, and nothing else is: a table
    // entry the case list missed would be a knob no test measures.
    const own = OWN_FIELDS[type].filter((field) => field !== "linkGroupId");
    if (JSON.stringify([...fields].sort()) !== JSON.stringify([...own].sort())) {
      wrong.push(`${type}: ${fields.join(",")} (own ${own.join(",")})`);
    }
    for (const field of FOREIGN_FIELDS[type]) if (fields.includes(field)) wrong.push(`${type} carries ${field}`);
  }
  expect(wrong).toEqual([]);
  // The value list covers each field's own accepted labels and numbers, which is what makes the record meaningful.
  const values = KNOB_VALUES.map(spell);
  expect(RECORDED_KNOBS.filter((record) => !values.includes(record[2])).map((record) => record[2])).toEqual([]);
});

test("the registry holds the consoles the product's packages contribute, each node type once", () => {
  const types = KNOB_TYPES.map((type) => consoleFor(type));
  expect(types.every((d) => d !== undefined)).toBe(true);
  const nodeTypes = types.map((d) => d!.nodeType);
  expect(new Set(nodeTypes).size).toBe(nodeTypes.length);
  // One descriptor per platform, and each platform's node type is the one the store places it with.
  const wrong: string[] = [];
  for (const platform of registeredPlatforms()) {
    const descriptor = consoleFor(systemNodeTypeFor(platform.id));
    if (!descriptor) wrong.push(`${platform.id}: no descriptor for its node`);
    else if (defaultCoreFor(platform.id) !== descriptor.core) {
      wrong.push(`${platform.id}: core ${String(defaultCoreFor(platform.id))}`);
    }
    if (platformEntry(platform.id)?.id !== platform.id) wrong.push(`${platform.id}: not in the platform list`);
  }
  expect(wrong).toEqual([]);
  // Every core a descriptor names is one the registry knows: the core-config role is named after its core, so a core
  // with no descriptor could not be configured by any role either.
  const cores = registeredCores();
  expect(cores).toEqual(["sameboy", "mesen"]);
  expect(types.filter((d) => !cores.includes(d!.core)).map((d) => d!.core)).toEqual([]);
  // The N8 is the one registered real cart, and it names a platform a descriptor registers.
  const cart = realCartOf("nes");
  expect(cart).toEqual({ platform: "nes", cartNode: "rp.n8.nes" });
  expect(platformEntry(cart!.platform) !== undefined).toBe(true);
  // The Game Gear is the one platform whose node needs a setting to be the right machine.
  expect(platformEntry("gg")?.nodeSettings).toEqual({ gameGear: true });
});

test("each split's tap mode is the export mode its config patch names", () => {
  // The mode a render builds a node in (the split's configPatch label) and the mode the engine arms for a lone system
  // (its tapMode) must be the same ordinal, or a split renders one layout and arms another.
  const wrong: string[] = [];
  for (const descriptor of CONSOLE_DESCRIPTORS) {
    for (const [name, split] of Object.entries(descriptor.splits ?? {})) {
      // A split that changes no config and arms no tap (the Game Boy's four channels) has no mode to agree on.
      if (split.tapMode === undefined && split.configPatch === undefined) continue;
      const modes = descriptor.exportModes;
      const label = modes === undefined ? undefined : split.configPatch?.[modes.field];
      const want = modes !== undefined && typeof label === "string" ? modes.values.indexOf(label) : -1;
      if (want < 0) {
        wrong.push(`${descriptor.id} ${name}: its patch names no export mode (tapMode ${String(split.tapMode)})`);
      } else if (split.tapMode !== want) {
        wrong.push(`${descriptor.id} ${name}: tapMode ${String(split.tapMode)}, the mode is ${want}`);
      }
    }
  }
  if (wrong.length) console.log(`# tap modes differ:\n#   ${wrong.join("\n#   ")}`);
  expect(wrong).toEqual([]);
});

test("a detector that answers a platform its own descriptor does not list is refused, naming the console", () => {
  // The registry's list is the product's, so a console that misdeclares itself cannot be registered in a test: the
  // classification's guard is exercised with the descriptor the registry would be handed.
  const misdeclared: ConsoleDescriptor = {
    id: "fixture.bad",
    core: "mesen",
    nodeType: "rp.fixture.bad",
    platforms: [{ id: "gb", label: "Game Boy", extensions: [".gb"] }],
    detect: { prefixBytes: 4, rank: 9, run: () => "n64" },
  };
  expect(detectorAnswer(misdeclared, "gb")).toBe("gb");
  expect(() => detectorAnswer(misdeclared, "n64")).toThrow('the console fixture.bad detects "n64"');
  expect(() => detectorAnswer(misdeclared, "n64")).toThrow("which its platforms do not list (gb)");
});

test("projectConfig refuses an unknown platform and core, naming the registered set", () => {
  const known = registeredPlatforms().map((p) => p.id);
  // The order is the descriptors': the product's, then a package's own list (mesen declares its GBA before its NES, so
  // the extension lists keep the order the shell's own lists had).
  expect(known).toEqual(["gb", "gba", "nes", "sms", "gg"]);
  expect(registeredCores()).toEqual(["sameboy", "mesen"]);
  const platform = platformSchema.safeParse("n64");
  expect(platform.success).toBe(false);
  expect(platform.error?.issues[0]?.message).toBe(`unknown platform "n64" (known: ${known.join(", ")})`);
  const core = coreSchema.safeParse("gambatte");
  expect(core.success).toBe(false);
  expect(core.error?.issues[0]?.message).toBe(`unknown core "gambatte" (known: sameboy, mesen)`);
  // parseConfig drops the entries that fail the strict parse silently, as it dropped an unknown platform's before, so
  // a file with one bad entry still loads the others.
  const loaded = parseConfig(
    JSON.stringify({
      schemaVersion: "4",
      systems: [
        { platform: "n64", core: "mesen" },
        { platform: "gb", core: "sameboy" },
      ],
    }),
  );
  expect(loaded.systems.map((s) => s.platform)).toEqual(["gb"]);
});

// ---- the byte builders the two-read test needs, kept minimal: the case list's fixtures are elsewhere ----------------

function bytesOf(at: { at: number; bytes: number[] }, len: number): Uint8Array {
  const b = new Uint8Array(len);
  b.set(at.bytes, at.at);
  return b;
}
function gbLike(): { at: number; bytes: number[] } {
  // The Game Boy logo's first bytes: enough for the 0x134 tier to answer, which is all this test is about.
  return {
    at: 0x104,
    bytes: [
      0xce, 0xed, 0x66, 0x66, 0xcc, 0x0d, 0x00, 0x0b, 0x03, 0x73, 0x00, 0x83, 0x00, 0x0c, 0x00, 0x0d,
      0x00, 0x08, 0x11, 0x1f, 0x88, 0x89, 0x00, 0x0e, 0xdc, 0xcc, 0x6e, 0xe6, 0xdd, 0xdd, 0xd9, 0x99,
      0xbb, 0xbb, 0x67, 0x63, 0x6e, 0x0e, 0xec, 0xcc, 0xdd, 0xdc, 0x99, 0x9f, 0xbb, 0xb9, 0x33, 0x3e,
    ],
  };
}
function segaLike(): { at: number; bytes: number[] } {
  return { at: 0x7ff0, bytes: [0x54, 0x4d, 0x52, 0x20, 0x53, 0x45, 0x47, 0x41] };
}
````

- [ ] **Step 9: The generator's fixtures, and the two tests that read them**

Five fixture modes hold the refusals the generated module raises (a duplicate platform, a duplicate node type, a core
with no system role, a real cart naming no platform, two carts on one platform, two carts on one node), the consoles
module itself is a sixth, `fixtures/expected/consoles.ts` is the emitted list the fixture product's own module
produces, and `fixtures/expected/packages.ts` follows `packages.ts`'s new import. `build-graph.test.ts` changes one
call site: the same assertion, with the node type passed beside the config, which is a forced signature change and not
a changed expectation.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/packages/fixtures/expected/consoles.ts`:

````ts
// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list and the
// packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and rebuild.
//
// The consoles the product's packages contribute, in product order, and the physical carts a project can drive.
// The descriptors say how a ROM is classified, which node type places a system, what that node's knobs and stream
// layouts are and how a render of it splits and shapes its output; a real cart says which platform's systems
// reach it. Nothing here imports an app module or zod: the planner reads this list, and a bundle of the planner
// must carry no role's schema (test/script/bundle-protocol.test.ts).
import type { ConsoleDescriptor, RealCart } from "@retroplug/core/consoles";
import consoles_alpha from "@retroplug/alpha/consoles";
import consoles_beta from "@retroplug/beta/consoles";

/** The consoles, in product order: each package's descriptors, which the classifier, the node table, the battery
 *  rules and the render are read from. */
export const CONSOLES: readonly ConsoleDescriptor[] = [
  ...(consoles_alpha.consoles ?? []),
  ...(consoles_beta.consoles ?? []),
];
// A platform id is looked up by the classifier, a stored project's validation and the menus, so one declared
// twice would leave one of the two consoles unreachable; a node type places a system, so two descriptors sharing
// one would make the node table depend on the order. (A descriptor's core must also be a system role, which
// ./packages.ts checks: the roles are its.)
const consolePlatforms = new Map<string, string>();
const consoleNodeTypes = new Map<string, string>();
for (const consoleDescriptor of CONSOLES) {
  for (const consolePlatform of consoleDescriptor.platforms) {
    const owner = consolePlatforms.get(consolePlatform.id);
    if (owner !== undefined) {
      throw new Error(`two console descriptors declare the platform ${consolePlatform.id}: ${owner} and ` +
        consoleDescriptor.id);
    }
    consolePlatforms.set(consolePlatform.id, consoleDescriptor.id);
  }
  const nodeOwner = consoleNodeTypes.get(consoleDescriptor.nodeType);
  if (nodeOwner !== undefined) {
    throw new Error(`two console descriptors declare the node type ${consoleDescriptor.nodeType}: ` +
      `${nodeOwner} and ${consoleDescriptor.id}`);
  }
  consoleNodeTypes.set(consoleDescriptor.nodeType, consoleDescriptor.id);
}

/** The physical carts a project can drive, in product order: each names the platform whose systems it receives
 *  and the node that owns its link. */
export const REAL_CARTS: readonly RealCart[] = [
  ...(consoles_alpha.realCarts ?? []),
  ...(consoles_beta.realCarts ?? []),
];
// One cart per platform and one per node, because a document places at most one: the store's lookup,
// buildGraph's placement and the menu's jobs all resolve a platform's cart, and with two registered the answer
// would be whichever package the product listed last.
const cartPlatforms = new Map<string, string>();
const cartNodes = new Map<string, string>();
for (const realCart of REAL_CARTS) {
  if (!consolePlatforms.has(realCart.platform)) {
    throw new Error(`the real cart ${realCart.cartNode} names the platform ${realCart.platform}, which no ` +
      "console descriptor registers");
  }
  const platformOwner = cartPlatforms.get(realCart.platform);
  if (platformOwner !== undefined) {
    throw new Error(`two real carts name the platform ${realCart.platform}: ${platformOwner} and ` +
      realCart.cartNode);
  }
  cartPlatforms.set(realCart.platform, realCart.cartNode);
  const nodeOwner = cartNodes.get(realCart.cartNode);
  if (nodeOwner !== undefined) {
    throw new Error(`two real carts name the cart node ${realCart.cartNode}: ${nodeOwner} and ` +
      realCart.platform);
  }
  cartNodes.set(realCart.cartNode, realCart.platform);
}
````

````diff
+        "packages/alpha/ts/consoles.ts",
+        consoleModule({
+          descriptors: [{ id: "alpha.nes", core: "alpha-core", nodeType: "rp.alpha.nes", platform: "nes" }],
+          realCarts: [{ platform: "nes", cartNode: "rp.alpha.cart" }],
+        }),
+      );
+      writeTree("packages/beta/ts/app.ts", consoleApp({ role: "beta-core" }));
+      writeTree(
+        "packages/beta/ts/consoles.ts",
+        consoleModule({
+          descriptors: [{ id: "beta.gba", core: "beta-core", nodeType: "rp.beta.gba", platform: "gba" }],
+          realCarts: [{ platform: "nes", cartNode: "rp.beta.cart" }],
+        }),
+      );
+      writeTree("packages/retroplug/src/app.ts", "export default {};\n");
+      generate({ root });
+      try {
+        result = await loadPackages();
+      } catch (e) {
+        result = { error: e.message };
+      }
+      break;
+    case "realcart-node-twice":
+      // Two packs naming one cart node: the node a document places for a cart would be claimed twice, and the second
+      // platform's systems would drive the first's link.
+      writeTree("packages/alpha/ts/app.ts", consoleApp({ role: "alpha-core", keepsApp: true }));
+      writeTree(
+        "packages/alpha/ts/consoles.ts",
+        consoleModule({
+          descriptors: [{ id: "alpha.nes", core: "alpha-core", nodeType: "rp.alpha.nes", platform: "nes" }],
+          realCarts: [{ platform: "nes", cartNode: "rp.alpha.cart" }],
+        }),
+      );
+      writeTree("packages/beta/ts/app.ts", consoleApp({ role: "beta-core" }));
+      writeTree(
+        "packages/beta/ts/consoles.ts",
+        consoleModule({
+          descriptors: [{ id: "beta.gba", core: "beta-core", nodeType: "rp.beta.gba", platform: "gba" }],
+          realCarts: [{ platform: "gba", cartNode: "rp.alpha.cart" }],
+        }),
+      );
+      writeTree("packages/retroplug/src/app.ts", "export default {};\n");
+      generate({ root });
+      try {
+        result = await loadPackages();
+      } catch (e) {
+        result = { error: e.message };
+      }
+      break;
     default:
       console.error(`run-generator.mjs: unknown mode "${MODE}"`);
       process.exit(2);
````

- [ ] **Step 11: The red proofs: the recorded tables, the absent modules, and three temporary mutations**

Four red proofs, the first two of them read-only. The stage 1 report records them all; the two commands below
reproduce the ones that need no edit of this tree, and the three mutations are the pass's own, each reversed by the
command after it.

**(a) The recorded tables are the OLD code's.** `recorded.ts` was produced by bundling `96d748e5c`'s `src/platform.ts`
(`detectPlatform`, `romHasBattery`) and `src/graph/buildGraph.ts` (`systemKnobs`, `droppedKnobs`, `exportModeOf`, and
`streamsOf` through `buildGraph`'s per-channel shape) over this task's `cases.ts`, BEFORE the first source edit, with
the throwaway recorder `/tmp/f4apro/record.mjs` (it lives outside the repository). Run it against a full `git archive`
of the parent tree and compare what it writes with the committed file: it must print `classify 97, battery 31, knobs
858, streams 16`, and the diff must be empty. The archive needs its own generator run first, because the old sources
import the generated `src/generated/protocol.ts` that a clone has none of; the recorder's bundle is written to
`/tmp/f4a-accept`, not into the prototype's work dir.

````js
// Records the console registry's tables from the code as it was before the descriptors existed, and writes
// packages/retroplug/test/consoles/recorded.ts. Throwaway (lives outside the repo), run once by hand:
//
//   node /tmp/f4apro/record.mjs
//
// It bundles a probe module with esbuild (the same resolution the test bundles use) and imports the OLD
// src/platform.ts (detectPlatform, romHasBattery), src/graph/buildGraph.ts (systemKnobs, droppedKnobs, buildGraph,
// exportModeOf) and the case list the test reads.
import { build } from "/workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/node_modules/esbuild/lib/main.js";
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const REPO = "/workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish";
const entry = `${REPO}/packages/retroplug/test/consoles/_record-entry.ts`;
const out = "/tmp/f4apro/record-bundle.mjs";
writeFileSync(
  entry,
  `import { detectPlatform, romHasBattery } from "${REPO}/packages/retroplug/src/platform";
import { buildGraph, systemKnobs, droppedKnobs, exportModeOf } from "${REPO}/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph";
import { CLASSIFY_CASES, BATTERY_CASES, KNOB_TYPES, OWN_FIELDS, FOREIGN_FIELDS, KNOB_VALUES, STREAM_MODES } from "${REPO}/packages/retroplug/test/consoles/cases";
export { detectPlatform, romHasBattery, buildGraph, systemKnobs, droppedKnobs, exportModeOf, CLASSIFY_CASES, BATTERY_CASES, KNOB_TYPES, OWN_FIELDS, FOREIGN_FIELDS, KNOB_VALUES, STREAM_MODES };
`,
);
await build({ entryPoints: [entry], bundle: true, platform: "node", format: "esm", outfile: out, target: "node20" });
const m = await import(out);

const ABSENT = "-";
const spell = (v) => (v === undefined ? "undefined" : JSON.stringify(v));

// ---- classification ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
const classify = m.CLASSIFY_CASES.map((c) => m.detectPlatform(c.bytes, c.ext));

// ---- battery ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
const battery = m.BATTERY_CASES.map((c) => m.romHasBattery(c.header, c.platform));

// ---- the system-node fields -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
const knobs = [];
for (const type of m.KNOB_TYPES) {
  for (const field of [...m.OWN_FIELDS[type], ...m.FOREIGN_FIELDS[type]]) {
    for (const value of m.KNOB_VALUES) {
      const config = { [field]: value };
      const answers = m.systemKnobs({ type, coreConfig: config });
      const has = (o) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o, field);
      const settings = has(answers.settings) ? spell(answers.settings[field]) : ABSENT;
      const construct = has(answers.construct) ? spell(answers.construct[field]) : ABSENT;
      const params = has(answers.params) ? spell(answers.params[field]) : ABSENT;
      const dropped = m.droppedKnobs(type, config).length > 0;
      knobs.push([type, field, value === undefined ? "undefined" : JSON.stringify(value), settings, construct, params, dropped]);
    }
  }
}

// ---- streamsOf, per mode -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// streamsOf is private, so it is recorded through the one shape that prints it: a lone system in the perChannel shape
// wires stream k to its own output bus, so the out node's `buses` and the wires' from-ports are the stream list.
const streamCases = [];
const SPLIT = { 1: "pinSplit", 3: "channelSplit" };
for (const type of m.KNOB_TYPES) {
  for (const mode of m.STREAM_MODES) {
    const labels = ["mix", "stereoModPins", "pinsPlusRef", "individualMono"];
    // Reach each mode the way a store does: the pins and channels splits by the routing (the engine's arm), the pin
    // reference layout by the stored export label. Only a NES reads either.
    const routing = type === "rp.mesen.nes" && (mode === 1 || mode === 3) ? SPLIT[mode] : "onePerInstance";
    const platform = type === "rp.sameboy.gb" ? "gb" : type === "rp.mesen.nes" ? "nes" : type === "rp.mesen.gba" ? "gba" : "sms";
    const system = {
      id: 1,
      platform,
      type,
      linkGroup: 0,
      exportMode: m.exportModeOf({ channelExportMode: labels[mode] }),
      resources: { rom: 1 },
      romName: "rom1",
      pipeline: [],
      coreConfig: { channelExportMode: labels[mode] },
    };
    const built = m.buildGraph({ systems: [system], routing, shape: { kind: "perChannel" } });
    const outNode = built.document.nodes.find((n) => n.id === "out");
    const ports = built.document.wires
      .filter((w) => w.to.startsWith("out.out."))
      .map((w) => ({ at: Number(w.to.slice("out.out.".length).split("-")[0]), port: w.from.slice("sys-1.".length) }))
      .sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at)
      .map((w) => w.port);
    streamCases.push([type, mode, outNode.settings.buses, ports]);
  }
}

// ---- emit -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
const lines = [];
const q = (s) => JSON.stringify(s);
lines.push(
  "// RECORDED, not computed: the answers the code at 96d748e5c gave over test/consoles/cases.ts, taken BEFORE the console",
  "// descriptors existed (test/consoles/registry.test.ts compares the descriptors to them). The recorder bundled the old",
  "// src/platform.ts (detectPlatform, romHasBattery) and src/graph/buildGraph.ts (systemKnobs, droppedKnobs, buildGraph,",
  "// exportModeOf) with esbuild and printed what they answered; nothing here is a hand-written expectation.",
  "//",
  "// Each record is data, so a diff says exactly which answer moved:",
  "//",
  "//   CLASSIFY          one platform (or \"unknown\") per CLASSIFY_CASES entry, in order",
  "//   BATTERY           one boolean per BATTERY_CASES entry, in order",
  "//   KNOBS             [type, field, value as JSON text, settings, construct, params, dropped]; \"-\" is absent",
  "//   STREAMS           [type, mode, the out node's buses, the ports the streams were wired from]",
  "",
  "/** The platform detectPlatform answered per CLASSIFY_CASES entry, in order. */",
  "export const RECORDED_CLASSIFY: readonly string[] = [",
);
for (let i = 0; i < classify.length; i += 8) {
  lines.push(`  ${classify.slice(i, i + 8).map(q).join(", ")},`);
}
lines.push("];", "", "/** The boolean romHasBattery answered per BATTERY_CASES entry, in order. */", "export const RECORDED_BATTERY: readonly boolean[] = [");
for (let i = 0; i < battery.length; i += 16) lines.push(`  ${battery.slice(i, i + 16).join(", ")},`);
lines.push("];", "", "/** One system-node field's answers, as buildGraph gave them. */", "export type RecordedKnob = readonly [", "  type: string,", "  field: string,", "  value: string,", "  settings: string,", "  construct: string,", "  params: string,", "  dropped: boolean,", "];", "", "/** Every (type, field, value) of cases.ts, and what systemKnobs and droppedKnobs answered it. */", "export const RECORDED_KNOBS: readonly RecordedKnob[] = [");
for (const r of knobs) lines.push(`  [${r.map((v) => (typeof v === "boolean" ? String(v) : q(v))).join(", ")}],`);
lines.push("];", "", "/** The streams a node type reports in a mode, as the perChannel shape wired them. */", "export type RecordedStreams = readonly [", "  type: string,", "  mode: number,", "  buses: readonly number[],", "  ports: readonly string[],", "];", "", "export const RECORDED_STREAMS: readonly RecordedStreams[] = [");
for (const [type, mode, buses, ports] of streamCases) {
  lines.push(`  [${q(type)}, ${mode}, [${buses.join(", ")}], [${ports.map(q).join(", ")}]],`);
}
lines.push("];", "");
writeFileSync(`${REPO}/packages/retroplug/test/consoles/recorded.ts`, lines.join("\n"));
console.log(`classify ${classify.length}, battery ${battery.length}, knobs ${knobs.length}, streams ${streamCases.length}`);
````

refusal has its fixture mode. The three mutations below are the fix pass's, and each is reversed by the command after
it.

**(d) `drivesRealCartOf` answered false for a platform with no registered cart**, so the GBA's mesen config opted it
out of a cart it does not have.

````patch
diff --git a/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph.ts b/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph.ts
--- a/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph.ts
+++ b/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph.ts
@@ -134,7 +134,7 @@
   // A platform with no cart has nothing to opt out of, so it drives one (a GBA's mesen config keeps the NES's field).
   if (platform !== undefined) {
     const cart = realCartOf(platform);
-    if (cart === undefined) return true;
+    if (cart === undefined) return false;  // RED
     const field = platformEntry(cart.platform)?.realCartOptOut;
     return field === undefined || config?.[field] !== false;
   }
````

**(f) The detector-answer guard.** A detector whose descriptor lists `gb` answers `n64`; without the guard the
registry accepts an answer its own descriptor does not list, and `systemNodeTypeFor` would throw later instead.

````patch

--- a/packages/retroplug/src/consoles.ts
````


(The `TinyUSB submodule has not been initialized` hint above it is `/opt/pico-sdk`'s own: the check needs no USB, which is why it uses that SDK.)

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f4apro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

Run: `bash -c 'R="(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 0-9][0-9] 20[0-9]{2}"; for e in build-device/rp-device-check.elf; do arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary $e /tmp/f4a-img.bin && LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -E "$R" /tmp/f4a-img.bin && LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/$R/Nov  4 2026/" /tmp/f4a-img.bin | sha256sum; done; rm -f /tmp/f4a-img.bin'`

### Task 2: render through the console registry, and the carts' render hooks

Design sections 4.1, 5.1, 6 (E1, E2, E4), 7.4 item 2 and 8's second stage. The render library stops naming a console or
a cart: it classifies its ROM through the registry, keeps the extension only for a file there is no content to read
(E1), takes the roles the registry gives that console (so the integration it asks for hooks is the one the built system
will have, E2), and reads the splits, their file names, the config patch and the mix's lanes from the console's
descriptor. Its pipeline is untouched: the boot, the settle, the lead-in, the sink, the part files, the end detection's
framing and the cancel points are the same code.

A cart contributes its render hooks to its tracker integration. Tracker owns the neutral contract (`TrackerRender`,
`RenderHost`, `RenderPlaySink`, `RenderFacts`, `PLAY_HOLD_MS`), and each cart's implementation sits beside the cart:
LSDj's song list, working-song seed and NR52 probe; risa's list, seed, SELECT+START gesture and sequencer probe; smsggdj's
list, verified work-RAM load, Pause press and two warnings. Their code moved out of `render.ts` verbatim, and the stage 2
review's fix pass is what put back the texts and gates the first cut had rewritten (the stage 3 report's table). The
task also carries the review's `RenderContext.registry` (design 9.5) and the CLI's `--list-songs` through the ROM's
integration.

- Modify (21 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 4 under `packages/retroplug/test/render/`; 3 under `packages/retroplug/src/render/`; 3 under `packages/retroplug/test-native/`; 2 under `packages/lsdj/ts/`; 1 under `packages/lsdj/`; 1 under `packages/retroplug/cli/` and the rest)

- [ ] **Step 1: Tracker's render contract**

`TrackerRender` is the member the shell asks for: `listSongs`, `seedSong?`, `loadSong?`, `pressPlay?`,
`playingProbe?`, and the members the prototype found it needed (`warnings?`, `songNameLength?`, `songList?`,
`seedRefusal?`), each with its doc saying what absent means. `RenderHost` is what a hook may do to the host
(`renderAudio`, `readCpu`, `readRam`, `writeRam`, `pressButton`), `RenderPlaySink` carries `renderChunk` because a
gesture must capture through the sink, and `RenderFacts` is the request data a probe or a warning is handed. The
integration gains the optional member, and the package publishes the module.

Create `packages/tracker/ts/trackerRender.ts`:

````ts
// The render hooks a cart contributes (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.1): what the shell's render
// library (packages/retroplug/src/render/render.ts) needs of a tracker to play and measure a saved song, as data and
// functions the cart owns. The library keeps its pipeline - the boot, the settle, the lead-in, the sink, the part files,
// the cancel points - and asks the integration for the parts that are the cart's: its songs, the SRAM a chosen one is
// seeded from (LSDj, risa), the live load a cart whose working song is work RAM needs (smsggdj), the button gesture that
// starts playback, the register or flag that says the song is still playing, and what a render of it should be warned it
// cannot do.
//
// The host and sink types are the shell's capabilities, narrowed to what these hooks use, so a hook is testable without a
// render: the library's RenderContext satisfies them structurally (render.ts builds the host over its backend and
// audio). Nothing here reads a file: the library passes the ROM and the battery bytes in, because resolving a sibling
// .sav is the host's (it owns the paths and the backend).
import type { SongInfo } from "./songCatalog";

/** The hold a play gesture's press needs to register, in whole milliseconds: the length of the chunk a gesture
 *  captures its head in. The render's pull length defaults to it too, so the lead-in a gesture returns is what its poll
 *  granularity counts per chunk; a cart reading its own value would skew the length cap. */
export const PLAY_HOLD_MS = 100;

/** What a render hook drives of the booted system: the cart's memory, its buttons and audio time. */
export interface RenderHost {
  /** The audio a hook discards while it works (a boot wait, a prep press): whole milliseconds, in the render's mix. */
  renderAudio(ms: number): void;
  /** A CPU register's value, or null when the core cannot be read: LSDj's NR52 sound-enable is the one such read. */
  readCpu(id: number, addr: number): number | null;
  /** The system's work RAM, or null when a snapshot is not available this block. */
  readRam(id: number): Uint8Array | null;
  /** Write into the system's work RAM; false when the range is refused (a wrong layout, a full command ring). */
  writeRam(id: number, offset: number, bytes: Uint8Array): boolean;
  pressButton(id: number, button: number, down: boolean): void;
}

/** The render's own stream: a chunk in the shape the request asked for (one mix buffer, or one per stream), rendered
 *  through the sink so what a play gesture captures is the recording's head rather than audio thrown away. */
export interface RenderPlaySink {
  /** Render `ms` and return the chunk: mix is one interleaved-stereo buffer, a split one buffer per stream. */
  renderChunk(ms: number): Float32Array[];
}

/** What a render of a cart is told about the request, for the warnings it is the cart's to raise. */
export interface RenderFacts {
  /** The ROM's bytes, as the render read them for its classification (null when the file could not be read). */
  readonly rom: Uint8Array | null;
  /** The battery the render will boot from, or null when there is none to read. */
  readonly sav: Uint8Array | null;
  /** The request carries a savestate: its work RAM is the working song, whatever the battery holds. */
  readonly state: boolean;
  /** A song was selected (--song / --song-index), so the cart's own load has it. */
  readonly song: boolean;
  /** The length the request pins, if it does. */
  readonly durationMs: number | undefined;
  /** The cap a render of no pinned length runs to (and the auto-detect's bound). */
  readonly maxDurationMs: number;
}

/** One cart's render hooks. Absent values mean the render does without: no seedSong and no loadSong refuses a song
 *  flag, no pressPlay keeps the console's default gesture (its descriptor's `render.defaultPlay`), and no playingProbe
 *  renders a fixed length. */
export interface TrackerRender {
  /** The saved songs of a battery, for --list-songs and for the not-found and empty-slot messages. */
  listSongs(sav: Uint8Array): readonly SongInfo[];
  /** The length the cart stores a song's name at, where a long enough --song is a prefix of the stored name (LSDj's 8:
   *  "--song MYSONGNAME" matches the project "MYSONGNA"). Absent: the whole name is compared. */
  songNameLength?: number;
  /** How this cart spells its songs where the neutral form will not do (LSDj's "(no named projects)", smsggdj's
   *  "0:METRO"), so a message the render prints keeps the cart's own words. Absent: `index: name` per song and
   *  "(no saved songs)". */
  songList?: {
    /** The one line a selection error prints (its "songs: ..." tail). */
    listing?(songs: readonly SongInfo[]): string;
    /** What --list-songs prints under its header when the battery holds none. */
    empty: string;
  };
  /** Before the boot: the SRAM the fresh system boots from, with project `index` promoted to the working song (LSDj,
   *  risa). Null when the slot holds no song this build can promote, which the render refuses (see seedRefusal). */
  seedSong?(sav: Uint8Array, index: number): Uint8Array | null;
  /** Why a seedSong that answered null cannot promote `index`, in the cart's words: the render throws this before the
   *  boot rather than play the battery's own working song. Absent: the render's own sentence, naming the cart and the
   *  battery. */
  seedRefusal?(index: number): string;
  /** After the boot settle: write song `index` into the booted core (smsggdj, whose working song is work RAM). Throws
   *  on every failure path, because rendering the blank boot song instead would make a silent WAV that looks like a
   *  successful render. */
  loadSong?(host: RenderHost, id: number, rom: Uint8Array, sav: Uint8Array, index: number): void;
  /** Press play and return the lead-in chunks the press rendered (they are the recording's head). Absent: the console's
   *  default gesture, or none. */
  pressPlay?(host: RenderHost, id: number, rom: Uint8Array, sink: RenderPlaySink): Float32Array[][];
  /** The "still playing?" probe for length auto-detect, or null when this build cannot tell (the render then runs for
   *  the fixed length). `facts` is the request, so the reason can quote the length the render falls back to, and `warn`
   *  says it when the reason is the cart's, not the request's. */
  playingProbe?(
    host: RenderHost,
    id: number,
    rom: Uint8Array,
    facts: RenderFacts,
    warn: (msg: string) => void,
  ): (() => boolean) | null;
  /** What a render of this cart should be told it cannot do, through `warn`: a boot state that will be silent without
   *  a song. Called once, after the settle and before the song loads. */
  warnings?(facts: RenderFacts, warn: (msg: string) => void): void;
}
````

- [ ] **Step 2: LSDj's hooks**

`lsdjRender.ts` is its song list, its working-song seed (the old `resolveLsdjSongSeed` minus the shell's selection)
and the NR52 probe (the old `buildPlayingProbe`'s Game Boy arm), attached on `lsdjIntegration`. `lsdjSongCatalog.ts`'s
`workingName` gains the `jk`-magic guard, so a battery that is not an LSDj image names no song (the fix pass restored
it; the old render got it from `isLsdjSav`). The manifest publishes the module.

Create `packages/lsdj/ts/lsdjRender.ts`:

````ts
// What rendering an LSDj song needs of the cart (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.1): its saved songs,
// how it spells them, the SRAM a chosen one is seeded from, and the register that says the song is still playing. The
// shell's render library (packages/retroplug/src/render/render.ts) keeps its pipeline and asks the integration for these.
//
// The end-of-song probe is the hardware's, not the codec's: LSDj's HFF command stops the song by powering the APU off, a
// 0 write to NR52 ($FF26), the sound-master-enable register (bit 7). Polling it each render chunk and stopping at the
// high-to-low edge is the technique lsdpack uses, and it is version-independent, so it holds for any LSDj build. It is
// chosen for a ROM whose roles name this cart (the integration's markerRole), not for a battery that decodes: a cart
// booted from a blank battery answers it too.
import type { SongInfo } from "@retroplug/tracker/songCatalog";
import type { TrackerRender } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerRender";
import { decodeSav, encodeSav, kSavSize } from "./codec/sav";

const NR52_ADDR = 0xff26;
const NR52_ON = 0x80; // bit 7 = all-sound-on

/** The populated project slots as one line ("0: HAPPYBD, 3: DEMO"), as a selection error prints them: LSDj's projects
 *  are NAMED slots, and a save holding none still has a working song worth saying so about. */
const lsdjListing = (songs: readonly SongInfo[]): string =>
  songs.length ? songs.map((s) => `${s.index}: ${s.name || "(unnamed)"}`).join(", ") : "(no named projects)";

/** The populated project slots, DECODED: a render has always read a battery through the codec, so a malformed 128 KiB
 *  image is refused in the codec's own words (where the header-only catalogue scan would answer "no songs") and an
 *  early 32 KiB image, which has no archive, lists none. */
function lsdjRenderSongs(sav: Uint8Array): SongInfo[] {
  const out: SongInfo[] = [];
  decodeSav(sav).projects.forEach((project, index) => {
    if (project) out.push({ index, name: project.name });
  });
  return out;
}

export const LSDJ_RENDER: TrackerRender = {
  listSongs: lsdjRenderSongs,
  songNameLength: 8, // LSDj stores a project name in 8 characters, and uppercases it
  songList: { listing: lsdjListing, empty: "(no named projects \u2014 only the working song)" },

  // LSDj plays its WORKING song at boot, whatever slot you would rather hear, so a chosen project is promoted into it
  // in the SRAM the fresh system boots from. The unmodelled regions come from the original battery when it is a full
  // image (a narrower one is authored fresh), which is what the codec's optional tail is for.
  seedSong: (sav, index) => {
    const decoded = decodeSav(sav);
    const project = decoded.projects[index];
    if (!project) return null;
    decoded.workingSong = project.song; // working song and project songs share the decoded Song shape
    decoded.activeProjectIndex = index;
    return encodeSav(decoded, sav.length >= kSavSize ? sav : undefined);
  },

  playingProbe: (host, id) => () => ((host.readCpu(id, NR52_ADDR) ?? 0) & NR52_ON) !== 0,
};
````

````ts
// What rendering a risa song needs of the cart (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.1): its saved songs,
// how it spells them, the battery a chosen one is seeded from, the button gesture that starts playback, and the
// sequencer flag that says the song is still playing. The shell's render library keeps its pipeline and asks the
// integration for these.
//
// risa begins song playback on SELECT+START (a plain START first nudges it off an empty phrase context, the sequence
// the runtime-reader test proved reliable). The two prep renders are pre-song and discarded; the SELECT+START render,
// where the song begins, is captured through the sink and returned as the recording's lead-in, so the opening frames
// are not lost.
// The end of the song is SEQ_MODE_STOPPED, read through the pure runtime reader from a work-RAM snapshot.
import type { SongInfo } from "@retroplug/tracker/songCatalog";
import { PLAY_HOLD_MS, type TrackerRender } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerRender";
import { listSongs as risaListSongs } from "./risaSav";
import { loadSongToWorkingInSav } from "./risaSongOps";
import { decodeRisaState, identifyRisaVersion, resolveRisaLayout, supportedRisaVersions } from "./runtime";

const NES_START = 7; // NesButton::Start
const NES_SELECT = 6; // NesButton::Select

/** The catalog's saved slots as one line, as a selection error prints them. A catalog read from a battery that holds no
 *  song entries is still a catalog. */
const risaListing = (songs: readonly SongInfo[]): string =>
  songs.length ? songs.map((s) => `${s.index}: ${s.name || "(unnamed)"}`).join(", ") : "(no saved songs)";

export const RISA_RENDER: TrackerRender = {
  listSongs: (sav) => risaListSongs(sav),
  songList: { listing: risaListing, empty: "(no saved songs in the catalog)" },

  // Promote the catalog song into the working banks (0-3), keeping the catalog (banks 4-7) intact. A current-layout
  // catalog is required: the firmware migrates legacy images on boot, so a live-read battery is always current. Null
  // when the slot names no song or the image is not one this build can promote.
  seedSong: (sav, index) => loadSongToWorkingInSav(sav, index),
  // The list offers a legacy-layout catalog's slots too, and those are exactly the ones this build cannot promote: the
  // render says so and refuses, rather than booting the battery's own working song and naming the file after another.
  seedRefusal: (index) => `render: could not load risa song ${index} (needs a current-layout catalog)`,

  pressPlay: (host, id, _rom, sink) => {
    host.pressButton(id, NES_START, true);
    sink.renderChunk(PLAY_HOLD_MS); // prep: nudge off an empty phrase context (pre-song, discarded)
    host.pressButton(id, NES_START, false);
    sink.renderChunk(PLAY_HOLD_MS); // prep (discarded)
    host.pressButton(id, NES_SELECT, true);
    host.pressButton(id, NES_START, true);
    const head = sink.renderChunk(PLAY_HOLD_MS); // the song starts here: capture it as the lead-in
    host.pressButton(id, NES_START, false);
    host.pressButton(id, NES_SELECT, false);
    return [head];
  },

  playingProbe: (host, id, rom, facts, warn) => {
    const layout = resolveRisaLayout(identifyRisaVersion(rom));
    if (!layout) {
      // A risa cart whose version has no internal-RAM layout: the reader cannot find seq_mode, so the render falls
      // back to a fixed length, and says why - or it just looks like the song never stops (it cannot be seen to stop).
      // Only these versions expose the addresses song-length auto-detect needs.
      warn(
        `render: risa ${identifyRisaVersion(rom) ?? "(unrecognized version)"} has no runtime layout \u2014 song-length ` +
          `auto-detect unavailable (supported: ${supportedRisaVersions().join(", ")}); ` +
          `rendering a fixed ${facts.durationMs ?? facts.maxDurationMs}ms`,
      );
      return null;
    }
    // A work-RAM read is the per-block snapshot (safe while the core plays). If it is momentarily unavailable, report
    // "playing" so a read gap never trims the song early; the render's maxDurationMs cap still bounds it.
    return () => {
      const ram = host.readRam(id);
      return ram ? decodeRisaState(ram, layout).playing : true;
    };
  },
};
````

````diff
+/** Classify a render's ROM: its content first, and its extension only for a file there is no content to read from (edge

+function classifyForRender(reader: PrefixReader, romPath: string): Platform | "unknown" {
+  let unreadable = false;

+    {
+      readFilePrefix: (path: string, length: number) => {

-// The load has to land AFTER the cart's boot-time `song_new`, which blanks the song block on the way up

-// 2500 ms and later survive. A bigger fixed number would be guessing - the margin is ~500 ms on NTSC and
-// PAL runs ~17% slower - and simply retrying until the block reads back is NOT enough either: measured,
-// a write at 1750 ms verifies perfectly (the whole 6,912-byte block byte-identical) and is then wiped
-// 400 ms later, so the loop stops on a match that does not last.
-//

-// waves, and work RAM powers on all zeros (MesenSmsSystem pins RamPowerOnState = AllZeros), so a
````

- [ ] **Step 8: The two new render suites**

`render-classify.test.ts` pins edges E1 and E2: a `.bin` Game Boy ROM renders its four channel stems; an LSDj ROM with
no battery auto-detects to an HFF stop and renders to the full cap, the old rule's opposite; a non-LSDj Game Boy
beside an LSDj battery runs the full cap and is named after its own ROM, and a real LSDj cart beside its own battery
keeps the working-song name. `render-hooks.test.ts` drives each integration's hooks over a fake `RenderHost` and a
fake sink: LSDj's list/seed/NR52 probe, risa's list/seed/three-pull gesture/no-layout warning/seed refusal, smsggdj's
verified work-RAM load, its Pause press (stopped presses, an already-playing render is not pressed), its
unversioned-ROM refusal and both warnings' exact conditions, and each cart's listing spelling.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/render/render-classify.test.ts`:

````ts
// Two edges the design changes deliberately (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 6): a render classifies its
// ROM by its CONTENT, and the end-of-song detection follows the ROM's cart rather than the battery beside it. Both are
// proved here in-process, over mocks: the audio is nothing, the decisions are everything.
//
// E1: `platformOf` read the extension alone, so a Game Boy ROM named `.bin` was an unknown console and `--split
// channels` was refused with "got other". The registry's content rule makes it a Game Boy, so the split is accepted and
// the stems take the descriptor's names.
//
// E2: the LSDj probe was chosen when the SIBLING BATTERY was a 128 KiB LSDj image, so an LSDj ROM with no battery
// rendered a fixed length and a non-LSDj Game Boy beside one was polled. The probe now follows the ROM's roles, and the
// output's default name follows the same cart.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { buildAppRegistry } from "../../src/appHost";
import {
  renderSongs,
  runRenderJob,
  validateRenderOpts,
  type RenderAudioDriver,
  type RenderContext,
  type RenderOpts,
} from "../../src/render";
import { gbRom, lsdjRom, risaRom } from "../systems/fixtures";
import { savBytes as lsdjSav } from "@retroplug/lsdj/testFixtures";
import { savBytes as risaSav } from "@retroplug/risa/testFixtures";

const SR = 44100;
const NR52 = 0x80;

/** Silence in every shape a render asks for. `streams` is the split's stream count, as the descriptor names it. */
function silentAudio(streams = 1): RenderAudioDriver {
  const frames = (ms: number): Float32Array => new Float32Array(Math.round((ms * SR) / 1000) * 2);
  return {
    renderAudio: (ms) => frames(ms),
    renderAudioPerChannel: (_id, ms) => Array.from({ length: streams }, () => frames(ms)),
    sampleRate: () => SR,
    setSampleRate: () => true,
    setBpm: () => true,
    setTransport: () => true,
    pressButton: () => true,
  };
}

/** A backend whose NR52 answers what `playing()` says: an LSDj cart whose APU the poll sees switch off after a while. */
class Nr52Backend extends MockBackend {
  private reads = 0;
  constructor(
    root: string,
    private readonly onReads: number,
  ) {
    super(root);
  }
  override readCpu(id: number, addr: number): number | null {
    if (addr !== 0xff26 || !super.readCpu(id, addr)) return 0;
    this.reads++;
    return this.reads <= this.onReads ? NR52 : 0;
  }
}

/** A context over `backend` with the mock's project store, which needs only the four calls buildSystem makes. */
function ctxOf(backend: MockBackend, audio: RenderAudioDriver): RenderContext {
  return {
    backend,
    audio,
    registry: buildAppRegistry(),
    project: {
      systems: { addSystem: () => 1, view: () => [{ id: 1 }], adopt: () => {}, loadState: () => 1 },
    } as unknown as RenderContext["project"],
  };
}

const opts = (over: Partial<RenderOpts> & { rom: string }): RenderOpts => ({
  out: "/out/song.wav",
  maxDurationMs: 5000,
  split: "mix",
  transport: false,
  start: true,
  listSongs: false,
  ...over,
});

test("E1: a Game Boy ROM under a .bin extension renders its channels, because the content decides", () => {
  const backend = new MockBackend("/config");
  backend.seed("/roms/cart.bin", gbRom());
  const ctx = ctxOf(backend, silentAudio(4));
  const result = runRenderJob(ctx, opts({ rom: "/roms/cart.bin", split: "channels", durationMs: 50 }), {
    log: () => {},
    warn: () => {},
  });
  // The descriptor's channel split: one file per stream, under its own name.
  expect(result.outputs.map((p) => p.slice(p.lastIndexOf("_"), -".wav".length))).toEqual([
    "_pulse1",
    "_pulse2",
    "_wave",
    "_noise",
  ]);
  for (const path of result.outputs) expect(backend.fileExists(path)).toBe(true);
});

test("E2: an LSDj ROM with no battery auto-detects its length, because the ROM names the cart", () => {
  // No sav is seeded at all: the old rule needed a 128 KiB LSDj image beside the ROM to choose the probe.
  const backend = new Nr52Backend("/config", 3);
  backend.seed("/roms/lsdj.gb", lsdjRom());
  const result = runRenderJob(ctxOf(backend, silentAudio()), opts({ rom: "/roms/lsdj.gb" }), {
    log: () => {},
    warn: () => {},
  });
  // The auto-detect path ran: it reports a length, and the APU going off ended it well under the cap.
  expect(result.lengthMs !== undefined).toBe(true);
  expect(result.hff).toBe(true);
  expect(result.lengthMs! < 5000).toBe(true);
});

test("E2: a Game Boy ROM that is not LSDj runs the full cap, even beside an LSDj battery", () => {
  // The backend answers NR52 on, then off: the poll the OLD rule chose here (a 128 KiB LSDj image beside the ROM) would
  // have ended this render a few hundred ms in. No duration is pinned, so a render with no probe runs to maxDurationMs.
  const backend = new Nr52Backend("/config", 3);
  backend.seed("/roms/song.gb", gbRom()); // a Game Boy cart whose title is not LSDj's
  backend.seed("/roms/song.sav", lsdjSav("lsdj499")); // ... next to one, which the old rule polled
  const progress: number[] = [];
  const result = runRenderJob(ctxOf(backend, silentAudio()), opts({ rom: "/roms/song.gb", out: undefined }), {
    log: () => {},
    warn: () => {},
    onRendered: (ms) => progress.push(ms),
  });
  // A fixed render of the whole cap: no detected length, no HFF, and the last progress report is the cap itself.
  expect(result.lengthMs).toBe(undefined);
  expect(result.hff).toBe(undefined);
  expect(progress[progress.length - 1]).toBe(5000);
  // Its name is the ROM's, because the battery's song is no cart of this ROM's (the naming follows the same rule as the
  // probe).
  expect(result.outputs).toEqual(["/roms/song.wav"]);
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/render/render-hooks.test.ts`:

````ts
// Each cart's render hooks (packages/tracker/ts/trackerRender.ts) over a fake RenderHost: what the shell's render
// library asks of a cart, without a core, an engine or a WAV. The library itself is held to its own suites
// (test/render/*, test-native/render-*); what is pinned here is that a hook answers what the pipeline needs, and that
// each cart's oddity is the cart's: LSDj promotes a slot into the SRAM it boots from, risa presses SELECT+START and
// reads its sequencer flag, smsggdj writes into work RAM after the boot and knows the two things a render of it cannot
// do.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import type { RenderFacts, RenderHost, RenderPlaySink } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerRender";
import { lsdjIntegration } from "@retroplug/lsdj/lsdjIntegration";
import { lsdjSongCatalog } from "@retroplug/lsdj/lsdjSongCatalog";
import { savBytes as lsdjSav } from "@retroplug/lsdj/testFixtures";
import { risaIntegration } from "@retroplug/risa/risaIntegration";
import { risaSongCatalog } from "@retroplug/risa/risaSongCatalog";
import { savBytes as risaSav } from "@retroplug/risa/testFixtures";
import { loadSongToWorkingInSav } from "@retroplug/risa/risaSongOps";
import { smsggdjIntegration } from "@retroplug/smsggdj/smsggdjIntegration";
import { SMDJ4_BLOCK_LEN, buildSav, readSongBlock } from "@retroplug/smsggdj/codec/sav";
import { resolveSmsggdjLayout } from "@retroplug/smsggdj/runtime/layout";

const LSDJ = lsdjIntegration.render!;
const RISA = risaIntegration.render!;
const SMSGGDJ = smsggdjIntegration.render!;

/** A host over one work-RAM buffer, so a write is what the next read sees: the pitch a cart's load loop verifies
 *  against. Buttons and audio time are recorded, and the CPU answers what a case sets. */
function fakeHost(over: Partial<RenderHost> & { ram?: Uint8Array } = {}): {
  host: RenderHost;
  ram: Uint8Array;
  buttons: [number, boolean][];
  audioMs: number[];
} {
  const ram = over.ram ?? new Uint8Array(0x2000);
  const buttons: [number, boolean][] = [];
  const audioMs: number[] = [];
  const host: RenderHost = {
    renderAudio: (ms) => audioMs.push(ms),
    readCpu: () => null,
    readRam: () => ram,
    writeRam: (_id, offset, bytes) => {
      if (offset < 0 || offset + bytes.length > ram.length) return false;
      ram.set(bytes, offset);
      return true;
    },
    pressButton: (_id, button, down) => buttons.push([button, down]),
    ...over,
  };
  return { host, ram, buttons, audioMs };
}

/** A sink that answers one silent chunk per pull and counts the pulls: what a play gesture captures through. */
function fakeSink(): { sink: RenderPlaySink; pulls: number[] } {
  const pulls: number[] = [];
  return {
    sink: {
      renderChunk: (ms) => {
        pulls.push(ms);
        return [new Float32Array(Math.round((ms * 44100) / 1000) * 2)];
      },
    },
    pulls,
  };
}

// ---- LSDj ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** The request facts a hook is handed: no ROM or battery read, nothing pinned, no song, no savestate, the 10-minute
 *  cap. */
const facts = (over: Partial<RenderFacts> = {}): RenderFacts => ({
  rom: null,
  sav: null,
  state: false,
  song: false,
  durationMs: undefined,
  maxDurationMs: 600000,
  ...over,
});

test("LSDj lists the battery's songs and seeds a chosen one as the working song", () => {
  const sav = lsdjSav("lsdj499");
  const songs = LSDJ.listSongs(sav);
  expect(songs.length > 0).toBe(true);
  expect(songs.map((s) => ({ index: s.index, name: s.name }))).toEqual(lsdjSongCatalog.list(sav));
  const pick = songs[0];
  const seed = LSDJ.seedSong!(sav, pick.index);
  expect(seed !== null).toBe(true);
  // The seed is the image a fresh system boots from, and the slot the caller picked is what it plays.
  expect(lsdjSongCatalog.workingName(seed!)).toBe(pick.name);
  expect(lsdjSongCatalog.list(seed!)).toEqual(songs.map((s) => ({ index: s.index, name: s.name })));
  // A slot the battery does not hold seeds nothing, rather than a silent cart.
  expect(songs.some((s) => s.index === 31)).toBe(false);
  expect(LSDJ.seedSong!(sav, 31)).toBe(null);
});

test("LSDj's end-of-song probe is NR52's sound-enable bit", () => {
  const rom = new Uint8Array(0x150); // the probe is the ROM's cart's, so what it is handed is the ROM
  const on = fakeHost({ readCpu: () => 0x80 });
  const off = fakeHost({ readCpu: () => 0x00 });
  const unreadable = fakeHost({ readCpu: () => null });
  expect(LSDJ.playingProbe!(on.host, 1, rom, facts(), () => {})!()).toBe(true);
  expect(LSDJ.playingProbe!(off.host, 1, rom, facts(), () => {})!()).toBe(false);
  // A core whose register cannot be read says nothing, which reads as stopped: the cap bounds the render.
  expect(LSDJ.playingProbe!(unreadable.host, 1, rom, facts(), () => {})!()).toBe(false);
});

// ---- risa ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

test("risa lists and seeds its catalog, and begins a song on SELECT+START", () => {
  const sav = risaSav("v2_blumarbl");
  const songs = RISA.listSongs(sav);
  expect(songs.length > 0).toBe(true);
  expect(songs.map((s) => ({ index: s.index, name: s.name }))).toEqual(risaSongCatalog.list(sav));
  const seed = RISA.seedSong!(sav, songs[0].index);
  expect(seed).toEqual(loadSongToWorkingInSav(sav, songs[0].index));
  // A slot the catalog does not hold seeds nothing.
  expect(RISA.seedSong!(sav, 31)).toBe(null);
  // ... and says why, in its own words: a legacy-layout catalog lists slots this build cannot promote.
  expect(RISA.seedRefusal!(31)).toBe("render: could not load risa song 31 (needs a current-layout catalog)");

  // The gesture: two discarded prep chunks, then the SELECT+START chunk captured as the lead-in.
  const { host, buttons } = fakeHost();
  const { sink, pulls } = fakeSink();
  const leadIn = RISA.pressPlay!(host, 1, new Uint8Array(0), sink);
  expect(pulls.length).toBe(3);
  expect(leadIn.length).toBe(1);
  expect(leadIn[0][0].length / 2).toBe(pulls[2] * 44.1); // interleaved stereo: frames are halves
  // Start down, Start up (the nudge), then SELECT and START together, then both released.
  expect(buttons).toEqual([
    [7, true],
    [7, false],
    [6, true],
    [7, true],
    [7, false],
    [6, false],
  ]);
});

test("risa's probe reads its sequencer flag, and says why it cannot when the build has no layout", () => {
  const warnings: string[] = [];
  const rom = new Uint8Array(0x4000);
  rom.set([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a], 0); // iNES
  expect(RISA.playingProbe!(fakeHost().host, 1, rom, facts(), (m) => warnings.push(m))).toBe(null);
  expect(warnings.length).toBe(1);
  expect(warnings[0].includes("no runtime layout")).toBe(true);
  // It names the length the render falls back to, so the log says what the WAV will be.
  expect(warnings[0].includes("rendering a fixed 600000ms")).toBe(true);
});

// ---- smsggdj ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** A ROM that identifies as an smsggdj build with a committed layout. */
function smsggdjRom(): Uint8Array {
  const rom = new Uint8Array(0x8000);
  const marker = "SMSGGDJ";
  for (let i = 0; i < marker.length; i++) rom[0x100 + i] = marker.charCodeAt(i);
  const version = "V0.45";
  for (let i = 0; i < version.length; i++) rom[0x180 + i] = version.charCodeAt(i);
  return rom;
}

/** A one-song battery this build can decode: the block's checksum is the image's, as buildSav writes it. */
function smsggdjSav(): Uint8Array {
  const block = new Uint8Array(SMDJ4_BLOCK_LEN);
  for (let i = 0; i < block.length; i += 16) block.set([0x11, 0xff, 0x00, 0x00], i);
  return buildSav([{ block, name: "TEST" }], 32 * 1024)!;
}

test("smsggdj loads a song into work RAM after the boot, and verifies it held", () => {
  const rom = smsggdjRom();
  const sav = smsggdjSav();
  const layout = resolveSmsggdjLayout("0.45")!;
  const { host, ram, audioMs } = fakeHost();
  SMSGGDJ.loadSong!(host, 1, rom, sav, 0);
  // The block the battery holds is what the cart's work RAM holds now, whole.
  const block = readSongBlock(sav, 0)!;
  expect(Array.from(ram.subarray(layout.song, layout.song + block.length))).toEqual(Array.from(block));
  // The load waited for the boot (up to 6 s of audio), then let the queued writes land: both are audio time.
  expect(audioMs.length > 0).toBe(true);
  // A slot with no song is a refusal, not a silent cart.
  expect(() => SMSGGDJ.loadSong!(host, 1, rom, sav, 9)).toThrow("could not load smsggdj song 9");
});

test("smsggdj presses Pause only on a cart it recognises and while the transport is stopped", () => {
  const rom = smsggdjRom();
  const layout = resolveSmsggdjLayout("0.45")!;
  const stopped = fakeHost();
  const { sink, pulls } = fakeSink();
  const leadIn = SMSGGDJ.pressPlay!(stopped.host, 1, rom, sink);
  expect(leadIn.length).toBe(1);
  expect(pulls).toEqual([100]);
  expect(stopped.buttons).toEqual([[7, true], [7, false]]);

  // A ROM carrying the build marker but no version string is not a build whose transport this knows: pressing Pause on
  // an ordinary Master System game pauses it.
  const unversioned = rom.slice();
  unversioned.fill(0, 0x180, 0x1a0);
  const other = fakeHost();
  expect(SMSGGDJ.pressPlay!(other.host, 1, unversioned, fakeSink().sink).length).toBe(0);
  expect(other.buttons).toEqual([]);

  // Already running (a render restored from a savestate, which carries work RAM): pressing would STOP it.
  const running = fakeHost();
  running.ram[layout.playState] = 1;
  const quiet = fakeSink();
  expect(SMSGGDJ.pressPlay!(running.host, 1, rom, quiet.sink).length).toBe(0);
  expect(running.buttons).toEqual([]);
  expect(quiet.pulls).toEqual([]);
});

test("smsggdj says what a render of it cannot do: no end marker, and a blank boot without a song", () => {
  const rom = smsggdjRom();
  const smsFacts = (over: Partial<RenderFacts> = {}): RenderFacts => facts({ rom, sav: smsggdjSav(), ...over });

  // Where a probe that can find the end would have answered: no pinned length, so the cap is what the WAV gets.
  const probeSays = (f: RenderFacts): string[] => {
    const out: string[] = [];
    SMSGGDJ.playingProbe!(fakeHost().host, 1, rom, f, (m) => out.push(m));
    return out;
  };
  const noEnd = probeSays(smsFacts());
  expect(noEnd.length).toBe(1);
  expect(noEnd[0].includes("loop forever")).toBe(true);
  expect(noEnd[0].includes("600000ms")).toBe(true);
  // A pinned duration answers it, and a ROM that is not this cart is left alone.
  expect(probeSays(smsFacts({ durationMs: 5000 }))).toEqual([]);
  expect(probeSays(facts({ rom: new Uint8Array(0x100) }))).toEqual([]);

  // The boot state: a blank boot is silence unless a song was selected or a savestate carries the working song.
  const said = (f: RenderFacts): string[] => {
    const out: string[] = [];
    SMSGGDJ.warnings!(f, (m) => out.push(m));
    return out;
  };
  const blank = said(smsFacts());
  expect(blank.length).toBe(1);
  expect(blank[0].includes("BLANK song")).toBe(true);
  expect(blank[0].includes("0:TEST")).toBe(true);
  expect(said(smsFacts({ song: true }))).toEqual([]);
  expect(said(smsFacts({ state: true }))).toEqual([]);
  expect(said(facts({ rom: new Uint8Array(0x100) }))).toEqual([]);
});

test("each cart's song listing keeps its own spelling", () => {
  // The selection errors and --list-songs print the cart's own line, which is why these are data on the hooks rather
  // than one neutral form: LSDj says "(no named projects)", smsggdj writes "0:METRO" with no space after the colon.
  expect(LSDJ.songList!.listing!([])).toBe("(no named projects)");
  expect(LSDJ.songList!.empty).toBe("(no named projects \u2014 only the working song)"); // the CLI's line, byte for byte
  const lsdj = LSDJ.listSongs(lsdjSav("lsdj499"));
  expect(LSDJ.songList!.listing!(lsdj)).toBe(lsdj.map((s) => `${s.index}: ${s.name}`).join(", "));
  expect(RISA.songList!.listing!([])).toBe("(no saved songs)");
  expect(RISA.songList!.empty).toBe("(no saved songs in the catalog)");
  expect(SMSGGDJ.songList!.listing!([{ index: 0, name: "METRO" }])).toBe("0:METRO");
  expect(SMSGGDJ.songList!.listing!([])).toBe("(none)");
  expect(SMSGGDJ.songList!.empty).toBe("(no saved songs in the catalog)");
});
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f4apro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
feat(f4a): render through the console registry and the carts' render hooks

The render library no longer names a console or a cart (design sections 4.1, 5.1, 6, 7.4 item 2, 8 stage 2). It
classifies its ROM through the console registry, keeping the extension only for a file there is no content to read
(edge E1); the roles it builds from are the registry's defaults for that console, so the tracker integration it asks
for hooks is the one the built system would have (edge E2); and the console's descriptor supplies the splits, their
file names, the config patch a split applies to the core-config role and the mix's lanes. Its own pipeline is
untouched: the boot, the settle, the lead-in, the sink, the part files, the end detection's framing and the cancel
points are the same code, and render.ts imports no cart package.

A cart contributes its render hooks to its tracker integration (`TrackerRender` in @retroplug/tracker, whose
RenderHost / RenderPlaySink are the neutral capabilities a hook uses, so a hook is testable without a host). LSDj
contributes its song list, its working-song seed and the NR52 probe; risa its list, its seed, the SELECT+START gesture
with its prep presses and its sequencer probe with the unsupported-version warning; smsggdj its list, the verified
work-RAM song load, the Pause press with its already-playing check and the two warnings a render of it owes (a blank
boot without a song, a length with no end marker). Their code moved out of render.ts verbatim.

The CLI's --list-songs goes through the ROM's integration, and the error text naming carts is built from the
registered integrations in product order. RenderContext gains the registry both constructors already hold.

New tests: test/render/render-hooks.test.ts drives each integration's hooks over a fake RenderHost, and
test/render/render-classify.test.ts pins edges E1 (a .bin Game Boy ROM renders its channels) and E2 (an LSDj ROM with
no battery auto-detects; a non-LSDj Game Boy beside an LSDj battery renders a fixed length and is named after its ROM).
EOF
````

---

### Task 3: the tracker playback and song-import hooks, and the shell's pollers through them

Design sections 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 6 (E3, E4's drop reason), 7.4 item 3 and 8's third stage. The control plane stops naming
a cart to follow one. Tracker owns the neutral contracts in a module per member beside `trackerRender` -
`TrackerPlayback` with `ControllerAnchor`, `PlaybackReader` and the row-tick table, `TrackerSongImport` with the host and
target shapes an import needs, and `SramSignature` - and each cart contributes its implementation.

The shell's four readers go through the integration: `projectStore`'s poll asks `resolveTracker(roles)?.playback` for
the sync mode, the song's change signature, the timing table and the anchor; `sramAutoSave` asks each integration for a
signature in product order before `hashBytes`; `fileDrop` recognises a song file by the target's tracker (and by the
product's union otherwise) and refuses with the new reason; `graph/controller.ts` reads the serial-out capture from the
protocol table the cart's manifest declares. The last of those is the task's one departure from the design's wording,
and its reason is F1's bundle rule: `playback.captureFor` would make the planner resolve a cart's integration.

A system whose integration has no `playback` reads no sync, no signature, no table and no reader, which is edge E3 -
wider than the design said, because the gate is the ROM's roles, and the controller accepted it. Two test fixtures
follow it, and the stage 3 report records both as failures of the new rule first.

**Files:**

- Create (9): `packages/lsdj/ts/lsdjPlayback.ts`, `packages/lsdj/ts/lsdjSongImport.ts`, `packages/lsdj/ts/lsdjSramSignature.ts`, `packages/lsdj/ts/test/sramSignature.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/songImportHost.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/tracker/playback-absent.test.ts`, `packages/tracker/ts/trackerPlayback.ts`, `packages/tracker/ts/trackerSongImport.ts`, `packages/tracker/ts/trackerSramSignature.ts`
- Modify (23 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 3 under `packages/retroplug/src/`; 2 under `packages/lsdj/ts/playback/`; 2 under `packages/retroplug/src/graph/`; 2 under `packages/retroplug/test/packages/`; 2 under `packages/retroplug/test/systems/`; 1 under `packages/lsdj/` and the rest)
- Delete (1): `packages/retroplug/src/lsdjSongImport.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Tracker's three contracts**

`trackerPlayback.ts` is `TrackerPlayback` (`syncMode`, `songSignature`, `rowTicks`, `anchor`), `PlaybackAnchor`
(`reader(header)`, `playing(state)`, `rows(state)`), `PlaybackReader` (`read(wram): unknown`) and the neutral types
tracker owns (`ControllerAnchor`, `RowTicksTable`, documented `[channel][row]`); a reader's state is the cart's, so it
is `unknown` here and read back by the same cart's `playing`/`rows`. `trackerSongImport.ts` is `TrackerSongImport`
