````ts
// The playback half of a tracker integration (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.2): what the control
// plane polls of a cart to follow the song it is playing, and what it reads of a cart's memory to know where the
// playhead is. A cart contributes it to its integration, beside its song catalog and its render hooks, and the shell
// asks the integration its roles name - so the controller's poll and the graph's placement name no cart and import
// none.
//
// The state a PlaybackReader answers with is the cart's own: the shell passes it back to the same integration's
// anchor.playing / anchor.rows, which read it, so the type stays unknown here.
//
// A system whose integration has no playback reads "no sync mode, no signature, no timing table, no reader", and the
// gate is the ROM's ROLES, not its battery: a ROM whose title names no tracker reads none of the four even beside a
// battery a tracker could read, which is the widening section 6's E3 records (test/tracker/playback-absent.test.ts
// pins what LSDj's own functions answer for a battery that is not its own, which is the same answer but for a
// different reason).

/** What the control plane polls of a cart, and how it reads one's position. */
export interface TrackerPlayback {
  /** The cart's own SYNC setting as its battery spells it ("MidiMap", "Lsdj", ...), or null when the image is not
   *  this cart's (a row launch into a cart that is not in MI.MAP is ignored without complaint, and the setting is the
   *  only sign). Polled. */
  syncMode(sram: Uint8Array | null): string | null;
  /** A cheap change signature over the parts of the battery the song's structure lives in, 0 for anything unreadable:
   *  an edit made inside the tracker is invisible to everything else, and this is what notices it. */
  songSignature(sram: Uint8Array | null): number;
  /** The per-song-row clock table the controller's predictor runs on, or null when the battery holds no song this
   *  build can read. Derived here because decoding a battery is a control-plane job: the audio thread has neither the
   *  bytes nor any business running a codec. */
  rowTicks(sram: Uint8Array | null): RowTicksTable | null;
  /** Reading a running cart: the reader itself, and what its state means. */
  readonly anchor: PlaybackAnchor;
}

/** The row-timing table the predictor runs on: `[channel][row]`, the clock ticks that row holds on that channel, or
 *  null for a channel with no chain there. */
export type RowTicksTable = (number | null)[][];

/** Decodes a cart's work RAM into the state its own `anchor.playing` / `anchor.rows` read. Built once per ROM from
 *  the header, not once per poll: the layout it decodes is the build's, which does not change while the system runs. */
export interface PlaybackReader {
  read(wram: Uint8Array): unknown;
}

/** Where a cart's playhead is, read from its live state. */
export interface PlaybackAnchor {
  /** The reader for a ROM header prefix (the cart's build, which decides the memory layout), or null for a version
   *  this build has no layout for. */
  reader(header: Uint8Array): PlaybackReader | null;
  /** Whether anything is playing at all: the signal a start edge is detected on. Reads what `reader` returned. */
  playing(state: unknown): boolean;
  /** Each channel's own song row, or null where it is not playing. Per channel rather than one row for the song,
   *  because channels genuinely diverge as their chains end. */
  rows(state: unknown): (number | null)[];
}

/** Where the cart was seen starting playback on its OWN, as the controller node is told: a start is a rare, discrete
 *  event that fits the "push it as role config" path, where streaming a position every block would not. */
export interface ControllerAnchor {
  rows: (number | null)[];
  /** Bumped once per anchoring event. The node re-anchors when this CHANGES, so the same anchor riding along on later
   *  structure pushes is applied once rather than re-applied forever. */
  seq: number;
}
````

````ts
// The song-import half of a tracker integration (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.4): the file types a
// cart can import, and how it folds them into a running system. A cart contributes it to its integration - LSDj's is
// the .lsdsng/.lsdprj importer - and the UI asks the integration its roles name, so neither the drop routing nor the
// menu names a cart or imports one.
//
// The host and target types are the shell's capabilities, narrowed to what an import uses, so an import is testable
// without the stores. The shell ADAPTS its backend and systems store to them (src/songImportHost.ts): a backend matches
// `caps` alone, and none of the rest, so every write, reload and role edit an import makes is a call on the host, and
// the shell keeps the backend, the serialization of edits and the reboot.
import type { ConstructCaps, RoleInstance } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";

/** The file I/O, the battery read, the role edit and the reboot of a system an import needs, which the shell adapts
 *  its backend and systems store to. */
export interface SongImportHost {
  /** The host's file I/O, as a construct hook's caps (core's ConstructCaps: readFile, fileExists, pngDecode),
   *  because an import that carries ROM assets patches the ROM through the same reads. The shell's backend
   *  satisfies this half alone. */
  readonly caps: ConstructCaps;
  /** Write one file whole; false when it did not land. */
  writeFileAtomic(path: string, bytes: Uint8Array): boolean;
  /** The system's live battery, or null when its core has none to read. */
  readSram(id: number): Uint8Array | null;
  /** Reboot the system from `path`, the `.sav` the import just wrote. The one rebuild: the edits before it are one
   *  cold boot, not one each. */
  loadSram(id: number, path: string): unknown;
  /** Replace a role's config on the system: what an import that also carried ROM assets records beside the songs. */
  setRoleConfig(id: number, kind: string, config: Record<string, unknown>): boolean;
  /** The `.sav` a save of system `id` writes: its paired-save override when it has one, else the file beside its ROM.
   *  The host pairs them, because which file a system's save is belongs to the shell. */
  savPathOf(id: number): string;
}

/** The system an import edits: the id the host's methods name, the ROM its assets patch, and the roles it reads. */
export interface SongImportTarget {
  readonly id: number;
  readonly romPath: string;
  readonly roles: readonly RoleInstance[];
}

/** How a cart imports song files onto a running system. */
export interface TrackerSongImport {
  /** The file types this cart imports, lowercase and dot included (".lsdsng", ".lsdprj"), for a drop's routing. */
  readonly extensions: readonly string[];
  /** Apply `paths` to `sys` and reboot it once. Returns true if at least one file was imported (and the save written
   *  and the core reloaded), false otherwise: no readable battery, none applied, or the write failed. */
  import(host: SongImportHost, sys: SongImportTarget, paths: readonly string[]): boolean;
}
````

Create `packages/lsdj/ts/lsdjPlayback.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's playback contribution to its tracker integration (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.2): the SYNC
// setting it is running, the change signature over its working song, the row-timing table the controller's predictor
// runs on, and the WRAM reader that says where its playhead is. The shell's project store polls these through the
// integration its roles name; the shapes are @retroplug/tracker's, so nothing here is a type the shell has to know.
//
// The reader is built from the cart's ROM header once per system (the version decides the memory layout) and read each
// frame. Reading is pure: no backend, no emulator.
import type { TrackerPlayback } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerPlayback";
import { songRowTicksFromSav, savSyncMode, workingSongSignature } from "./playback/fromSav";
import { anyChannelPlaying, anchorRowsFromState } from "./playback/anchor";
import { LsdjReader } from "./runtime";
import type { LsdjState } from "./runtime/types";

export const LSDJ_PLAYBACK: TrackerPlayback = {
  syncMode: (sram) => savSyncMode(sram),
  songSignature: (sram) => workingSongSignature(sram),
  rowTicks: (sram) => songRowTicksFromSav(sram),
  anchor: {
    // A version with no bundled layout has no memory map to read, so there is no reader rather than one answering
    // nonsense: the same answer the controller poll's own gate gave when it keyed on the lsdj-sync role.
    reader: (header) => {
      const reader = LsdjReader.fromHeader(header);
      return reader.supported ? reader : null;
    },
    playing: (state) => anyChannelPlaying(state as LsdjState),
    rows: (state) => anchorRowsFromState(state as LsdjState),
  },
};
````

````ts
// LSDj's song-file import (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.4): adds one or more `.lsdsng`/`.lsdprj`
// files to a live LSDj system in ONE readSram → edit → write → loadSram cycle (a single cold-boot for the whole batch).
// The one orchestrator behind both the Songs menu's Add and drag-and-drop of song files onto an instance. Byte-level
// throughout (never the lossy Song model - see lsdjSongOps): `.lsdsng` folds straight into a free slot; `.lsdprj` also
// imports its kits as `lsdj-assets` overrides (linking the file by path), accumulating across the batch. Both importers
// load their song into working memory, so the LAST file dropped is the one showing after the reboot.
//
// The host is the shell's ADAPTER over its backend and systems store (packages/retroplug/src/songImportHost.ts), and the
// target is the system view's id, ROM path and roles: they are narrowed here rather than imported, because a package
// imports no shell.
import type { SongImportHost, SongImportTarget, TrackerSongImport } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerSongImport";
import { addLsdsngToSav } from "./lsdjSongOps";
import { planLsdprjImport } from "./lsdjLsdprjImport";
import { applyOverridesToRom, readOverrides, type LsdjAssetOverride } from "./lsdjAssetsRole";

/** The file types this importer handles. */
const extensions = [".lsdsng", ".lsdprj"] as const;

const isSongPath = (path: string): boolean => extensions.some((ext) => path.toLowerCase().endsWith(ext));

/** Apply `paths` (each `.lsdsng`/`.lsdprj`) to LSDj system `sys` and reboot it once. Returns true if at least one
 *  song was imported (and the SAV written + core reloaded), false otherwise (no readable SRAM, none applied, or the
 *  write failed). */
function importSongs(host: SongImportHost, sys: SongImportTarget, paths: readonly string[]): boolean {
  let sav = host.readSram(sys.id);
  if (!sav) return false;
  const baseRom = sys.romPath ? host.caps.readFile(sys.romPath) : null;
  let overrides = readOverrides(sys.roles.find((r) => r.kind === "lsdj-assets")?.config);
  let overridesChanged = false;
  let applied = 0;

  for (const path of paths) {
    const data = isSongPath(path) ? host.caps.readFile(path) : null;
    if (!data) continue;
    if (/\.lsdprj$/i.test(path)) {
      if (!baseRom) continue; // .lsdprj needs a base ROM to patch its kits into
      const plan = planLsdprjImport({
        file: data,
        path,
        effectiveRom: applyOverridesToRom(baseRom, overrides, host.caps),
        overrides,
        liveSram: sav,
      });
      if (!plan) continue;
      sav = plan.savBytes;
      if (plan.addedKits > 0) {
        overrides = plan.overrides; // accumulate; the next .lsdprj sees these kits (dedupe + free-slot)
        overridesChanged = true;
      }
      applied++;
    } else {
      const next = addLsdsngToSav(sav, data);
      if (!next) continue;
      sav = next;
      applied++;
    }
  }

  if (applied === 0) return false;
  const target = host.savPathOf(sys.id);
  if (!host.writeFileAtomic(target, sav)) return false;
  if (overridesChanged) host.setRoleConfig(sys.id, "lsdj-assets", { overrides: overrides as LsdjAssetOverride[] });
  host.loadSram(sys.id, target); // one rebuild: kit overrides → romBytes + boot the last imported song
  return true;
}

export const LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT: TrackerSongImport = { extensions, import: importSongs };
````

Create `packages/lsdj/ts/lsdjSramSignature.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's meaningful-change signature over a battery (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.3). The shell's
// loose-`.sav` auto-save asks every tracker integration for one, in product order, and falls back to a whole-image hash;
// this is the cart's, and it is the image's, not a role's: it reads the bytes and nothing else.
//
// LSDj rewrites its working RAM every frame (the work/total-time clocks tick constantly), so a whole-SRAM hash reports
// a fresh sav as "dirty" the instant it boots. Those volatile bytes are NOT modeled by the codec, so a canonical
// re-encode `encodeSong(decodeSong(workingSong))` normalises them away; the header + stored-project archive
// (0x8000..end) is static (it changes only on an explicit LSDj SAVE) and is hashed raw. The signature is dedup-only,
// never persisted.
import { decodeSong, encodeSong } from "./codec/song";

function fnvInto(h: number, bytes: Uint8Array): number {
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) {
    h ^= bytes[i];
    h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193);
  }
  return h;
}

/** The signature of a full 128 KiB LSDj `.sav`, or `null` if `bytes` isn't one (the caller then asks the next
 *  integration, and finally a whole-SRAM hash). */
export function lsdjSramSignature(bytes: Uint8Array): number | null {
  // A full LSDj image is 128 KiB with the 'jk' SRAM-init magic at 0x813E.
  if (bytes.length < 0x20000 || bytes[0x813e] !== 0x6a || bytes[0x813f] !== 0x6b) return null;
  let canonical: Uint8Array;
  try {
    canonical = encodeSong(decodeSong(bytes.subarray(0, 0x8000)));
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  let h = fnvInto(0x811c9dc5, canonical);
  h = fnvInto(h, bytes.subarray(0x8000));
  return h >>> 0;
}
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The capture table, and the generator's rule for it**

`rp.lsdj.sync`'s manifest entry declares `capture: { "midiOut": "drive", "masterSync": "listen" }`; the generator
accepts `capture` as a node field, refuses a capture that is not an object, a value that is none of `off`, `listen` or
`drive`, a capture on a node that is not wired (an unwired node is dropped from `PROTOCOL_NODES` whole, so the table
would be dead data), on a node with no `out`, and on a node whose `out` no package declares or declares with no
`serialOut`; each has its own sentence and fixture. The emitted table is spelled `{ "k": "v", ... }` like its
neighbours, `ProtocolNodeSpec.capture` is typed `SerialOutCaptureMode`, and `controller.ts` maps the (possibly forced)
mode through it with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` (not `Object.hasOwn`, which the shell's lib target
refuses).

- [ ] **Step 4: The shell's pollers, the import host, and the door the import leaves**

`projectStore.ts`: the poll, the controller's timing table and the anchor go through a new private
`controllerPlayback(id)` asking `resolveTracker(roles)?.playback`; the `"lsdj-sync"` literal and the four LSDj imports
are gone, and the poll timer, its fields and the publish stay. `graph/controller.ts`'s `serialOutCaptureFor` reads the
capture table the node declares and imports no cart. `sramAutoSave.ts`'s `sramSignature` asks `TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS`'
`sramSignature` in product order, then `hashBytes`. `fileDrop.ts`'s `DropContext.targetIsLsdj` becomes
`targetSongExtensions` and the refusal says "song files need a tracker that imports them"; recognition is the
product's extension union, so a song file dropped where nothing imports it is still refused with that reason.
`songImportHost.ts` builds tracker's host from the backend and the systems store, `render.ts`'s read stays as stage 2
left it (the shared helper is Task 4's), and `src/lsdjSongImport.ts` is deleted: its content is lsdj's. It is `git
rm`ed, not edited.

Create `packages/retroplug/src/songImportHost.ts`:

````ts
// The shell's half of a tracker integration's song import (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.4): the
// backend's files, the systems store's battery read and reload, and the `.sav` a save of the system writes, adapted to
// tracker's SongImportHost so a cart's import needs no shell import. Built where the import is called, because the
// shell owns the stores and the package must not.
import type { SongImportHost } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerSongImport";
import type { HostBackend } from "./backend";
import type { SystemsStore } from "./systemsStore";
import { resolveSavPath } from "./savPaths";

export function songImportHost(backend: HostBackend, systems: SystemsStore): SongImportHost {
  return {
    caps: backend,
    writeFileAtomic: (path, bytes) => backend.writeFileAtomic(path, bytes),
    readSram: (id) => systems.readSram(id),
    loadSram: (id, path) => systems.loadSram(id, path),
    setRoleConfig: (id, kind, config) => systems.setRoleConfig(id, kind, config),
    savPathOf: (id) => {
      const sys = systems.view().find((s) => s.id === id);
      return sys ? resolveSavPath(sys.romPath, sys.savSuffix, sys.savPath) : "";
    },
  };
}
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The new cases, and the moved signature cases**

`test/tracker/playback-absent.test.ts` pins edge E3: the equal cases (the SYNC setting null, the timing table null for
a full image with no magic, the reader null for a non-LSDj header) and the two that differ (a 64 KiB risa battery
answers a table an absent member says none for; `workingSongSignature` hashes any image of at least one song bank, so
it is non-zero and moves), because they are the reason the change is a narrowing rather than a no-op. Its last case is
the store-level one the stage 3 review asked for: a `gbRom()` with a 64 KiB risa battery and the controller enabled
does not refresh, publishes nothing, notifies nothing across an edit, reads no sync and publishes an empty table.
`lsdj/ts/test/sramSignature.test.ts` is the moved `lsdjSramSignature` cases (the ticking clock normalised, a real edit
caught, null for a non-LSDj image and for a full-size one with no magic).

````ts
// A system whose tracker integration has no `playback` member reads "no sync mode, no signature, no timing table, no
// reader" (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 6, edge E3). For a battery that is not the cart's, that is
// what LSDj's own functions answered before the controller poll went through the integration - which is what the poll
// relied on, since it asked them of every system. The exceptions are recorded here too, because they are the reason
// this is a narrowing rather than a no-op: no shipped combination reaches them (MI.MAP drives an LSDj cart), and they
// are the two cases where a non-LSDj battery used to move the controller's state.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { lsdjIntegration } from "@retroplug/lsdj/lsdjIntegration";
import { kModernRegions, kSongByteCount } from "@retroplug/lsdj/codec/regions";
import { savBytes as risaSav } from "@retroplug/risa/testFixtures";
import type { TrackerPlayback } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerPlayback";
import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { composeAppStores } from "../../src/appStores";
import { gbRom } from "../systems/fixtures";

const LSDJ = lsdjIntegration.playback!;

/** The answers a system with no playback member gives: no sync mode, no signature, no table, no reader. */
const ABSENT: TrackerPlayback = {
  syncMode: () => null,
  songSignature: () => 0,
  rowTicks: () => null,
  anchor: { reader: () => null, playing: () => false, rows: () => [] },
};

/** A 64 KiB battery no cart's (risa's v2 catalog): past LSDj's song bank, short of a full LSDj image. */
const otherCart = risaSav("v2_blumarbl");
/** A full-size image that carries no LSDj 'jk' magic: the size `workingSongSignature` hashes, and `decodeSav` refuses. */
const unrecognised = new Uint8Array(0x20000);

test("E3: the SYNC setting agrees - neither answers for a battery that is not LSDj's", () => {
  for (const sram of [otherCart, unrecognised, null]) {
    expect(LSDJ.syncMode(sram)).toBe(ABSENT.syncMode(sram));
    expect(LSDJ.syncMode(sram)).toBe(null);
  }
});

test("E3: the timing table agrees for an image no cart can decode", () => {
  // decodeSav throws on a full-size image with no magic, and songRowTicksFromSav answers null rather than throwing:
  // the same null an absent member gives, so the controller's empty table is unchanged.
  expect(LSDJ.rowTicks(unrecognised)).toBe(null);
  expect(ABSENT.rowTicks(unrecognised)).toBe(null);
});

test("E3: the timing table DIFFERS for a battery between 32 and 128 KiB (nothing shipped reaches it)", () => {
  // decodeSav reads a 64 KiB image as an early-LSDj one and songRowTicks runs over bytes that are not a song, so the
  // cart answers a table where an absent member says none. The controller then shaded rows of a battery that is not
  // an LSDj cart's; MI.MAP never drives one, so no shipped project ever saw it.
  expect(otherCart.length >= kSongByteCount && otherCart.length < 0x20000).toBe(true);
  expect(LSDJ.rowTicks(otherCart) !== null).toBe(true);
  expect(ABSENT.rowTicks(otherCart)).toBe(null);
});

test("E3: the song signature DIFFERS for any image of at least one song bank (nothing shipped reaches it)", () => {
  // workingSongSignature hashes the song-structure regions of ANY image that long, so a non-LSDj battery used to
  // report a moving signature - re-publishing the graph and notifying the systems observers on the poll. An absent
  // member answers 0, which compares equal to itself and so never fires.
  expect(otherCart.length >= kSongByteCount).toBe(true);
  const sig = LSDJ.songSignature(otherCart);
  expect(sig !== 0).toBe(true);
  expect(sig === ABSENT.songSignature(otherCart)).toBe(false);
  // It MOVES: a byte in a region the table is derived from is what an in-cart edit looks like.
  const edited = otherCart.slice();
  edited[kModernRegions.chainAssignments] ^= 0xff;
  expect(LSDJ.songSignature(edited) !== sig).toBe(true);
});

test("E3: the reader agrees - an absent member and an unsupported build both have none", () => {
  const notLsdj = new Uint8Array(0x150); // a Game Boy header whose title is not LSDj's
  expect(LSDJ.anchor.reader(notLsdj)).toBe(null);
  expect(ABSENT.anchor.reader(notLsdj)).toBe(null);
  // Neither ever reports a start, so the not-playing -> playing edge cannot fire.
  expect(ABSENT.anchor.playing(null)).toBe(false);
  expect(ABSENT.anchor.rows(null)).toEqual([]);
});

// ---- the store's absent path, which is what E3 actually changes -----------------------------------

test("E3: a system that runs no tracker neither publishes nor notifies, and holds no timing table", () => {
  // The two DIFFERS cases above are what the old poll acted on: a non-LSDj battery moved the signature, so the poll
  // re-published the graph and notified every observer, and its timing table shaded rows. A system whose integration
  // has no playback now answers all four reads itself, so none of that fires - the store-level half of E3.
  const be = new MockBackend();
  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: be });
  be.seed("/roms/other.gb", gbRom()); // a Game Boy cart whose title names no tracker
  stores.project.systems.addSystem("/roms/other.gb");
  const id = stores.project.systems.view()[0].id;
  be.setSram(id, otherCart.slice()); // a 64 KiB battery: the one the OLD poll read a moving signature from
  stores.project.setController({ enabled: true });

  let publishes = 0;
  const graph = stores.project.graph;
  const publish = graph.publish.bind(graph);
  graph.publish = (...args) => {
    publishes++;
    return publish(...args);
  };
  let notifies = 0;
  stores.project.addOnSystemsChange(() => void notifies++);

  // The first look adopts nothing either: with no playback there is no signature to adopt and no start to anchor.
  expect(stores.project.refreshControllerSong()).toBe(false);
  expect(publishes).toBe(0);
  expect(notifies).toBe(0);
  expect(stores.project.controllerCartSync()).toBe(null);
  // The model the publish derives: an empty table reads as "no content anywhere", which is what a table-less
  // integration gives.
  expect(be.graphNode("controller")?.settings?.songRowTicks).toEqual([]);

  // An edit in the region the signature hashed: the battery moves, the poll stays silent.
  const edited = otherCart.slice();
  edited[kModernRegions.chainAssignments] ^= 0xff;
  be.setSram(id, edited);
  expect(stores.project.refreshControllerSong()).toBe(false);
  expect(publishes).toBe(0);
  expect(notifies).toBe(0);
});
````

Create `packages/lsdj/ts/test/sramSignature.test.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's meaningful-change signature over a battery (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.3): the shell's
// loose-`.sav` auto-save asks each tracker integration for one and falls back to a whole-image hash, so this is what an
// LSDj image answers with, and null is how it hands any other image on.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { savFrom } from "../index";
import { lsdjSramSignature } from "../lsdjSramSignature";

const WORK_HOURS = 0x3fb2; // a ticking work-clock byte: LSDj rewrites it every frame; NOT modeled
const TEMPO = 0x3fb4; // a meaningful, modeled byte

test("lsdjSramSignature ignores the ticking work-clock but catches a real edit", () => {
  const orig = savFrom({ workingSong: { settings: { tempo: 150 } } });
  expect(orig.length).toBe(0x20000);

  // A frame tick bumps the work clock (and its checksum) but changes nothing meaningful.
  const ticked = orig.slice();
  ticked[WORK_HOURS] = (ticked[WORK_HOURS] + 7) & 0xff;
  ticked[0x3fb9] = (ticked[0x3fb9] + 7) & 0xff; // totalTimeChecksum
  expect(lsdjSramSignature(ticked)).toBe(lsdjSramSignature(orig)); // same signature
  expect(ticked[WORK_HOURS] !== orig[WORK_HOURS]).toBe(true); // but the raw bytes differ

  // A tempo change IS meaningful (a modeled field) → the signature changes.
  const edited = orig.slice();
  edited[TEMPO] = 90;
  expect(lsdjSramSignature(edited) === lsdjSramSignature(orig)).toBeFalsy();
});

test("lsdjSramSignature answers null for an image that is not a full LSDj one", () => {
  expect(lsdjSramSignature(new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3, 4]))).toBe(null); // far too short
  // A full-size image without the 'jk' SRAM-init magic is some other cart's: the next integration, or the hash, takes it.
  expect(lsdjSramSignature(new Uint8Array(0x20000))).toBe(null);
});
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f4apro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

### Task 4: the role hooks, the embedded ROM and the cart-named API

Design sections 4.5, 4.6, 5.2, 5.3, 7.4 item 4 and 8's fourth stage. The carts' last shell-side tables and rules become
the roles' own, and the two APIs that named a cart become ids a package registers.

`RoleType` gains `parameters(config)`, `deriveConfig { headerBytes(short), derive }` and `hostLatencyMs(config)`. mGB's
and BlipToaster's parameter tables move into their packages, with the CC-spec types and `expandRomSpec` into
`core/ts/romParameters.ts` because a package may not import the shell and each cart builds its table with them.
BlipToaster's chip scan becomes its role's `deriveConfig`, and the header read (the providers' prefix, then each role's
deeper request) becomes ONE helper, `src/rolesForRom.ts`, which the store's `defaultRoles` and a render's
`resolveRenderRom` both call; the providers see the short header and write no `chip`, so the field has one writer. LSDj's
sync role serves its 33 ms, so the plugin sums its systems' PLACED roles through the registry. `inheritLinkGroup` finds
each system's core-config role and gates on the console's `linkCable`, and `savFromJson` leaves `ConstructCaps` and the
backend so the shell has no sav encoder.

The embedded ROM is declared in TypeScript and paired with the manifest's `embed` by the generated module; the start
menu's rows read the registry's labels. `loadEmbedded(id)` and `compileKitFormat(id, spec)` replace `loadMgb`,
`compileKit` and `compileDmc` in every caller, including the Node addon and the SDK's types. Nothing is re-recorded.

**Files:**

- Create (9): `packages/bliptoaster/ts/parameters.ts`, `packages/core/ts/romParameters.ts`, `packages/mgb/ts/parameters.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/embeds.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/rolesForRom.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/controller/sync-latency.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/midi/recordedParameters.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/midi/role-parameters.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/systems/role-derive.test.ts`
- Modify (86 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 23 under `packages/retroplug/test-native/`; 9 under `packages/retroplug/src/`; 6 under `packages/retroplug/cli/sessions/`; 4 under `packages/retroplug/test/systems/`; 3 under `packages/lsdj/ts/`; 3 under `packages/retroplug/test-native/parity/` and the rest)

what absent means and what a hook may assume (a role's `derive` is called only with a readable file's bytes;

Create `packages/core/ts/romParameters.ts`:

````ts
// A ROM's DAW automation parameters, as the cart that owns the ROM describes them (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md
// section 4.5): one lane per control a build responds to, and the expansion of a build's CC table into those lanes. The
// shell's projectParameterMap (packages/retroplug/src/parameterMap.ts) projects the lanes onto the plugin's fixed slot
// pool; a cart's app module supplies the table, so the shell knows no cart's CC set and no cart's build names.
//
// The tables themselves are transcribed from each ROM's own documentation, not guessed (mGB's from the MIDI
// implementation map in trash80/mGB's README, BlipToaster's from the per-chip tables in its docs/chips/*.md).

/** One control a ROM exposes, expanded to a single automation lane. */
export interface RomParameter {
  /** 0-based MIDI channel the ROM listens on for this control, relative to the ROM's first voice. */
  channel: number;
  /** MIDI CC number, 0..127. */
  cc: number;
  /** Full name for the host's parameter list. */
  name: string;
  /** Abbreviated name for hosts that show a short parameter label. */
  shortName: string;
}

/** One CC a ROM responds to, and which of its 0-based channels accept it. */
export interface CcSpec {
  cc: number;
  /** Parameter name, prefixed with the voice name unless `shared`. */
  name: string;
  /** Abbreviated name, prefixed with the voice's short tag unless `shared`. */
  short: string;
  /** 0-based channels that respond to it. */
  channels: number[];
  /** The control is chip-global rather than per-voice (one register shared by several channels), so it
   *  gets ONE lane, addressed on `channels[0]`, with no voice prefix. */
  shared?: boolean;
}

/** A ROM build: what its voices are called, and every CC it responds to. */
export interface RomSpec {
  /** 0-based channel -> voice name. A gap (undefined) means that channel carries no voice. */
  voices: (readonly [full: string, short: string] | undefined)[];
  ccs: CcSpec[];
}

// Deliberately NOT exposed as lanes, on every ROM: the RPN bend-range handshake (CC101/100/6/38 is a
// three-message sequence, not a value) and the channel-mode messages (CC120 All Sound Off, CC121 Reset
// All Controllers, CC123 All Notes Off) - automating a panic message is actively harmful.

/** Expand a build's CC table into one lane per (CC, channel), in channel-then-CC order so a host's
 *  parameter list reads voice by voice. A `shared` CC contributes a single un-prefixed lane. */
export function expandRomSpec(spec: RomSpec): RomParameter[] {
  const out: RomParameter[] = [];

  for (let ch = 0; ch < spec.voices.length; ch++) {
    const voice = spec.voices[ch];
    if (!voice) continue;
    for (const c of spec.ccs) {
      if (!c.channels.includes(ch)) continue;
      if (c.shared) {
        if (c.channels[0] !== ch) continue; // one lane only, on its first channel
        out.push({ channel: ch, cc: c.cc, name: c.name, shortName: c.short });
      } else {
        out.push({
          channel: ch,
          cc: c.cc,
          name: `${voice[0]} ${c.name}`,
          shortName: `${voice[1]} ${c.short}`,
        });
      }
    }
  }

  return out;
}
````

````ts
// mGB's DAW parameter table (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.5): the lanes the synth's MIDI
// implementation map exposes, which the `mgb` role serves through its `parameters` hook. From the map in trash80/mGB's
// README: MIDI 1 PU1, 2 PU2, 3 WAV, 4 NOISE (channel 5 is POLY mode, for which the README documents no CCs, so it claims
// none).
import { expandRomSpec, type RomParameter, type RomSpec } from "@retroplug/core/romParameters";

const MGB_PU1 = 0, MGB_PU2 = 1, MGB_WAV = 2, MGB_NOI = 3;
const MGB: RomSpec = {
  voices: [["PU1", "PU1"], ["PU2", "PU2"], ["WAV", "WAV"], ["Noise", "Noi"]],
  ccs: [
    // CC1 and CC2 mean different things on WAV than on the pulses, so they are split into two specs.
    { cc: 1, name: "Pulse Width", short: "Width", channels: [MGB_PU1, MGB_PU2] },
    { cc: 2, name: "Envelope", short: "Env", channels: [MGB_PU1, MGB_PU2, MGB_NOI] },
    { cc: 1, name: "Shape", short: "Shape", channels: [MGB_WAV] },
    { cc: 2, name: "Shape Offset", short: "Offset", channels: [MGB_WAV] },
    { cc: 3, name: "Pitch Sweep", short: "Sweep", channels: [MGB_PU1, MGB_WAV] },
    { cc: 4, name: "Bend Range", short: "Bend", channels: [MGB_PU1, MGB_PU2, MGB_WAV] },
    { cc: 5, name: "Load Preset", short: "Preset", channels: [MGB_PU1, MGB_PU2, MGB_WAV, MGB_NOI] },
    { cc: 10, name: "Pan", short: "Pan", channels: [MGB_PU1, MGB_PU2, MGB_WAV, MGB_NOI] },
    { cc: 64, name: "Sustain", short: "Sus", channels: [MGB_PU1, MGB_PU2, MGB_WAV, MGB_NOI] },
  ],
};

/** mGB's lanes, in the order a host lists them. */
export const MGB_PARAMETERS: readonly RomParameter[] = expandRomSpec(MGB);
````

````ts
// BlipToaster's DAW parameter tables (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.5): one per expansion build,
// keyed by the `chip` on the system's `bliptoaster` role, plus the lanes each expands to. The `bliptoaster` role serves
// them through its `parameters` hook, so the shell's slot projection asks this cart rather than holding a copy.
//
// The CCs are transcribed from BlipToaster's own per-chip documentation (its docs/chips/*.md), not guessed.
import { expandRomSpec, type CcSpec, type RomParameter, type RomSpec } from "@retroplug/core/romParameters";

// Channel map is the same on every build: 1 Pulse 1, 2 Pulse 2, 3 Triangle, 4 Noise, 5 DMC, then the
// expansion voices from 6, and (where the build has it) polyphony on 12.
const BT_CORE_VOICES = [
  ["Pulse 1", "P1"],
  ["Pulse 2", "P2"],
  ["Triangle", "Tri"],
  ["Noise", "Noi"],
  ["DMC", "DMC"],
] as const;

const P1 = 0, P2 = 1, TRI = 2, NOI = 3, DMC = 4, POLY = 11;

// The 2A03 core, present on every BlipToaster build. Per-CC channel lists are from docs/chips/2a03.md.

  { cc: 21, name: "Sustain / Length Flag", short: "Sus", channels: [P1, P2, TRI, NOI] },
  { cc: 22, name: "Envelope Rate", short: "EnvRat", channels: [P1, P2, NOI] },
  { cc: 23, name: "Gate Length", short: "Gate", channels: [P1, P2, TRI, NOI] },
  { cc: 24, name: "Sweep Rate", short: "SwpRat", channels: [P1, P2] },
  { cc: 25, name: "Sweep Direction", short: "SwpDir", channels: [P1, P2] },
  { cc: 26, name: "Sweep Shift", short: "SwpShf", channels: [P1, P2] },
  { cc: 27, name: "Linear Reload", short: "LinRel", channels: [TRI] },
  { cc: 64, name: "Sustain Pedal", short: "Pedal", channels: [P1, P2, TRI, NOI] },
  { cc: 115, name: "MOD Hack", short: "MOD", channels: [P1, P2] },
  { cc: 116, name: "MOD Rate", short: "MODRat", channels: [P1, P2] },
  { cc: 117, name: "Fine Bend", short: "Fine", channels: [P1, P2, TRI] },
  // DMC / sample channel
  { cc: 3, name: "Sample Rate", short: "Rate", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 9, name: "Traveler Step", short: "TrvStp", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 14, name: "Kit / Index Mode", short: "Kit", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 85, name: "Address Override", short: "AdrEn", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 86, name: "Start Address", short: "Start", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 87, name: "Length Override", short: "Len", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 88, name: "Loop", short: "Loop", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 89, name: "Direct PCM", short: "PCM", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 90, name: "DAC Value", short: "DAC", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 118, name: "Wave Traveler", short: "Trav", channels: [DMC] },
  { cc: 119, name: "Traveler Speed", short: "TrvSpd", channels: [DMC] },
];

/** Copy the core CC set, adding `channels` to whichever CCs an expansion build extends. */
function extendCore(extra: Record<number, number[]>): CcSpec[] {
  return BT_CORE_CCS.map((c) =>
    extra[c.cc] ? { ...c, channels: [...c.channels, ...extra[c.cc]] } : c,
  );

const BT_2A03: RomSpec = { voices: [...BT_CORE_VOICES], ccs: BT_CORE_CCS };

// VRC6: 2 pulse (8 duty steps) + a sawtooth whose rate register is its amplitude, plus square polyphony.

// Sunsoft 5B: three squares sharing ONE hardware envelope and ONE noise generator, so CC28/29/30 are
// chip-global (one lane each), while the per-voice noise mix and volume are not.
const S5B_A = 5, S5B_B = 6, S5B_C = 7;
const BT_S5B: RomSpec = {
  voices: [
    ...BT_CORE_VOICES,
    ["Square A", "SqA"], ["Square B", "SqB"], ["Square C", "SqC"],
  ],
  ccs: [
    ...extendCore({
      7: [S5B_A, S5B_B, S5B_C],
      20: [S5B_A, S5B_B, S5B_C],
      64: [S5B_A, S5B_B, S5B_C],
      117: [S5B_A, S5B_B, S5B_C],
    }),
    { cc: 28, name: "S5B Envelope Rate", short: "S5BRat", channels: [S5B_A], shared: true },
    { cc: 29, name: "S5B Envelope Shape", short: "S5BShp", channels: [S5B_A], shared: true },
    { cc: 30, name: "S5B Noise Period", short: "S5BNoi", channels: [S5B_A], shared: true },
  ],
};

// Namco 163: four wavetable voices; CC1 selects the waveform.
const N163_CH = [5, 6, 7, 8];
const BT_N163: RomSpec = {
  voices: [
    ...BT_CORE_VOICES,
    ["Wave 0", "W0"], ["Wave 1", "W1"], ["Wave 2", "W2"], ["Wave 3", "W3"],
  ],
  ccs: extendCore({
    1: N163_CH,
    7: N163_CH,
    15: N163_CH,
    64: N163_CH,
    117: N163_CH,
  }),
};

// MMC5: two squares mirroring the 2A03 pulses (envelope + length, but no sweep), plus square polyphony.
const M5_P1 = 5, M5_P2 = 6;
const BT_MMC5: RomSpec = {
  voices: [
    ...BT_CORE_VOICES,
    ["MMC5 Pulse 1", "M5P1"], ["MMC5 Pulse 2", "M5P2"],
    undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined,
    ["Poly", "Poly"],
  ],
  ccs: extendCore({
    1: [M5_P1, M5_P2, POLY],
    7: [M5_P1, M5_P2, POLY],
    15: [M5_P1, M5_P2, POLY],
    20: [M5_P1, M5_P2],
    21: [M5_P1, M5_P2],
    22: [M5_P1, M5_P2],
    23: [M5_P1, M5_P2],
    64: [M5_P1, M5_P2, POLY],
    115: [M5_P1, M5_P2, POLY],
    116: [M5_P1, M5_P2, POLY],
    117: [M5_P1, M5_P2, POLY],
  }),
};

/** BlipToaster build -> its parameter set. Keyed by the `chip` on the system's `bliptoaster` role. */
export const BLIPTOASTER_SPECS: Record<string, RomSpec> = {
  "2a03": BT_2A03,
  vrc6: BT_VRC6,
  vrc7: BT_VRC7,
  s5b: BT_S5B,
  n163: BT_N163,
  mmc5: BT_MMC5,
};

/** The lanes a build exposes, by the `chip` config its role carries. An unknown chip (an older project, or a build newer
 *  than this table) falls back to the 2A03 core, which every BlipToaster build has: fewer lanes, never wrong ones. */
export function blipToasterParameters(config: Record<string, unknown>): readonly RomParameter[] {
  const chip = typeof config.chip === "string" ? config.chip : "2a03";
  return expandRomSpec(BLIPTOASTER_SPECS[chip] ?? BT_2A03);
}
````

after the providers (decision 11) and a loaded project (`withDerivedRoleFacts`, now `derivedRoleConfigs`).
`bliptoaster`'s role derives `chip`: `headerBytes` is the short length unless the ROM predates the SIG chip tag, when

Create `packages/retroplug/src/rolesForRom.ts`:

````ts
// The roles a ROM gets, in ONE place: the header the shell reads for the ROM providers, the providers' own role
// suggestions, and the config fields a role derives from the FILE rather than from the user's choices
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.5). A fresh system's build (SystemsStore.defaultRoles) and a render's
// classification of the ROM it is about to build (render/render.ts resolveRenderRom) both come through here, so a render
// asks the integration the built system will have instead of keeping a second copy of the read.
//
// The read is in TIERS, because two cases need more than a header and neither is the common one:
//
//  - **Sega always.** No title field, and the header itself sits at the END of a bank. smsggdj's marker is at $3640, so
//    a ROLE_HEADER_LEN read would leave the provider nothing to match on and force `sms-sync` onto every SMS cart -
//    which it must not, since it drives Player 2's button lines. The console's descriptor says how much: its
//    `providerHeaderBytes`.
//  - **A role that derives a fact from deeper in the file.** BlipToaster's chip is named in the SIG block for a tagged
//    ROM (inside the short header) and only in the on-screen label inside the PRG region for an older one, so the role's
//    `deriveConfig.headerBytes` asks for the deeper read exactly then. A role that asks for nothing pays nothing.
import { ROLE_HEADER_LEN, type RoleInstance, type RoleRegistry } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { providerHeaderBytes, type Core, type Platform } from "./consoles";

/** A reader of a file's first `length` bytes: the backend's readFilePrefix, narrowed to what the roles need. */
export interface RoleHeaderReader {
  readFilePrefix(path: string, length: number): Uint8Array | null;
}

/** What a ROM build asks of the roles: its console, the core that runs it, and where its bytes are. `embeddedRom` is the
 *  baked-in marker ("" for a file-backed ROM), the one signal an embedded ROM has, since its bytes never reach TS. */
export interface RomRoles {
  readonly core: Core;
  readonly platform: Platform;
  readonly romPath: string;
  readonly embeddedRom?: string;
}

function readHeader(reader: RoleHeaderReader, romPath: string, length: number): Uint8Array {
  return reader.readFilePrefix(romPath, length) ?? new Uint8Array();
}

/** The roles a fresh system built from `rom` gets: the core-config role, then every provider's feature roles for the
 *  header it is shown, with each role's ROM-derived config fields applied. Empty for a ROM with no file to read (an
 *  embedded one), which is what its providers are told. */
export function rolesForRom(registry: RoleRegistry, reader: RoleHeaderReader, rom: RomRoles): RoleInstance[] {
  const embeddedRom = rom.embeddedRom ?? "";
  const header =
    rom.romPath && !embeddedRom
      ? readHeader(reader, rom.romPath, providerHeaderBytes(rom.platform) ?? ROLE_HEADER_LEN)
      : new Uint8Array();
  const roles = registry.defaultRoles(rom.core, rom.platform, header, embeddedRom);
  return derivedRoleConfigs(registry, reader, roles, rom, header);
}

/** `roles` with each role's ROM-derived config fields applied, for a role list that is already known (a loaded
 *  project's, which was stored). `header` is a read the caller already made, when it made one. */
export function derivedRoleConfigs(
  registry: RoleRegistry,
  reader: RoleHeaderReader,
  roles: readonly RoleInstance[],
  rom: Pick<RomRoles, "romPath" | "embeddedRom">,
  header?: Uint8Array,
): RoleInstance[] {
  const embeddedRom = rom.embeddedRom ?? "";
  if (!rom.romPath || embeddedRom) return [...roles];
  const deriving = roles.flatMap((role) => {
    const derive = registry.roleType(role.kind)?.deriveConfig;
    return derive ? [derive] : [];
  });
  if (!deriving.length) return [...roles];

  // An unreadable file derives nothing: the roles keep the config they carry, as they always have. A role that
  // derives from zero bytes would otherwise be asked to write a "fact" about nothing.
  let bytes = header ?? readHeader(reader, rom.romPath, ROLE_HEADER_LEN);
  if (!bytes.length) return [...roles];
  // The short header is what every role's `headerBytes` is asked about; a role that needs more asks for it, and the
  // deepest answer is read ONCE for all of them.
  const short = bytes.length > ROLE_HEADER_LEN ? bytes.subarray(0, ROLE_HEADER_LEN) : bytes;
  let need = short.length;
  for (const derive of deriving) need = Math.max(need, derive.headerBytes(short));
  if (need > bytes.length) bytes = readHeader(reader, rom.romPath, need);

  return roles.map((role) => {
    const derive = registry.roleType(role.kind)?.deriveConfig;
    return derive ? { ...role, config: derive.derive(bytes, role.config ?? {}) } : role;
  });
}
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The embed: the TS declaration, the generated pairing, and the menu**

`PackageContributions.embeds` is `Embeds[]` (`{ id, label, platform }`), mgb's app declares `{ id: "mgb", label: "mGB
(GB MIDI Synth)", platform: "gb" }` beside the manifest's `retroplug.embed`, and the generator reads and validates the
manifest side (a malformed entry and a duplicated id) and emits `EMBEDS` and `MANIFEST_EMBEDS`. The generated
`packages.ts` refuses a manifest entry no app module declares, a declaration no manifest bakes in, the two halves in
different packages, an id declared by two packages or twice by one, and a platform no console registers.
`src/embeds.ts` is the registry the shell reads (`embeddedRoms`, `embeddedRomOf`), the start menu's rows are generated
from it (identical today: `Load mGB (GB MIDI Synth)`, action id `start-mgb`), and `SystemsStore.loadEmbedded` takes
the platform from the declaration (the store's diff is the derived-chip step's).

Create `packages/retroplug/src/embeds.ts`:

````ts
// The embedded ROMs the product bakes into its binary (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 5.2): mGB's synth
// is one. Which ids exist, what to call them and which console each runs on are the OWNING PACKAGE's declaration (its
// app module's `embeds`, paired with the manifest entry that names the file), so a load of an embedded ROM takes its
// platform from data rather than the shell assuming "an embedded ROM is a Game Boy".
//
// The generated list is src/generated/packages.ts, beside the roles and the providers: the same module concatenates
// every package's app contribution, in product order.
import type { Embed } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import { EMBEDS } from "./generated/packages";

/** Every embedded ROM a package of this product declares, in product order. */
export function embeddedRoms(): readonly Embed[] {
  return EMBEDS;
}

/** The declaration of the embedded ROM `id` names, or undefined for an id nothing declares: what `loadEmbedded`
 *  refuses rather than booting a resource native has no bytes for. */
export function embeddedRomOf(id: string): Embed | undefined {
  return EMBEDS.find((embed) => embed.id === id);
}
````

````diff
+        json.retroplug.embed = [{ id: "shared-rom", file: "rom/alpha.bin" }];
+      });
+      editManifest("beta", (json) => {
+        json.retroplug.embed = [{ id: "shared-rom", file: "rom/beta.bin" }];
+      });
+      generate({ root });
+      try {
+        result = await loadPackages();
+      } catch (e) {
+        result = { error: e.message };
+      }
+      break;
+    case "embed-declared-twice":
+      // One package declaring one id twice: the menu would offer two rows for one ROM and the store would take the
+      // first, so the generated module counts declarations, not declaring packages.
+      writeTree(
+        "packages/alpha/ts/app.ts",
+        embedApp("alpha", [
+          { id: "alpha-rom", platform: "nes" },
+          { id: "alpha-rom", platform: "nes" },
+        ]),
+      );
+      writeTree(
+        "packages/alpha/ts/consoles.ts",
+        consoleModule({ descriptors: [{ id: "alpha.nes", core: "alpha-core", nodeType: "rp.alpha.nes", platform: "nes" }] }),
+      );
+      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
+        json.retroplug.embed = [{ id: "alpha-rom", file: "rom/alpha.bin" }];
+      });
+      generate({ root });
+      try {
+        result = await loadPackages();
+      } catch (e) {
+        result = { error: e.message };
+      }
+      break;
+    case "embed-manifest-not-list":
+      // The manifest half is a list of resources; anything else names no bytes to bake in.
+      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
+        json.retroplug.embed = { id: "alpha-rom", file: "rom/alpha.bin" };
+      });
+      result = refusal();
+      break;
+    case "embed-manifest-no-id":
+      // A resource native's table cannot name: it is looked up by the id an app module declares.
+      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
+        json.retroplug.embed = [{ file: "rom/alpha.bin" }];
+      });
+      result = refusal();
+      break;
+    case "embed-manifest-no-file":
+      // An id with nothing baked in under it.
+      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
+        json.retroplug.embed = [{ id: "alpha-rom" }];
+      });
+      result = refusal();
+      break;
+    case "embed-manifest-id-twice":
+      // Two files under one id: which resource native bakes in would be whichever the table listed last.
+      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
+        json.retroplug.embed = [
+          { id: "alpha-rom", file: "rom/alpha.bin" },
+          { id: "alpha-rom", file: "rom/other.bin" },
+        ];
+      });
+      result = refusal();
+      break;
+    case "embed-mismatched-package":
+      // Declared by one package and baked in by another: the two halves of an embedded ROM are one package's.
+      writeTree("packages/alpha/ts/app.ts", embedApp("alpha", [{ id: "beta-rom", platform: "nes" }]));
+      editManifest("beta", (json) => {
+        json.retroplug.embed = [{ id: "beta-rom", file: "rom/beta.bin" }];
+      });
+      generate({ root });
+      try {
+        result = await loadPackages();
+      } catch (e) {
+        result = { error: e.message };
+      }
+      break;
     default:
       console.error(`run-generator.mjs: unknown mode "${MODE}"`);
       process.exit(2);
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The cart-named API, and every caller**

`SystemsStore.loadMgb()` becomes `loadEmbedded(id)`, which refuses an id no package declares by returning null and
takes the platform from the declaration; the two "embedded means gb" lines go. `AudioDriver.compileKit`/`compileDmc`
become `compileKitFormat<S>(id, spec)` (`async`, so an unknown id rejects), dispatching through `kitFormat(id)`; the
two cart formats' compilers take names that say which bank they compile, `compileLsdjKit` and `compileRisaKit`.
`src/kit`'s two files re-export them for now (Task 5 deletes the doors). Every caller in the repository is updated:
the CLI's six sessions, the Node addon's `emu-ops.mjs` and README, the SDK's types, and the tests whose subjects are
those calls. No `loadMgb`, `compileKit` or `compileDmc` token is left outside the dated records.

- [ ] **Step 7: The new tests**

`test/midi/recordedParameters.ts` is the tables the design commit's `parameterMap.ts` expanded (mGB 24 lanes, the six
BlipToaster builds 51, 73, 88, 66, 71 and 80), and `role-parameters.test.ts` holds each role's answer to them lane for
lane through the registry. `role-derive.test.ts` pins the deep read only for a role that asks (tagged 0x150, untagged
at least 0x4010, a non-BlipToaster NES 0x150) and the guard the stage 4 review restored: an unreadable ROM leaves a
stored `chip` alone. `sync-latency.test.ts` holds every LSDj sync mode's latency and that a role with none declares no
hook.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/midi/recordedParameters.ts`:

````ts
// The DAW parameter tables are their carts' now (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.5): the `mgb` role
// serves mGB's lanes, the `bliptoaster` role serves the lanes of the build its `chip` config names, and the shell's slot
// projection asks the registry. This holds the move to the bytes: every lane the shell expanded before the move, for
// mGB and for each of BlipToaster's six builds, comes back lane for lane (test/midi/recordedParameters.ts, recorded from
// the design commit's parameterMap.ts), so no host sees a different parameter list than it did.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { buildAppRegistry } from "../../src/appHost";
import { projectParameterMap } from "../../src/parameterMap";
import { MidiRouting } from "@retroplug/core/midiRouting";
import type { RomParameter } from "@retroplug/core/romParameters";
import { RECORDED_PARAMETER_LANES } from "./recordedParameters";

const registry = buildAppRegistry();

/** The lanes a role kind serves for `config`, as the projection asks for them. */
const lanesOf = (kind: string, config: Record<string, unknown> = {}): readonly RomParameter[] | undefined =>
  registry.roleType(kind)?.parameters?.(config);

test("mGB's role serves exactly the lanes the shell's own table expanded", () => {
  expect(lanesOf("mgb")).toEqual(RECORDED_PARAMETER_LANES.mgb);
});

for (const chip of ["2a03", "vrc6", "vrc7", "s5b", "n163", "mmc5"]) {
  test(`BlipToaster's ${chip} build serves exactly the lanes the shell's own table expanded`, () => {
    expect(lanesOf("bliptoaster", { chip })).toEqual(RECORDED_PARAMETER_LANES[chip]);
  });
}

test("an unknown chip, or none, serves the 2A03 core's lanes", () => {
  // An older project (before the field) or a build newer than this table: the core set is never wrong for a build,
  // only narrower.
  expect(lanesOf("bliptoaster", { chip: "fictional" })).toEqual(RECORDED_PARAMETER_LANES["2a03"]);
  expect(lanesOf("bliptoaster")).toEqual(RECORDED_PARAMETER_LANES["2a03"]);
});

test("the projection reaches the same lanes through the registry, slot for slot", () => {
  // The whole path a host sees: a system's roles in, the registry's tables, the slot pool out. The mGB system's first
  // lane is slot 0, and there are exactly as many claimed lanes as the table has under SendToAll.
  const map = projectParameterMap([{ roles: [{ kind: "mgb" }] }], MidiRouting.SendToAll, registry);
  expect(map.length).toEqual(RECORDED_PARAMETER_LANES.mgb.length);
  expect(map[0].slot).toEqual(0);
  const first = RECORDED_PARAMETER_LANES.mgb[0];
  expect([map[0].channel, map[0].cc, map[0].name, map[0].shortName]).toEqual([
    first.channel,
    first.cc,
    first.name,
    first.shortName,
  ]);
  // A role whose type serves no parameters claims nothing, and the registry is what says so.
  expect(projectParameterMap([{ roles: [{ kind: "sameboy", config: {} }] }], MidiRouting.SendToAll, registry)).toEqual(
    [],
  );
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/systems/role-derive.test.ts`:

````ts
// A role's ROM-derived config (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.5): BlipToaster's `chip` is a fact
// about the ROM FILE, so the store re-derives it at every build - the role says how much of the file it needs, and the
// read happens only for a role that asks for it. Today that role is `bliptoaster`: a tagged ROM names its build in the
// short SIG block, an untagged one only in the on-screen label inside the PRG region, and a ROM that is not BlipToaster
// at all is never read deeper than the short header.
//
// The behaviour held here is the one the provider's header read had: a fresh load of an untagged S5B build gets `s5b`
// (not the ambiguous mapper's fallback), and a cart that is not BlipToaster pays no deep read. What changed is WHERE it
// is decided (the role's hook, not a NES branch in the shell) and that a fresh build now derives through the same
// function a loaded project does.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { SystemsStore } from "../../src/systemsStore";
import { RoleRegistry } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { registerCoreRoles } from "../_coreRoles";
import { registerFeatureRoles } from "../_featureRoles";
import { registerBlipToasterRole } from "@retroplug/bliptoaster/bliptoasterRole";
import { registerBlipToasterAssetsRole } from "@retroplug/bliptoaster/bliptoasterAssetsRole";
import { registerRomProviders } from "../../src/romProviders";
import { blipToasterRom, nesRom } from "./fixtures";

/** The shell's short header: the most a provider is shown for a console whose header sits at the start of the file. */
const ROLE_HEADER_LEN = 0x150;
/** The deep prefix an untagged BlipToaster ROM's build label needs (its linker's RODATA, inside the PRG region). */
const CHIP_SCAN_LEN = 0x4010;

/** A backend that records the longest prefix each ROM path was read at: the proof a deep read did or did not happen. */
class CountingBackend extends MockBackend {
  readonly longest = new Map<string, number>();
  override readFilePrefix(path: string, length: number): Uint8Array | null {
    const key = this.canonicalize(path);
    this.longest.set(key, Math.max(this.longest.get(key) ?? 0, length));
    return super.readFilePrefix(path, length);
  }
  longestFor(path: string): number {
    return this.longest.get(this.canonicalize(path)) ?? 0;
  }
}

function newStore() {
  const be = new CountingBackend("/cfg");
  const reg = new RoleRegistry();
  registerCoreRoles(reg); // the mesen system role
  registerFeatureRoles(reg); // the feature roles with a protocol node
  registerBlipToasterRole(reg); // the marker whose `deriveConfig` this file is about
  registerBlipToasterAssetsRole(reg);
  registerRomProviders(reg); // BlipToaster's marker, LSDj's, mGB's
  return { be, store: new SystemsStore(be, () => {}, reg) };
}

/** The fixture ROM with its iNES mapper number rewritten (FME-7, 69, is the pair the label has to separate). */
function withMapper(rom: Uint8Array, mapper: number): Uint8Array {
  const b = rom.slice();
  b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0f) | ((mapper & 0x0f) << 4);
  b[7] = (b[7] & 0x0f) | (mapper & 0xf0);
  return b;
}

/** Write the 4-byte SIG chip tag at +14 from the marker, as the cart's own sig.s bakes it. */
function withSigChip(rom: Uint8Array, tag: string, markerAt = 0x10): Uint8Array {
  const b = rom.slice();
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) b[markerAt + 14 + i] = i < tag.length ? tag.charCodeAt(i) : 0;
  return b;
}

/** Write the NUL-terminated on-screen chip label where the cart's RODATA carries it (an untagged ROM's only source). */
function withLabel(rom: Uint8Array, label: string, at = 0x2f00): Uint8Array {
  const b = rom.slice();
  for (let i = 0; i < label.length; i++) b[at + i] = label.charCodeAt(i);
  b[at + label.length] = 0;
  return b;
}

/** The chip a built system's bliptoaster role carries. */
function chipOf(store: SystemsStore): unknown {
  return (store.view()[0].roles.find((r) => r.kind === "bliptoaster")?.config as { chip?: unknown } | undefined)?.chip;
}

test("a fresh load of an untagged S5B build derives s5b, from the deep read its role asks for", () => {
  // The fixture predates the SIG chip tag, and FME-7 (69) is BOTH the base build's mapper and the Sunsoft 5B's, so the
  // header alone cannot say: the label inside the PRG region is the only source, and the store reads that far.
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  const rom = withLabel(withMapper(blipToasterRom(), 69), "S5B");
  be.seed("/roms/bt-s5b.nes", rom);
  expect(store.addSystem("/roms/bt-s5b.nes")).toBeTruthy();
  expect(chipOf(store)).toBe("s5b");
  expect(be.longestFor("/roms/bt-s5b.nes") >= CHIP_SCAN_LEN).toBe(true);
});

test("a tagged build derives its tag, and pays no deep read", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/bt-tagged.nes", withSigChip(withMapper(blipToasterRom(), 69), "S5B"));
  expect(store.addSystem("/roms/bt-tagged.nes")).toBeTruthy();
  expect(chipOf(store)).toBe("s5b");
  expect(be.longestFor("/roms/bt-tagged.nes")).toBe(ROLE_HEADER_LEN); // the SIG block is inside the short header
});

test("a cart that is not BlipToaster is never read deeper than the short header", () => {
  // No role asks for more, so no NES cart pays the 16 KB read: the provider's header is all anything reads.
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/game.nes", nesRom());
  expect(store.addSystem("/roms/game.nes")).toBeTruthy();
  expect(store.view()[0].roles.some((r) => r.kind === "bliptoaster")).toBe(false);
  expect(be.longestFor("/roms/game.nes")).toBe(ROLE_HEADER_LEN);
});

test("a loaded project re-derives the chip from the ROM on disk, over the stored value", () => {
  // The loaded path runs the same derivation: a project stored while the chip was the ambiguous mapper's fallback (or
  // before the field existed) reads the build the ROM is today, in the same construct.
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/bt-late.nes", withLabel(withMapper(blipToasterRom(), 69), "S5B"));
  const id = store.adopt({
    core: "mesen",
    romPath: "/roms/bt-late.nes",
    roles: [
      { kind: "mesen", config: {} },
      { kind: "bliptoaster", config: { chip: "2a03" } },
      { kind: "bliptoaster-assets", config: { overrides: [] } },
    ],
  });
  expect(id).toBeTruthy();
  expect(chipOf(store)).toBe("s5b");
});

test("a stored chip survives a ROM the backend cannot read", () => {
  // The old load path returned the stored roles unchanged when the read came back empty, and it must still: a
  // derivation run on zero bytes would write the fallback (2a03) over the chip the project stored. Only a Sega platform
  // classifies from the extension alone, so that is where a missing file reaches the roles with nothing to read.
  const { store } = newStore();
  let handed: readonly { kind: string; config: Record<string, unknown> }[] = [];
  (store as unknown as { boot: (spec: unknown, entry: { roles: typeof handed }) => null }).boot = (_spec, entry) => {
    handed = entry.roles;
    return null;
  };
  const id = store.adopt({
    core: "mesen",
    romPath: "/roms/bt-gone.sms",
    roles: [
      { kind: "mesen", config: {} },
      { kind: "bliptoaster", config: { chip: "vrc7" } },
      { kind: "bliptoaster-assets", config: { overrides: [] } },
    ],
  });
  expect(id === null).toBe(true); // the intercepted boot placed nothing; the roles it was handed are what this pins
  expect(handed.find((r) => r.kind === "bliptoaster")?.config.chip).toBe("vrc7");
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/controller/sync-latency.test.ts`:

````ts
// A role's host latency is its own (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 4.5): the plugin's
// `__rp_syncLatencyMs` takes the maximum over each system's PLACED roles, so the shell names no cart and no mode. LSDj's
// sync role is the one that declares any - the two modes that lock its playback to the host's clock run a fixed distance
// behind it - and the placement rule (a role the pipeline leaves out adds nothing) is pinned end to end by
// test-native/plugin-controlplane.test.ts.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { buildAppRegistry } from "../../src/appHost";
import { LSDJ_MODE_VALUES } from "@retroplug/lsdj/enums";

const registry = buildAppRegistry();
const latencyOf = (kind: string, config: Record<string, unknown>): number | undefined =>
  registry.roleType(kind)?.hostLatencyMs?.(config);

test("the two host-clocked LSDj modes add the cart's 33 ms, and every other mode adds none", () => {
  for (const mode of LSDJ_MODE_VALUES) {
    const hostClocked = mode === "midiSync" || mode === "midiSyncArduinoboy";
    expect(latencyOf("lsdj-sync", { mode })).toBe(hostClocked ? 33 : 0);
  }
});

test("a role that adds no latency declares no hook", () => {
  // The consoles' own roles, mGB's, risa's and smsggdj's sync roles: no host-locked playback, so nothing to compensate.
  for (const kind of ["sameboy", "mesen", "mgb", "risa-sync", "sms-sync"]) {
    expect(latencyOf(kind, { mode: "midiSync" })).toBe(undefined);
  }
});
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f4apro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(f4a): the role hooks, the embedded ROM and the cart-named API

The carts' last shell-side tables and rules become the roles' own, and the two APIs that named a cart become
ids a package registers.

Role hooks (core's RoleType). `parameters(config)` serves a ROM's DAW automation lanes: mGB's table is
`packages/mgb/ts/parameters.ts` and BlipToaster's six builds are `packages/bliptoaster/ts/parameters.ts`,
with the unknown-chip 2A03 fallback beside them; the CC-spec types and `expandRomSpec` are
`core/ts/romParameters.ts`. `parameterMap.ts` keeps the slot pool, `preRoutingChannel` and
`projectParameterMap`, which asks the registry for the first role whose type serves parameters.
`deriveConfig { headerBytes(short), derive }` lets a role declare the config fields that are facts about
the ROM FILE: BlipToaster's `chip`, which the store now derives at every build - right after the providers
on a fresh load and where a loaded project already re-derived it - so the provider writes no chip and the
field has one writer. The header read (providers, then each role's deeper request) is ONE helper,
`src/rolesForRom.ts`, which the store's `defaultRoles` and a render's `resolveRenderRom` both use; the
shell's NES deep-scan branch goes with it. `hostLatencyMs(config)` is LSDj's 33 ms in the two modes that
lock its playback to the host clock, so the plugin's `__rp_syncLatencyMs` sums the systems' PLACED roles
through the registry and the shell imports neither the mode enum nor the number.

`inheritLinkGroup` finds each system's core-config role by kind === its core and gates on the console
descriptor's `linkCable`, writing the field it names: no "sameboy" literal is left in the store.
`savFromJson` leaves `ConstructCaps`, the Backend, its HostBackend pick and realBackend: lsdj's construct
hook builds its own battery from its own codec, and the three tests that counted the backend's log entry
assert the seeded sramBytes instead.

The embed (design 5.2). `PackageContributions.embeds` is `{ id, label, platform }`; mgb declares the synth,
and the generator emits both halves (the app modules' declarations and the manifests' `retroplug.embed`
entries) so the generated module refuses a manifest entry with no declaration, a declaration with no
entry, a pair split across packages, an id declared twice and a platform no console registers.
`SystemsStore.loadEmbedded(id)` takes the platform from the declaration (the two "embedded means gb"
lines go), and the start menu's rows read their labels from the registry.

The cart-named API (design 5.3). `loadEmbedded(id)` replaces `loadMgb` in the 33 files that called it, the
Node addon and its README, the CLI's SDK types and the specs; `AudioDriver.compileKitFormat<S>(id, spec)`
replaces `compileKit` / `compileDmc` and every caller, and the two cart formats' compilers take names that
say which bank they compile. No `loadMgb`, `compileKit` or `compileDmc` token is left outside the dated
records.

New tests: the parameter tables recorded from the design commit's parameterMap and asserted lane for lane
through the registry (mGB and the six builds, and the 2A03 fallback); the derived chip (a fresh untagged
S5B build is s5b, a tagged one pays no deep read, a cart that is not BlipToaster is never read deep, and
a loaded project re-derives); the embed generator's refusals and pairing; `loadEmbedded` of an id nothing
declares; and the host latency per mode. Nothing is re-recorded: the kit baseline, the render baseline and
chunks, the render-cli sizes, the goldens, the protocol digests and the device and box images are identical.
EOF
````

### Task 5: the shell's boundary, the doors gone, the tests with their code, and the docs

Design sections 4.7, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4 item 5, 8's fifth stage and 10. The four doors are deleted and every importer
names the owning package: a kit caller imports `@retroplug/lsdj/kitFormat` or `@retroplug/risa/kitFormat` (and the spec
types from `@retroplug/dsp`), a tracker caller imports the cart catalog or integration it wants, `src/tracker`'s
live-save helpers are `./tracker/liveSav`, `trackerRegistry` keeps only the generated list and its resolvers, and
`audioDriver` keeps its facade and drops its re-exports. The v2-to-v3 migration freezes the five cart-owned enum lists
beside the step, so `projectConfig` imports no sameboy, mesen or lsdj: the shell's sources name no package but core,
tracker, dsp and launchpad.

Rule 9 holds the shell to an explicit list of contract modules, each with its reason, and fails an entry no import uses;
its relative half refuses a relative import out of `packages/retroplug/src` (the design had neither the list nor the
half). A scanner test refuses a platform id or a ROM-extension literal in `src`, walking the syntax tree with its sets
read from the generated `CONSOLES` list. Tests follow their code into the packages' `ts/test`, with one shell case kept
for the song-import adapter. The docs catch up, and the design gains its as-built section, which this task lands.

This is the only task with moves, deletions and new files in the same commit: four tests move to their packages, four
files are deleted, and the boundary and scanner fixtures are new. Section 7.3's oracles are the proof it changed no
behaviour.

````ts
// The .lsdprj import PLANNER (planLsdprjImport): song injected byte-level, a missing kit assigned to a free ROM slot
// and recorded as an override linking the .lsdprj by path+ordinal, and every failure path returning null with its
// inputs untouched - the caller then writes nothing. The store-driven role path (a lsdprjKit override patched into
// the effective ROM at construct) is the shell's, test/systems/lsdj-lsdprj.test.ts: it needs the systems store.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { sameBytes } from "@retroplug/testing/bytes";
import { savFrom, decodeSav, encodeLsdprj, injectSong, listProjects, decompressSlot } from "..";
import { planLsdprjImport } from "../lsdjLsdprjImport";
import { LsdjRom, buildKitBank, ROM_SIZE, KIT_COUNT } from "../rom";
import type { LsdjAssetOverride } from "../lsdjAssetsRole";

/** A minimal 1 MiB image LsdjRom accepts (GB logo + a version title); all kit slots start free. */
function lsdjRom1M(): Uint8Array {
  const b = new Uint8Array(ROM_SIZE);
  b.set(gbRomBattery(), 0);
  const title = "LSDJ-V9.4.2";
  for (let i = 0; i < title.length; i++) b[0x134 + i] = title.charCodeAt(i);
  return b;
}

/** A GB cartridge header with the logo at 0x104 (what classifies it) and a battery (MBC1+RAM+BATTERY, 8 KB SRAM). */
function gbRomBattery(): Uint8Array {
  const b = new Uint8Array(0x8000);
  b.set(GB_LOGO, 0x104);
  b[0x147] = 0x03;
  b[0x149] = 0x02;
  return b;
}

// The Game Boy's Nintendo logo, which is what classifies a buffer as a Game Boy ROM.
const GB_LOGO = [
  0xce, 0xed, 0x66, 0x66, 0xcc, 0x0d, 0x00, 0x0b, 0x03, 0x73, 0x00, 0x83, 0x00, 0x0c, 0x00, 0x0d,
  0x00, 0x08, 0x11, 0x1f, 0x88, 0x89, 0x00, 0x0e, 0xdc, 0xcc, 0x6e, 0xe6, 0xdd, 0xdd, 0xd9, 0x99,
  0xbb, 0xbb, 0x67, 0x63, 0x6e, 0x0e, 0xec, 0xcc, 0xdd, 0xdc, 0x99, 0x9f, 0xbb, 0xb9, 0x33, 0x3e,
];

// A .lsdprj whose song uses kit index 5, carrying one custom kit bank ("DRUMS").
function lsdprjWithKit(): { file: Uint8Array; kit: Uint8Array } {
  const song = savFrom({ workingSong: { instruments: [{ type: "kit", kit1: 5, kit2: 5 }] } }).subarray(0, 0x8000);
  const kit = buildKitBank("DRUMS", [{ name: "BD", bytes: Uint8Array.of(1, 2, 3, 4) }]);
  return { file: encodeLsdprj({ name: "MYPRJ", version: 0x40, songBytes: song, kitBanks: [kit] }), kit };
}
const rawSong = (tempo: number) => savFrom({ workingSong: { settings: { tempo } } }).subarray(0, 0x8000).slice();

test("planLsdprjImport assigns a missing kit to a free slot + injects the song", () => {
  const { file } = lsdprjWithKit();
  const plan = planLsdprjImport({ file, path: "/p.lsdprj", effectiveRom: lsdjRom1M(), overrides: [], liveSram: savFrom({}) })!;
  expect(plan != null).toBeTruthy();
  expect(plan.addedKits).toBe(1);
  expect(plan.songSlot).toBe(0);
  const ov = plan.overrides[0];
  expect(ov.type).toBe("kit");
  expect(ov.path).toBe("/p.lsdprj");
  expect(ov.lsdprjKit).toBe(0);
  expect(ov.name).toBe("DRUMS");
  expect(decodeSav(plan.savBytes).projects[0]!.name).toBe("MYPRJ"); // song injected
});

test("planLsdprjImport dedupes a kit already present in the ROM (no new override)", () => {
  const { file, kit } = lsdprjWithKit();
  const rom = LsdjRom.fromBytes(lsdjRom1M());
  rom.importKitFile(3, kit); // the same kit already lives at slot 3
  const plan = planLsdprjImport({ file, path: "/p.lsdprj", effectiveRom: rom.bytes(), overrides: [], liveSram: savFrom({}) })!;
  expect(plan.addedKits).toBe(0); // reused slot 3, no new override
  expect(plan.overrides.length).toBe(0);
});

test("planLsdprjImport returns null on a malformed .lsdprj and never mutates its inputs", () => {
  const liveSram = savFrom({});
  const before = liveSram.slice();
  const overrides: LsdjAssetOverride[] = [];
  expect(planLsdprjImport({ file: new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]), path: "/bad.lsdprj", effectiveRom: lsdjRom1M(), overrides, liveSram })).toBe(null);
  expect(sameBytes(liveSram, before)).toBe(true);
  expect(overrides.length).toBe(0);
});

test("planLsdprjImport returns null when the effective ROM isn't LSDj", () => {
  const notLsdj = new Uint8Array(ROM_SIZE); // no logo / version title
  expect(planLsdprjImport({ file: lsdprjWithKit().file, path: "/p.lsdprj", effectiveRom: notLsdj, overrides: [], liveSram: savFrom({}) })).toBe(null);
});

test("planLsdprjImport returns null when the ROM is out of free kit slots", () => {
  const rom = LsdjRom.fromBytes(lsdjRom1M());
  for (let k = 0; k < KIT_COUNT; k++) rom.importKitFile(k, buildKitBank(`K${k}`, [{ name: "X", bytes: Uint8Array.of(k + 1) }])); // fill all 51
  expect(planLsdprjImport({ file: lsdprjWithKit().file, path: "/p.lsdprj", effectiveRom: rom.bytes(), overrides: [], liveSram: savFrom({}) })).toBe(null);
});

test("planLsdprjImport returns null when the SAV is out of song slots (no targetSlot)", () => {
  let full = savFrom({});
  for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) full = injectSong(full, i, `S${i}`, 1, rawSong(60))!; // fill all 32 slots
  const before = full.slice();
  expect(planLsdprjImport({ file: lsdprjWithKit().file, path: "/p.lsdprj", effectiveRom: lsdjRom1M(), overrides: [], liveSram: full })).toBe(null);
  expect(sameBytes(full, before)).toBe(true); // the full SAV is untouched
});

test("planLsdprjImport Replace (targetSlot) frees the target + injects there, leaving other songs intact", () => {
  let sav = savFrom({});
  sav = injectSong(sav, 0, "KEEP", 1, rawSong(111))!;
  sav = injectSong(sav, 5, "OLD", 2, rawSong(222))!;
  const keep = decompressSlot(sav, 0)!;
  const plan = planLsdprjImport({ file: lsdprjWithKit().file, path: "/p.lsdprj", effectiveRom: lsdjRom1M(), overrides: [], liveSram: sav, targetSlot: 5 })!;
  expect(plan.songSlot).toBe(5);
  expect(listProjects(plan.savBytes).map((p) => `${p.slot}:${p.name}`)).toEqual(["0:KEEP", "5:MYPRJ"]); // OLD replaced, KEEP intact
  expect(sameBytes(decompressSlot(plan.savBytes, 0)!, keep)).toBe(true); // KEEP byte-identical
});
````
