Create `packages/lsdj/ts/test/renderHooks.test.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's render hooks (packages/tracker/ts/trackerRender.ts) over a fake RenderHost: what the shell's render library asks
// of the cart, without a core, an engine or a WAV. The library itself is held to its own suites; what is pinned here is
// that the cart's hook answers what the pipeline needs - LSDj promotes a slot into the SRAM it boots from, probes NR52
// for the end of a song, and spells its song listings its own way.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import type { RenderFacts, RenderHost } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerRender";
import { lsdjIntegration } from "../lsdjIntegration";
import { lsdjSongCatalog } from "../lsdjSongCatalog";
import { savBytes as lsdjSav } from "../fixtures";

const LSDJ = lsdjIntegration.render!;

/** A host over one work-RAM buffer, so a write is what the next read sees: the pitch a cart's load loop verifies
 *  against. Buttons and audio time are recorded, and the CPU answers what a case sets. */
function fakeHost(over: Partial<RenderHost> & { ram?: Uint8Array } = {}): {
  host: RenderHost;
  ram: Uint8Array;
  buttons: [number, boolean][];
  audioMs: number[];
} {
  const ram = over.ram ?? new Uint8Array(0x2000);
  const buttons: [number, boolean][] = [];
  const audioMs: number[] = [];
  const host: RenderHost = {
    renderAudio: (ms) => audioMs.push(ms),
    readCpu: () => null,
    readRam: () => ram,
    writeRam: (_id, offset, bytes) => {
      if (offset < 0 || offset + bytes.length > ram.length) return false;
      ram.set(bytes, offset);
      return true;
    },
    pressButton: (_id, button, down) => buttons.push([button, down]),
    ...over,
  };
  return { host, ram, buttons, audioMs };
}

/** The request facts a hook is handed: no ROM or battery read, nothing pinned, no song, no savestate, the 10-minute
 *  cap. */
const facts = (over: Partial<RenderFacts> = {}): RenderFacts => ({
  rom: null,
  sav: null,
  state: false,
  song: false,
  durationMs: undefined,
  maxDurationMs: 600000,
  ...over,
});

test("LSDj lists the battery's songs and seeds a chosen one as the working song", () => {
  const sav = lsdjSav("lsdj499");
  const songs = LSDJ.listSongs(sav);
  expect(songs.length > 0).toBe(true);
  expect(songs.map((s) => ({ index: s.index, name: s.name }))).toEqual(lsdjSongCatalog.list(sav));
  const pick = songs[0];
  const seed = LSDJ.seedSong!(sav, pick.index);
  expect(seed !== null).toBe(true);
  // The seed is the image a fresh system boots from, and the slot the caller picked is what it plays.
  expect(lsdjSongCatalog.workingName(seed!)).toBe(pick.name);
  expect(lsdjSongCatalog.list(seed!)).toEqual(songs.map((s) => ({ index: s.index, name: s.name })));
  // A slot the battery does not hold seeds nothing, rather than a silent cart.
  expect(songs.some((s) => s.index === 31)).toBe(false);
  expect(LSDJ.seedSong!(sav, 31)).toBe(null);
});

test("LSDj's end-of-song probe is NR52's sound-enable bit", () => {
  const rom = new Uint8Array(0x150); // the probe is the ROM's cart's, so what it is handed is the ROM
  const on = fakeHost({ readCpu: () => 0x80 });
  const off = fakeHost({ readCpu: () => 0x00 });
  const unreadable = fakeHost({ readCpu: () => null });
  expect(LSDJ.playingProbe!(on.host, 1, rom, facts(), () => {})!()).toBe(true);
  expect(LSDJ.playingProbe!(off.host, 1, rom, facts(), () => {})!()).toBe(false);
  // A core whose register cannot be read says nothing, which reads as stopped: the cap bounds the render.
  expect(LSDJ.playingProbe!(unreadable.host, 1, rom, facts(), () => {})!()).toBe(false);
});

test("LSDj's song listing keeps its own spelling", () => {
  // The selection errors and --list-songs print the cart's own line, which is why these are data on the hooks rather
  // than one neutral form: LSDj says "(no named projects)".
  expect(LSDJ.songList!.listing!([])).toBe("(no named projects)");
  expect(LSDJ.songList!.empty).toBe("(no named projects \u2014 only the working song)"); // the CLI's line, byte for byte
  const lsdj = LSDJ.listSongs(lsdjSav("lsdj499"));
  expect(LSDJ.songList!.listing!(lsdj)).toBe(lsdj.map((s) => `${s.index}: ${s.name}`).join(", "));
});
````

Create `packages/lsdj/ts/test/songImport.test.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's song importer (lsdjSongImport.ts), the batch behind the Songs menu's Add and a drag-and-drop: fold one or more
// .lsdsng/.lsdprj into the live SAV in ONE readSram -> edit -> write -> loadSram cycle, with a .lsdprj's kits recorded as
// lsdj-assets overrides. Driven over a fake SongImportHost - the shell adapts its backend and stores to that contract -
// so every write, reload and role edit the import makes is recorded here, and no store is needed.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { sameBytes } from "@retroplug/testing/bytes";
import type { ConstructCaps } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import type { SongImportHost, SongImportTarget } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerSongImport";
import { LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT } from "../lsdjSongImport";
import { savFrom, encodeLsdsngRaw, encodeLsdprj, decompressSlot, listProjects } from "..";
import { applyOverridesToRom, readOverrides, type LsdjAssetOverride } from "../lsdjAssetsRole";
import { LsdjRom, buildKitBank, ROM_SIZE } from "../rom";

/** A 1 MiB LSDj image: a GB battery header and a version title, all kit slots free. */
function lsdjRom1M(title = "LSDJ-V9.1.C"): Uint8Array {
  const b = new Uint8Array(ROM_SIZE);
  b.set([0xce, 0xed, 0x66, 0x66], 0x104); // the Game Boy's logo; the importer only reads bytes here
  for (let i = 0; i < title.length; i++) b[0x134 + i] = title.charCodeAt(i);
  return b;
}

const song = (tempo: number, sentinel: number): Uint8Array => {
  const raw = savFrom({ workingSong: { settings: { tempo } } }).subarray(0, 0x8000).slice();
  raw[0x1730] = sentinel;
  return raw;
};
const rawSong = (tempo: number) => savFrom({ workingSong: { settings: { tempo } } }).subarray(0, 0x8000).slice();

/** The host an import is handed: an in-memory disk, one live battery, one written .sav, and the role edits and reloads
 *  it made. `writeOk` is the disk's answer, so a failed write is a case. */
class FakeHost implements SongImportHost {
  readonly files = new Map<string, Uint8Array>();
  readonly writes: { path: string; bytes: Uint8Array }[] = [];
  readonly loads: { id: number; path: string }[] = [];
  readonly roleEdits: { id: number; kind: string; config: Record<string, unknown> }[] = [];
  sram: Uint8Array;
  writeOk = true;
  private readonly roles = new Map<string, Record<string, unknown>>();
  readonly caps: ConstructCaps = {
    fileExists: (path) => this.files.has(path),
    readFile: (path) => this.files.get(path) ?? null,
    pngDecode: () => null,
  };

  constructor(rom: Uint8Array, sram: Uint8Array) {
    this.files.set("/roms/song.gb", rom);
    this.sram = sram;
  }

  writeFileAtomic(path: string, bytes: Uint8Array): boolean {
    if (!this.writeOk) return false;
    this.files.set(path, bytes);
    this.writes.push({ path, bytes });
    return true;
  }

  readSram(): Uint8Array | null {
    return this.sram;
  }

  loadSram(id: number, path: string): boolean {
    this.loads.push({ id, path });
    return true;
  }

  setRoleConfig(_id: number, kind: string, config: Record<string, unknown>): boolean {
    this.roles.set(kind, config);
    this.roleEdits.push({ id: _id, kind, config });
    return true;
  }

  savPathOf(): string | null {
    return "/roms/song.sav";
  }
}

function target(): SongImportTarget {
  return {
    id: 1,
    romPath: "/roms/song.gb",
    roles: [{ kind: "lsdj-assets", config: { overrides: [] } }],
  };
}

test("a .lsdsng + a .lsdprj land in ONE reload; kits ride overrides", () => {
  const host = new FakeHost(lsdjRom1M(), savFrom({})); // blank live battery
  const aSong = song(100, 0x11); // a plain .lsdsng: stays byte-exact
  // a .lsdprj whose song references kit 5, so its bundled bank imports as an override and the refs remap
  const bSong = savFrom({ workingSong: { settings: { tempo: 140 }, instruments: [{ type: "kit", kit1: 5, kit2: 5 }] } }).subarray(0, 0x8000);
  host.files.set("/s/a.lsdsng", encodeLsdsngRaw("AAA", 1, aSong));
  host.files.set(
    "/s/b.lsdprj",
    encodeLsdprj({ name: "BBB", version: 2, songBytes: bSong, kitBanks: [buildKitBank("DRUMS", [{ name: "BD", bytes: Uint8Array.of(1, 2, 3, 4) }])] }),
  );

  expect(LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT.import(host, target(), ["/s/a.lsdsng", "/s/b.lsdprj"])).toBeTruthy();

  // Exactly one rebuild for the whole batch, from the one file written.
  expect(host.loads).toEqual([{ id: 1, path: "/roms/song.sav" }]);
  expect(host.writes.length).toBe(1);
  const sav = host.writes[0].bytes;
  expect(listProjects(sav).map((p) => p.slot)).toEqual([0, 1]); // both songs present
  expect(sameBytes(decompressSlot(sav, 0)!, aSong)).toBe(true); // .lsdsng byte-exact in slot 0
  expect(sameBytes(sav.subarray(0, 0x8000), decompressSlot(sav, 1)!)).toBe(true); // working memory = the LAST song

  // The .lsdprj's kit was recorded as an lsdj-assets override (linking the file by path), and the ROM an override
  // folds onto carries it.
  expect(host.roleEdits.length).toBe(1);
  expect(host.roleEdits[0].kind).toBe("lsdj-assets");
  const ov = readOverrides(host.roleEdits[0].config);
  expect(ov.some((o) => o.type === "kit" && o.path === "/s/b.lsdprj" && o.lsdprjKit === 0)).toBeTruthy();
  expect(LsdjRom.fromBytes(applyOverridesToRom(lsdjRom1M(), ov as LsdjAssetOverride[], host.caps)).kit(0).name()).toBe("DRUMS");
});

test("an empty or all-bad list writes nothing and reloads nothing", () => {
  const host = new FakeHost(lsdjRom1M(), savFrom({}));
  expect(LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT.import(host, target(), [])).toBe(false);
  expect(LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT.import(host, target(), ["/nope.lsdsng"])).toBe(false); // unreadable
  expect(host.loads.length).toBe(0);
  expect(host.writes.length).toBe(0);
});

test("a .lsdprj whose base ROM cannot be read is skipped (nothing written, no reload, no clobber)", () => {
  const host = new FakeHost(lsdjRom1M(), savFrom({}));
  host.files.delete("/roms/song.gb"); // the ROM becomes unreadable: .lsdprj needs it to patch its kits
  host.files.set("/s/b.lsdprj", encodeLsdprj({ name: "BBB", version: 2, songBytes: rawSong(120), kitBanks: [] }));
  expect(LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT.import(host, target(), ["/s/b.lsdprj"])).toBe(false);
  expect(host.loads.length).toBe(0);
  expect(host.writes.length).toBe(0);
});

test("the valid song lands and a malformed one in the same batch is skipped, in one reload", () => {
  const host = new FakeHost(lsdjRom1M(), savFrom({}));
  const good = rawSong(90);
  host.files.set("/s/good.lsdsng", encodeLsdsngRaw("GOOD", 1, good));
  host.files.set("/s/bad.lsdprj", new Uint8Array([9, 9, 9])); // malformed
  expect(LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT.import(host, target(), ["/s/good.lsdsng", "/s/bad.lsdprj"])).toBe(true);
  expect(host.loads.length).toBe(1);
  const sav = host.writes[0].bytes;
  expect(listProjects(sav).map((p) => p.name)).toEqual(["GOOD"]); // only the good song; the bad file corrupted nothing
  expect(sameBytes(decompressSlot(sav, 0)!, good)).toBe(true);
});

test("a failed atomic write aborts cleanly: false, no reload, nothing on disk", () => {
  const host = new FakeHost(lsdjRom1M(), savFrom({}));
  host.files.set("/s/good.lsdsng", encodeLsdsngRaw("GOOD", 1, rawSong(90)));
  host.writeOk = false; // the disk write fails
  expect(LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT.import(host, target(), ["/s/good.lsdsng"])).toBe(false);
  expect(host.loads.length).toBe(0); // no cold-boot from a failed write
  expect(host.files.has("/roms/song.sav")).toBe(false); // nothing was written
  expect(host.roleEdits.length).toBe(0); // the lsdj-assets role was never touched
});

test("a system that went away between the target and the write imports nothing", () => {
  // The host answers null for a missing system, and the import must not write its battery to an empty path.
  const host = new FakeHost(lsdjRom1M(), savFrom({}));
  host.files.set("/s/good.lsdsng", encodeLsdsngRaw("GOOD", 1, rawSong(90)));
  host.savPathOf = () => null;
  expect(LSDJ_SONG_IMPORT.import(host, target(), ["/s/good.lsdsng"])).toBe(false);
  expect(host.writes.length).toBe(0);
  expect(host.loads.length).toBe(0);
});
````

````ts
// The working-song signature LSDj's playback hook answers with (lsdjPlayback.ts, workingSongSignature): a poll compares
// it to notice a song edited ON THE CART, so it must move for every edit that changes row timing and for nothing else -
// a false positive decodes the whole battery again, several times a minute, while somebody works. The store's poll and
// its publish are the shell's (test/controller/songRefresh.test.ts).
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { workingSongSignature } from "../playback/fromSav";
import * as R from "../codec/regions";

/** A blank song bank, big enough to be a plausible battery. */
function sav(): Uint8Array {
  return new Uint8Array(R.kSongByteCount + 0x200);
}

test("the signature moves when a song row's chain changes", () => {
  const a = sav();
  const before = workingSongSignature(a);
  a[R.kModernRegions.chainAssignments + 4 * R.kChannelCount] = 3; // row 4, pu1 -> chain 3
  expect(workingSongSignature(a) !== before).toBe(true);
});

test("the signature moves when a chain gains or loses a phrase", () => {
  const a = sav();
  const before = workingSongSignature(a);
  a[R.kModernRegions.chainPhrases + 3 * R.kChainLength + 1] = 9; // chain 3, slot 1 -> phrase 9
  expect(workingSongSignature(a) !== before).toBe(true);
  const withPhrase = workingSongSignature(a);
  a[R.kModernRegions.chainAllocations] ^= 0x08; // chain 3 allocated/not
  expect(workingSongSignature(a) !== withPhrase).toBe(true);
});

test("the signature moves when groove 0 changes, because that sets the row duration", () => {
  const a = sav();
  const before = workingSongSignature(a);
  a[R.kModernRegions.grooves + 1] = 3;
  expect(workingSongSignature(a) !== before).toBe(true);
});

test("the signature IGNORES edits that cannot change row timing", () => {
  // Renaming a file, tweaking an instrument, writing a phrase note: all real edits, none of which move a
  // single row's duration. Re-pushing for these would decode the whole sav for nothing, several times a
  // minute, while somebody works.
  const a = sav();
  const before = workingSongSignature(a);
  a[R.kModernRegions.instrumentNames + 2] = 0x41;
  a[R.kModernRegions.instrumentParams + 5] = 0x7f;
  a[R.kModernRegions.phraseNotes + 40] = 0x50;
  a[R.kModernRegions.tempo] = 150;
  expect(workingSongSignature(a)).toBe(before);
});

test("an unreadable battery is inert rather than a change", () => {
  // Null / too short / not yet published. Returning a constant means the poll simply never fires, which
  // is what "no song feedback" should look like everywhere else in this feature.
  expect(workingSongSignature(null)).toBe(0);
  expect(workingSongSignature(new Uint8Array(16))).toBe(0);
  expect(workingSongSignature(undefined)).toBe(0);
});
````

Create `packages/risa/ts/test/renderHooks.test.ts`:

````ts
// risa's render hooks over a fake RenderHost: what the shell's render library asks of the cart, without a core, an
// engine or a WAV. risa presses SELECT+START with two discarded prep chunks, reads its own sequencer flag for the end of
// a song, and says what it cannot do when the ROM predates a runtime layout.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import type { RenderFacts, RenderHost, RenderPlaySink } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerRender";
import { risaIntegration } from "../risaIntegration";
import { risaSongCatalog } from "../risaSongCatalog";
import { savBytes as risaSav } from "../fixtures";
import { loadSongToWorkingInSav } from "../risaSongOps";

const RISA = risaIntegration.render!;

/** A host over one work-RAM buffer, so a write is what the next read sees. Buttons and audio time are recorded, and
 *  the CPU answers what a case sets. */
function fakeHost(over: Partial<RenderHost> & { ram?: Uint8Array } = {}): {
  host: RenderHost;
  ram: Uint8Array;
  buttons: [number, boolean][];
  audioMs: number[];
} {
  const ram = over.ram ?? new Uint8Array(0x2000);
  const buttons: [number, boolean][] = [];
  const audioMs: number[] = [];
  const host: RenderHost = {
    renderAudio: (ms) => audioMs.push(ms),
    readCpu: () => null,
    readRam: () => ram,
    writeRam: (_id, offset, bytes) => {
      if (offset < 0 || offset + bytes.length > ram.length) return false;
      ram.set(bytes, offset);
      return true;
    },
    pressButton: (_id, button, down) => buttons.push([button, down]),
    ...over,
  };
  return { host, ram, buttons, audioMs };
}

/** A sink that answers one silent chunk per pull and counts the pulls: what a play gesture captures through. */
function fakeSink(): { sink: RenderPlaySink; pulls: number[] } {
  const pulls: number[] = [];
  return {
    sink: {
      renderChunk: (ms) => {
        pulls.push(ms);
        return [new Float32Array(Math.round((ms * 44100) / 1000) * 2)];
      },
    },
    pulls,
  };
}

/** The request facts a hook is handed: no ROM or battery read, nothing pinned, no song, no savestate, the 10-minute
 *  cap. */
const facts = (over: Partial<RenderFacts> = {}): RenderFacts => ({
  rom: null,
  sav: null,
  state: false,
  song: false,
  durationMs: undefined,
  maxDurationMs: 600000,
  ...over,
});

test("risa lists and seeds its catalog, and begins a song on SELECT+START", () => {
  const sav = risaSav("v2_blumarbl");
  const songs = RISA.listSongs(sav);
  expect(songs.length > 0).toBe(true);
  expect(songs.map((s) => ({ index: s.index, name: s.name }))).toEqual(risaSongCatalog.list(sav));
  const seed = RISA.seedSong!(sav, songs[0].index);
  expect(seed).toEqual(loadSongToWorkingInSav(sav, songs[0].index));
  // A slot the catalog does not hold seeds nothing.
  expect(RISA.seedSong!(sav, 31)).toBe(null);
  // ... and says why, in its own words: a legacy-layout catalog lists slots this build cannot promote.
  expect(RISA.seedRefusal!(31)).toBe("render: could not load risa song 31 (needs a current-layout catalog)");

  // The gesture: two discarded prep chunks, then the SELECT+START chunk captured as the lead-in.
  const { host, buttons } = fakeHost();
  const { sink, pulls } = fakeSink();
  const leadIn = RISA.pressPlay!(host, 1, new Uint8Array(0), sink);
  expect(pulls.length).toBe(3);
  expect(leadIn.length).toBe(1);
  expect(leadIn[0][0].length / 2).toBe(pulls[2] * 44.1); // interleaved stereo: frames are halves
  // Start down, Start up (the nudge), then SELECT and START together, then both released.
  expect(buttons).toEqual([
    [7, true],
    [7, false],
    [6, true],
    [7, true],
    [7, false],
    [6, false],
  ]);
});

test("risa's probe reads its sequencer flag, and says why it cannot when the build has no layout", () => {
  const warnings: string[] = [];
  const rom = new Uint8Array(0x4000);
  rom.set([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a], 0); // iNES
  expect(RISA.playingProbe!(fakeHost().host, 1, rom, facts(), (m) => warnings.push(m))).toBe(null);
  expect(warnings.length).toBe(1);
  expect(warnings[0].includes("no runtime layout")).toBe(true);
  // It names the length the render falls back to, so the log says what the WAV will be.
  expect(warnings[0].includes("rendering a fixed 600000ms")).toBe(true);
});

test("risa's song listing keeps its own spelling", () => {
  expect(RISA.songList!.listing!([])).toBe("(no saved songs)");
  expect(RISA.songList!.empty).toBe("(no saved songs in the catalog)");
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/bliptoaster/rolesForRom.test.ts`:

````ts
// The shell's half of BlipToaster's ROM detection (packages/bliptoaster/ts/test/romDetect.test.ts holds the byte-level
// half): the PROVIDER only marks the cart and writes no chip, so which build it is belongs to the role's `deriveConfig`,
// and the shell's rolesForRom is what asks it, with as deep a read as the role needs. The reader here serves whatever
// length is asked for, so the label case's read past the short header lands.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { buildAppRegistry } from "../../src/appHost";
import { rolesForRom } from "../../src/rolesForRom";
import { blipToasterRom, nesRom } from "../systems/fixtures";

/** The fixture ROM with its iNES mapper number rewritten (FME-7, 69, is the pair a label has to separate). */
function withMapper(rom: Uint8Array, mapper: number): Uint8Array {
  const b = rom.slice();
  b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0f) | ((mapper & 0x0f) << 4);
  b[7] = (b[7] & 0x0f) | (mapper & 0xf0);
  return b;
}

/** Write the NUL-terminated on-screen chip label where the cart's RODATA carries it. */
function withLabel(rom: Uint8Array, label: string, at = 0x2f00): Uint8Array {
  const b = rom.slice();
  for (let i = 0; i < label.length; i++) b[at + i] = label.charCodeAt(i);
  b[at + label.length] = 0;
  return b;
}

test("the ROM's roles carry the build on the `bliptoaster` role, which derives it", () => {
  // The PROVIDER only marks the cart (it writes no chip, so there is one writer); which build it is belongs to the role's
  // `deriveConfig`, and the shell's rolesForRom is what asks it, with as deep a read as it needs (the label case reads
  // past the short header, which is why the reader here serves whatever length is asked for).
  const reg = buildAppRegistry();
  const chipOf = (rom: Uint8Array): string | undefined => {
    const roles = rolesForRom(
      reg,
      { readFilePrefix: (_path, length) => rom.subarray(0, length) },
      { core: "mesen", platform: "nes", romPath: "/roms/synth.nes" },
    );
    return (roles.find((r) => r.kind === "bliptoaster")?.config as { chip?: string } | undefined)?.chip;
  };
  expect(chipOf(withLabel(withMapper(blipToasterRom(), 69), "S5B"))).toBe("s5b");
  expect(chipOf(withMapper(blipToasterRom(), 85))).toBe("vrc7");
  expect(chipOf(withMapper(blipToasterRom(), 24))).toBe("vrc6");
  expect(chipOf(blipToasterRom())).toBe("2a03");
  // a non-BlipToaster NES ROM gets no such role at all
  const roles = rolesForRom(
    reg,
    { readFilePrefix: (_path, length) => nesRom().subarray(0, length) },
    { core: "mesen", platform: "nes", romPath: "/roms/game.nes" },
  );
  expect(roles.some((r) => r.kind === "bliptoaster")).toBe(false);
});

// The marker is a wire contract with the ROM repo's rom/src/core/sig.s, and it has moved twice ("EVERMIDI"
// -> "evermidi-n8" -> "bliptoaster"). Pin the exact bytes here so a drift is a failing test rather than a
// ROM that silently loses its Kits/Fonts/Themes menu. The pre-rename spellings must NOT be detected.
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The frozen v2 lists, and the test that reads them**

`projectConfig.ts` freezes the five index-ordered v2 lists beside the v2-to-v3 step, exported as `V3_ROLE_ENUMS`, so
the sameboy, mesen and lsdj enum imports leave it and the shell names no console or cart package at all.
`migrate-v3-frozen.test.ts` iterates THOSE lists, not a copy and not the packages' current ones: every frozen value
must still be one the owning package accepts, so a rename fails and names the value it lost, and every ordinal through
`parseConfig` must map to the value the v2 writer had at that index, so an append or a reorder passes. The first
version iterated the current lists and could not fail on a reorder, which the whole-prototype review found.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/project/migrate-v3-frozen.test.ts`:

````ts
// The v2 to v3 step rewrites integer enum values to their string spellings, and it must go on doing that from the lists
// the v2 writers had, not from today's packages: a rename in a cart's enum would otherwise migrate an old project to a
// DEFAULT. This asserts every frozen value is still one the owning package's schema accepts, and runs the step for
// every ordinal so the file's own integer still means the value its writer meant. An append or a reorder in a package
// passes (the frozen ordinals have not moved); a rename fails here, which is the case the freeze exists to catch.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { parseConfig, V3_ROLE_ENUMS } from "../../src/projectConfig";
import { MODEL_VALUES, HIGHPASS_VALUES } from "@retroplug/sameboy/enums";
import { REGION_VALUES, CHANNEL_EXPORT_VALUES } from "@retroplug/mesen/enums";
import { LSDJ_MODE_VALUES } from "@retroplug/lsdj/enums";

/** A v2 file carrying one role, so the step's role-config half runs for its ordinal fields. */
function v2(platform: string, core: string, kind: string, config: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  return JSON.stringify({
    schemaVersion: "2",
    settings: {},
    systems: [{ platform, core, romPath: "/rom", roles: [{ kind, config }] }],
  });
}

const CASES: { platform: string; core: string; kind: string; field: string; current: readonly string[] }[] = [
  { platform: "gb", core: "sameboy", kind: "sameboy", field: "model", current: MODEL_VALUES },
  { platform: "gb", core: "sameboy", kind: "sameboy", field: "highpass", current: HIGHPASS_VALUES },
  { platform: "nes", core: "mesen", kind: "mesen", field: "region", current: REGION_VALUES },
  { platform: "nes", core: "mesen", kind: "mesen", field: "channelExportMode", current: CHANNEL_EXPORT_VALUES },
  { platform: "gb", core: "sameboy", kind: "lsdj-sync", field: "mode", current: LSDJ_MODE_VALUES },
];

for (const { platform, core, kind, field, current } of CASES) {
  // The frozen values the package no longer accepts: a renamed member leaves its old spelling here, and the step would
  // write a value the schema does not know.
  test(`every frozen ${kind}.${field} value is still one the package accepts`, () => {
    const frozen = V3_ROLE_ENUMS[kind][field];
    expect(frozen.filter((value) => !current.includes(value))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test(`v2→v3 maps every ${kind}.${field} ordinal to the value the v2 writer had`, () => {
    for (const [index, value] of V3_ROLE_ENUMS[kind][field].entries()) {
      const cfg = parseConfig(v2(platform, core, kind, { [field]: index }));
      const role = cfg.systems[0]?.roles?.find((r) => r.kind === kind);
      expect(role?.config[field], `${kind}.${field} ordinal ${index}`).toBe(value);
    }
  });
}
````

contract import and an in-`src` relative import accepted beside a generated cart import) and `shell-source-relative`
(two refusals).

- [ ] **Step 6: The literal scanner, and its fixtures**

`run-scan.mjs` walks every file of `packages/retroplug/src` (not `src/generated/`) with `ts.createSourceFile` from the
pinned `typescript-5`, collecting every `StringLiteral`, every `NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral` and every template's
head and span text; comments are trivia, and a regular expression or a template's `${...}` cannot move the walk's
place. It takes `--root`, `--platforms` and `--extensions` and keeps no copy of either set (without them it exits 2),
and a hit is a platform id, a descriptor extension, or `*` plus an extension. `no-cart-literals.test.ts` imports
`CONSOLES` from `src/generated/consoles.ts` and passes the descriptors' ids and extensions, so a console a product
registers later is guarded with no edit. The fixture spells a literal in each place a program holds one (a bare id, an
extension, a glob, a template span, a literal after a substitution template, one after a quote-holding regex) and a
comment and a generated module the walk must skip.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/source-literals/run-scan.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Walks the app shell's sources for a platform or ROM-extension literal, for
// test/source-literals/no-cart-literals.test.ts (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 7.2). The walk is over
// TypeScript's own syntax tree (the pinned `typescript-5` the boundary check loads), so a comment is trivia and every
// string a program can hold is read: a quoted string, a template with no substitution, and each span of a template
// that has one. A regular expression or a template with a substitution cannot move the walk's place, which a bare
// token scan loses at the `${...}` that closes a span.
//
//   node test/source-literals/run-scan.mjs --platforms <id,...> --extensions <.ext,...> [--root <dir>]
//
// The guarded sets are the console registry's, not this file's: the test imports the generated CONSOLES list and passes
// its platform ids and extensions, so a console a product registers later is guarded without an edit here. A value is a
// hit when it is a platform id, one of the descriptors' extensions, or the `*.gb`-style glob a file filter would take.
// Prints one JSON line: { literals: [{ file, value }] }, src/generated/ not scanned.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const ts = createRequire(import.meta.url)("typescript-5");
const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = resolve(HERE, "../../../..");

/** The value of `--name`, or undefined. */
function option(name) {
  const at = process.argv.indexOf(name);
  return at === -1 ? undefined : process.argv[at + 1];
}

const platforms = option("--platforms");
const extensions = option("--extensions");
if (!platforms || !extensions) {
  console.error(
    "run-scan: --platforms and --extensions are required: they are the console registry's ids and extensions, which " +
      "the caller reads from the generated CONSOLES list rather than this file keeping a second copy of them.",
  );
  process.exit(2);
}
const root = resolve(option("--root") ?? REPO);
const list = (csv) => csv.split(",").filter((entry) => entry !== "");
const PLATFORMS = new Set(list(platforms));
const EXTENSIONS = new Set(list(extensions));
const isExtensionPattern = (value) => value.startsWith("*.") && EXTENSIONS.has(value.slice(1));
const isHit = (value) => PLATFORMS.has(value) || EXTENSIONS.has(value) || isExtensionPattern(value);

/** Every .ts/.tsx file under `dir`, in a stable order, without the generated registries. */
function walk(dir, out = []) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => (a.name < b.name ? -1 : 1))) {
    const path = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      if (entry.name !== "generated") walk(path, out);
    } else if (/\.(ts|tsx)$/.test(entry.name)) out.push(path);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The text of every string the tree holds, in source order: the literals a program can compare, not the trivia around
 *  them. A template's head and each span's literal are nodes of their own, which the tree does not visit as children of
 *  the expression that holds them. */
function stringsOf(file, text) {
  const source = ts.createSourceFile(
    file,
    text,
    ts.ScriptTarget.Latest,
    true,
    file.endsWith(".tsx") ? ts.ScriptKind.TSX : ts.ScriptKind.TS,
  );
  const found = [];
  const visit = (node) => {
    if (ts.isTemplateExpression(node)) {
      found.push(node.head.text);
      for (const span of node.templateSpans) {
        found.push(span.literal.text);
        visit(span.expression);
      }
      return;
    }
    if (ts.isStringLiteral(node) || ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral(node)) found.push(node.text);
    ts.forEachChild(node, visit);
  };
  visit(source);
  return found;
}

const literals = [];
for (const file of walk(join(root, "packages/retroplug/src"))) {
  for (const value of stringsOf(file, readFileSync(file, "utf8"))) {
    if (isHit(value)) literals.push({ file: relative(root, file).split("\\").join("/"), value });
  }
}
console.log(JSON.stringify({ literals }));
````

````ts
// The shell's sources hold no platform or ROM-extension LITERAL (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 7.2):
// after F4a a console is known by its descriptor (src/consoles.ts reads the generated registries), a ROM is classified
// by its content through one, and a save path or a file-filter pattern takes its extensions from the same descriptor. A
// literal that spelled "gb" or ".nes" again would be a second copy of a console's knowledge in the shell - exactly what
// the package split removes - so the rule is a test rather than a review note.
//
// The scan walks TypeScript's syntax tree (the pinned `typescript-5` the boundary check loads), not a regular
// expression and not a bare token scan: a comment that says "gb" is trivia, a template's head and each of its spans are
// read, and a template's `${...}` or a regular expression cannot move the walk's place. The guarded ids and extensions
// are the registry's, not a list here: the generated CONSOLES list is read below, so a console a product adds later is
// guarded without an edit to this test. It catches an accident, not a determined author: a computed platform
// (["g", "b"].join("")) is invisible to it, as the boundary check says of itself.
//
// The scanner is Node's, so the test spawns test/source-literals/run-scan.mjs, as the boundary test spawns its runner.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { CONSOLES } from "../../src/generated/consoles";

/** The console registry's platform ids and ROM extensions: the descriptors' own, so nothing here is a second copy. */
const PLATFORM_IDS = [
  ...new Set(CONSOLES.flatMap((console) => console.platforms.map((platform) => platform.id))),
].sort();
const ROM_EXTENSIONS = [
  ...new Set(CONSOLES.flatMap((console) => console.platforms.flatMap((platform) => platform.extensions))),
].sort();

interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

/** The scan's findings over a tree: `--root` names a fixture that spells literals, no argument the real tree. */
async function scan(root?: string): Promise<{ file: string; value: string }[]> {
  const args = [
    tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node",
    "test/source-literals/run-scan.mjs",
    "--platforms",
    PLATFORM_IDS.join(","),
    "--extensions",
    ROM_EXTENSIONS.join(","),
    ...(root ? ["--root", root] : []),
  ];
  const child = tjs.spawn(args, { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.term_signal || status.exit_status !== 0) throw new Error(`the literal scan failed: ${err || out}`);
  return (JSON.parse(out) as { literals: { file: string; value: string }[] }).literals;
}

test("the shell's sources spell no platform and no ROM extension", async () => {
  console.log(`# the registry's ids: ${PLATFORM_IDS.join(", ")}; its extensions: ${ROM_EXTENSIONS.join(", ")}`);
  const literals = await scan();
  console.log(`# platform/extension literals: ${JSON.stringify(literals)}`);
  expect(literals).toEqual([]);
});

test("the walk finds a literal after a template and a regex, in a span, not a comment", async () => {
  // The fixture spells platform ids and ROM extensions as string literals in every place a program holds one: a quoted
  // string, a template span, and literals after a substitution template and a quote-holding regular expression. It says
  // "gb" and "sms" in a comment, and names every platform in src/generated: neither the comment nor the generated
  // registry is the shell's to change.
  const literals = await scan("test/source-literals/fixtures/literals");
  expect(literals).toEqual([
    { file: "packages/retroplug/src/render.ts", value: "gb" },
    { file: "packages/retroplug/src/render.ts", value: ".nes" },
    { file: "packages/retroplug/src/render.ts", value: "*.gba" },
    { file: "packages/retroplug/src/render.ts", value: "gb" },
    { file: "packages/retroplug/src/render.ts", value: ".gbc" },
    { file: "packages/retroplug/src/render.ts", value: ".sms" },
  ]);
});
````

````ts
// A comment naming "gb", "sms" and ".nes" is not a literal: the walk reads the tree, and a comment is trivia.
export function classify(name: string): string {
  const platform = "gb";
  const extension = ".nes";
  const pattern = "*.gba";
  // A template with a substitution still holds literals: its head and each span's text are read.
  const middle = `${name}gb${name}`;
  // A literal AFTER a substitution template, where a bare token scan that never re-scanned a span has lost its place.
  const afterTemplate = ".gbc";
  // A regular expression holding a quote does not open a string.
  const quoted = /["']/;
  // A literal after that regular expression.
  const afterRegex = ".sms";
  return [platform, extension, pattern, middle, afterTemplate, afterRegex, quoted.source].join("/");
}
````

````diff
-### 7.2 The grep test
-
-**A test that `src/` holds no platform literal outside comments is reliable and is added in stage 5.** Today
-`"gb" | "nes" | "gba" | "sms" | "gg"` as a string literal outside a comment occurs 46 times in 6 files (`render/render.ts` 26,
-`platform.ts` 10, `systemsStore.ts` 6, `graph/buildGraph.ts` 2, `render/types.ts` 1, `projectConfig.ts` 1), and the extension
-literals `.gb` ... `.gg` in `savPaths.ts:77`, `render.ts:68 to 73` and `platform.ts:111, 112` (and as glob patterns in
-`fileSelection.ts:20, 21`, which the test's literal scan also catches as `*.gb`). After the moves none remains, and the
-test reads tokens with TypeScript's scanner (`ts.createScanner`, from the same pinned `typescript` the boundary check
-loads; `preProcessFile` reads imports only) rather than a regular expression over text, so a literal in a template string or a comment is told apart. What it cannot see is a computed
-platform (`["g", "b"].join("")`) or a platform id spelled in a string that is not a bare literal: it guards accident, not a
-determined author, as the boundary check says of itself. Allowed: `src/generated/` and the registry's own error messages
-(which interpolate ids rather than spell them).

+`V3_ROLE_ENUMS`, so a test can read the frozen lists and not a copy), the sameboy, mesen and lsdj imports go, and the shell
+imports no sameboy, mesen or lsdj module at all. `test/project/migrate-v3-frozen.test.ts` (10 cases) iterates the FROZEN
+lists, not the packages' current ones: every frozen value must still be one the owning package accepts, so a rename in a

+### 7.2 The literal scanner (the "grep test")
+
+**A test that `src/` holds no platform or ROM-extension literal outside comments is reliable and is stage 5's; as built it
+walks the syntax tree, with its sets read from the registry.** `test/source-literals/no-cart-literals.test.ts` runs
+`run-scan.mjs`, which parses every file of `packages/retroplug/src` (not `src/generated/`) with `ts.createSourceFile` from
+the same pinned `typescript-5` the boundary check loads (a `.tsx` file as TSX) and collects every `StringLiteral`, every
+`NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral` and every template's head and span text. Comments are trivia, and neither a regular
+expression literal nor a template's `${...}` can move the walk's place. **The first version drove `ts.createScanner` and
+lost its place after a template or a regular expression, finding 46 of the 86 literals the base held** (the Critical finding
+of the whole-prototype review); the design's own sentence, "reads tokens with TypeScript's scanner", was the mistake, and a
+bare scanner does not track template nesting or regex-versus-division. The sets are not in the script: the test imports
+`CONSOLES` from `src/generated/consoles.ts` and passes every descriptor's platform ids (`gb, gba, gg, nes, sms`) and
+extensions (`.gb, .gba, .gbc, .gg, .nes, .sms`) as `--platforms` and `--extensions`; the script keeps no copy and exits 2
+without them. A hit is a platform id, a descriptor extension, or `*` plus an extension (the `*.gb` glob). A console a
+product registers later is therefore guarded with no edit to the test, and `.gbc` is guarded (a hard-coded list omitted it).
+What it cannot see is a computed platform (`["g", "b"].join("")`) or a platform id spelled in a string that is not a bare
+literal: it guards accident, not a determined author, as the boundary check says of itself. **RED on `96d748e5c`'s `src`:
+90 literals in 8 files** (`fileSelection.ts` 12, `buildGraph.ts` 2, `platform.ts` 12, `projectConfig.ts` 5, `render/render.ts`
+41, `render/types.ts` 5, `savPaths.ts` 6, `systemsStore.ts` 7); the design's 46 in 6 files was a different predicate (platform
+ids only, outside comments) that neither walk reproduces, and the 86 of the reviewer's independent scan differ from 90 by
+exactly the four `.gbc` literals its hard-coded set omitted. A fixture holds six literals (a bare one, a `.nes`, a `*.gba`
+glob, a template span, a literal after a substitution template and one after a regular expression) and a comment and a
+generated module it must skip; the old scanner found 3 of the 6. The real tree prints `{"literals":[]}`.

+## 11. As built (the prototype)
+
+The prototype, on `feature/modularize` over the design commit `96d748e5c`, is five commits, one per stage, each built by
+DeepSeek Flash and reviewed by Opus, with the reviews' fix passes folded into the commit they belong to by fixup and
+autosquash, so the five trees stand as final (the last pass folded into all five at once, which is why a stage report's sha
+is older than the branch's). Sections 3 to 10 above were corrected in place to what the build found; this section is the
+record of how, and the plan is written against it.
+
+**The stages**, by commit subject and current sha:
+
+1. `cf1d152da feat(f4a): register the consoles as package descriptors`: `core/ts/consoles.ts`, the `retroplug.consoles`
+   manifest member and `src/generated/consoles.ts`, the three consoles modules, `src/consoles.ts` and `src/platform.ts` over
+   it, open `Platform` / `Core`, `projectConfig` validation, `buildGraph`'s tables off the descriptors, `savPaths` and
+   `fileSelection` extensions.
+2. `81e6f0f60 feat(f4a): render through the console registry and the carts' render hooks`: `trackerRender.ts`, the three
+   carts' render modules, `render.ts` and the CLI session off every platform switch, `RenderContext.registry`.
+3. `60762c266 feat(f4a): the tracker playback and song-import hooks, and the shell's pollers through them`: `playback`,
+   `sramSignature`, `songImport` and the manifest `capture`, the controller poll, `controller.ts`, `fileDrop`, `songImportHost`.
+4. `898d87866 feat(f4a): the role hooks, the embedded ROM and the cart-named API`: `parameters`, `deriveConfig`,
+   `hostLatencyMs`, link groups, `savFromJson` out of the caps, the TS embed and its pairing, `loadEmbedded`,
+   `compileKitFormat` and every caller.
+5. `0ccc5a9cf feat(f4a): the shell's boundary, the doors gone and the tests with their code`: the four doors deleted, tests
+   moved to their packages, rule 9, the literal scanner, `migrate-v3-frozen`, the docs pass.
+
+The branch is 231 files, +8375 -2328 over the design commit (per commit now: stage 1 35 files, stage 2 26, stage 3 33, stage 4 95,
+stage 5 100). Nothing was pushed.
+
+**What each review found, and what the fix pass changed.**
+
+1. *Stage 1 (with fixes, no Critical).* Important: the first cut generated the descriptors into `packages.ts`, so the planner's
+   bundle went from 12 modules to 210 (780 KB) and F1's bundle-protocol invariant was loosened in its test to let it pass;
+   real carts had no uniqueness refusals; `linkGroupOf` and `exportModeOf` scanned every descriptor rather than reading the
+   system's (and `directGraph` was half converted); and the registry test checked the data, not the new lookups. Thirteen
+   minors. Fix pass: the `retroplug.consoles` manifest member and `generated/consoles.ts` (controller decision, section 3),
+   `bundle-protocol.test.ts` restored byte for byte (16 modules, 29,230 bytes), the two cart uniqueness refusals, both lookups
+   keyed by node type, the recorded tables replayed through `systemKnobs`, `droppedKnobs`, `classifyRom` and `buildGraph`'s own
+   shapes, the `detectorAnswer` guard (RED shown), `drivesRealCartOf` answering true for a platform with no cart. The last
+   pass added `consoles.ts` to `bundles.cmake`'s byproducts.
+2. *Stage 2 (with fixes).* Critical: a `seedSong` that answered null was dropped and a legacy risa catalog rendered the wrong
+   song silently where the old code threw. Important: the first E2 case passed on the old code; `render-cli.test.ts:94`'s
+   expectation had been changed outside E1 to E4; and the moved code had been rewritten (LSDj's 8-character `--song` match,
+   risa's `; rendering a fixed Nms` clause, the smsggdj and LSDj listings, the split log lines, the smsggdj Pause gate, the
+   loops-forever warning's place). Fix pass: `seedRefusal`, `songNameLength`, `songList`, `warnings` and the facts argument,
+   every moved text and gate restored verbatim, `render-cli.test.ts` byte-identical to its pre-stage text, E2 rebuilt to pin
+   the full cap. Stage 3's pass also took `drivesRealCartOf`'s fall-through and a garbled comment.
+3. *Stage 3 (with fixes, no Critical).* Important: the E3 test pinned no store behaviour; E3 was wider than the design said (the
+   gate is the ROM's roles, so a generic ROM beside an LSDj battery reads nothing, and `launchpad.test`'s `withCart` fixture had
+   to change); and the previous fix pass was not byte-identical (the split refusals were reworded, three outputs lost an em
+   dash, a malformed LSDj battery no longer threw, a generic ROM beside a tracker battery was newly refused). Controller
+   decisions: a store-level E3 case; the widened E3 and the generic-ROM refusal accepted as design edges (E3, E7), because they
+   follow from decisions 4 and 5; the split refusals rebuilt byte-identical from the descriptors' labels; the em dash kept in
+   OUTPUT through `\u2014` escapes; the malformed-battery throw restored. The generator's capture rule (wired node, a
+   `serialOut` `out`) and the reader cache keyed by ROM path came in the same pass.
+4. *Stage 4 (with fixes, no Critical).* Important: `derivedRoleConfigs` lost the empty-read guard, so an unreadable ROM
+   overwrote a stored `chip` with the 2A03 default (fixed, section 4.5, with a case, RED shown). Nine minors: the embed's
+   platform plumbing (`construct` looks it up by id), the same-package duplicate embed and the manifest-side fixtures,
+   `hostLatencyMs`'s doc, `ROLE_HEADER_LEN` in core and the dead `providerHeaderLength`, `parameters.ts` leftovers, the kit
+   spec types imported through `audioDriver`, `compileKitFormat` throwing synchronously (now async), `controllerModel`
+   reading the battery on every call, `savPathOf`, `inheritLinkGroup` across consoles, and two inherited em dashes. Decision:
+   the `got other` text restored for byte identity. The last pass changed `inheritLinkGroup` to compare the cable fields.
+5. *Stage 5 and the whole prototype (with fixes).* Critical: the scanner test drove a bare `ts.createScanner` and lost its place
+   after templates and regular expressions, finding 46 of 86 literals on the base (section 7.2). Important: the shell lost its
+   only end-to-end song-import test in the moves; `migrate-v3-frozen` iterated the packages' current lists, so it could not
+   fail on a reorder; and the docs pass left false statements (`src/kit` as the compiler's home, spec/06's capture shape,
+   AGENTS.md's generated modules, "empty allowlist"). Also rule 9's relative-import gap, comments reworded only to dodge the
+   exit grep (reverted, the grep now matches import specifiers), wrapping, a duplicate import. Fix pass (folded into all five
+   commits): the syntax-tree scanner over registry-derived sets, `systems/lsdj-song-import` restored, `V3_ROLE_ENUMS` exported
+   and the test over the frozen lists, rule 9's relative half with its fixture, the docs fixed (`AGENTS.md`, `spec/02`, `04`,
+   `06`, `07`, `docs/lsdj.md`, `docs/package-split.md`, `dsp/ts/kitContract.ts`). The whole-prototype review's verdict: every
+   behaviour change sanctioned, every departure recorded, and the growth below attributed.
+
+**Departures from the design as committed (`96d748e5c`), and why.**
+
+- **Console descriptors come through a `retroplug.consoles` manifest member and an import-light `src/generated/consoles.ts`,
+  not the app module or `packages.ts`.** The planner's bundle is `buildGraph.ts`'s, and the descriptors are its tables; through
+  the app they dragged every app, every role schema and zod into it (12 to 210 modules), which breaks F1's invariant.
+  `PackageContributions` carries no `consoles` or `realCarts`; n8's cart is `n8/ts/consoles.ts`. Same pattern as F1's protocol
+  tables.
+- **`ConsoleDescriptor.exportModes`** (not in the design's interface): `pinsPlusRef` has an export mode and no split, so the
+  mode's ordinal cannot come from a split's `tapMode` (`parity/render-shapes` caught it).
+- **Mesen lists its GBA before its NES**, because a platform's registry place is behaviour (`siblingRomCandidates` pins `gb, gbc,
+  gba, nes, sms, gg`), so the validation message names `gb, gba, nes, sms, gg` and not the design's example order.
+- **The registry's extra lookups** (section 3), `systemNodeTypeFor` throwing for an unregistered platform, `exportModeOf` and
+  `linkGroupOf` keyed by node type, `drivesRealCartOf` gaining an optional platform, `detectorAnswer`, and `rank` ties broken by
+  descriptor id (a total order).
+- **`platformSchema` and `coreSchema` are exported `superRefine`s** (a choice: the message names the set read at run time).
+- **The generator's refusals are emitted into the generated modules**, not raised by the script, where they need TypeScript
+  data (a role's category, an app's `embeds`); the data-only ones sit in `consoles.ts`. Two real-cart uniqueness refusals were
+  added.
+- **`TrackerRender` gained `warnings`, `songNameLength`, `songList` and `seedRefusal`, and `playingProbe` takes `RenderFacts`**;
+  `RenderHost` has no `readFile`; `PLAY_HOLD_MS` is tracker's one value. Each exists to keep an old text or condition exactly.
+- **Each tracker member's contract is a tracker module** (`trackerRender`, `trackerPlayback`, `trackerSongImport`,
+  `trackerSramSignature`), the cart's implementation beside the cart.
+- **The capture mapping is manifest data** (`capture` on `rp.lsdj.sync` in `PROTOCOL_NODES`), not `playback.captureFor`, so the
+  planner resolves no integration; the generator refuses six malformed shapes.
+- **The `--song` and `--list-songs` refusal names the integrations' labels** (`LSDj, SMSGGDJ, Risa (this ROM runs no tracker:
+  its console is Game Boy)`), not `label (platform label)`; no contract ties an integration to a platform.
+- **E3 is wider than designed and E7 is new** (section 6): the gate is the ROM's roles; a generic ROM beside a tracker battery
+  reads no playback and refuses the song flags. Both accepted by the controller as consequences of decisions 4 and 5.
+- **`songImport.import` takes a `SongImportHost` adapter** (`src/songImportHost.ts`), and `savPathOf` answers null for a system
+  that went away, in which case the import refuses; the design passed the store's pieces ad hoc.
+- **One shared `src/rolesForRom.ts`** serves the store and the render; `ROLE_HEADER_LEN` lives in core; `derivedRoleConfigs`
+  applies nothing to an unreadable file.
+- **The embed pairing is checked by the generated `packages.ts`**, which also refuses a declaration repeated inside one package;
+  the generator script reads and validates the manifest side. The start menu's mGB row is generated from `embeddedRoms()`.
+- **`compileKit` and `compileDmc` became `compileLsdjKit` and `compileRisaKit`** (the old names could not survive the exit grep),
+  and **`compileKitFormat` is async** (an unknown id rejects).
+- **`inheritLinkGroup` compares the two systems' cable fields**, and reads the group as a number.
+- **Rule 9's allowlist is 24 entries derived from the tree**, with a refusal of a relative import out of `src` the design did not
+  have; `EXCEPTIONS` stays empty and rule 9's `SHELL_IMPORTS` is the one deliberate list.
+- **The scanner walks the syntax tree and reads its sets from the registry**, finding `.gbc` too; RED 90 literals in 8 files on
+  `96d748e5c`.
+- **Decision 13's test iterates the frozen lists** and `V3_ROLE_ENUMS` is exported.
+- **Two non-TypeScript edits**, against "no C++ and no CMake": `SystemNode.test.cpp`'s `[settings]` oracle read the tables out
+  of `buildGraph.ts` textually and now reads the descriptors (`descriptorSource(type)`, no case added, removed or
+  re-recorded); and `bundles.cmake`'s byproduct list names `consoles.ts`. No C++ source or build rule changed.
+- **`Object.hasOwn` is spelled `hasOwnProperty.call`** (the shell's lib target refuses `TS2550`).
+- **The exit grep for the old API excludes dated records** (`docs/audit-2026-09-20.md`, the plan and design documents), and the
+  docs pass touched `spec/04`, `spec/07`'s D2 bullet, `docs/lsdj.md`, `docs/package-split.md` and `dsp/ts/kitContract.ts`
+  beyond the design's list, because each stated something F4a made false.
+- **One shell test kept** (`systems/lsdj-song-import`) where the design moved all song-import cases to lsdj.
+
+Existing tests whose expectations or fixtures changed, each judged by a stage review: the three `savFromJson` tests (section
+4.6), `test/controller/songRefresh.test.ts` and `test/menu/launchpad.test.ts` (E3), `test/file-drop/route.test.ts`
+(`targetSongExtensions` and the reason), `test-native/sms-render.test.ts` (`validateRenderOpts` takes the hooks),
+`test-native/risa-render.test.ts` (`renderSongs`), the mock render contexts (a registry), `build-graph.test.ts` (the two
+lookups' signatures) and `kit-baseline.test.ts` (a comment rewrap, no data). `render-cli.test.ts` is byte-identical to the
+design commit's. No golden, baseline, digest, image or pack byte moved at any stage, and no `RP_*_UPDATE` was set.
+
+**Verification.** A baseline run at `96d748e5c` and a run at every stage and at the tip were each 43 legs (`tip-verify.sh`: the
+F2 kit's 42 plus the measure), every one exit 0, and each stage's summary matched the baseline's but for the counts below.
+The tip's run is `/tmp/f4apro/s5fv-*`, taken on the tip's tree.
+
+| | baseline | tip (`0ccc5a9cf`) |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `pnpm test` | 190 files, 1999 cases, 0 skips | 207 files, 2094 cases, 0 skips |
+| `test:native` (fixtures, `RP_FAIL_ON_SKIP=1`) | 172 files, 629 ok, 2 bench skips | identical |
+| `test:native` (no fixtures, the CI picture) | 172 files, 629 ok, 144 skips | identical |
+| parity (strict) | 30 files, 250 cases | identical |
+| `test:ui` | 42 files, 46 cases | identical |
+| `test:plugin` / the engine-graph binary | 13 binaries, 336 cases (325 passed, 11 skipped) | identical cases; assertion totals move run to run (1,701,888 and 1,701,892; 1,713,639 and 1,713,850) |
+| `check:boundaries`, `check:docs`, `typecheck` | 0 refusals, 93 files clean, 0 | identical, with rule 9 in force |
+| tsan and asan (engine-graph, graph, n8, launchpad, devmode, kit) | 172 / 80 / 104 / 53 / 51 and 172 / 296 / 104 / 96 / 3 cases | identical |
+| kit baseline, render baseline, `render-chunks`, `render-cli`, the risa and sms render suites | 3 / 9, 5, 5, 6 | identical (hashes unchanged) |
+| device check, box, device mode | totals, `flash 199920`, 96 cases | identical |
+| images (box native `af36f223`, PIO `4b4f9abc`, check `38665e2c`) and the three `bliptoaster` pack byte hashes | recorded | identical (`diff` of the logs is empty) |

+| `reaper:params`, `reaper:params-clap` | not run at the baseline | PASS: 2725 and 644 parameters before and after the click on `Load mGB`, count unchanged |
+
+Two stage runs were not clean first time, both recorded: stage 2's `asandevmode` exited 42 once on a loaded machine (the
+timing-sensitive `ScriptPack` deadline case under ASAN; 96/96 on the re-run, no device-mode code touched), and stage 3's first
+`native` and `nativeci` runs failed on `render-cli.test.ts`'s line because a fold had put the test's restore in the wrong commit
+(re-folded, both green with the baseline's totals). The test delta is the stages' own cases (+17 files, +95 cases net of the
+moves; the moved files' cases are conserved and one new shell file is `bliptoaster/rolesForRom`).
+
+**Bundle sizes** (`measure.sh`, recorded and not gated; `/tmp/f4apro/base-measure.log` against `s5fv-measure.log`):
+
+| Bundle | base | tip | growth |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |

+| `cp-bundle.js` | 1,141,126 | 1,176,381 | +35,255 |
+| `render-worker-bundle.js` | 1,189,430 | 1,225,868 | +36,438 |
+| `ui-bundle.js` | 1,943,736 | 1,981,163 | +37,427 |

+| `dsp-kernel`, `script`, `script-test`, `ts-stripper` | | | 0 |
+
+The binaries grow 25 to 78 KB (the embedded TypeScript), `libmesen` and its 288 objects are unchanged, and the planner bundle
+stays import-light (16 modules and 29,230 bytes after stage 1's fix, 15 modules and 29,184 bytes at stage 4, no app, generated
+`packages.ts` or zod module in either). The reviewer's per-stage attribution (each stage's increment, in KB;
+the fix pass over stage 5 added 47 to 128 bytes):
+

+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| cp | +10.5 | +9.6 | +8.4 | +5.8 | +0.8 |
+| cli | +10.6 | +10.1 | +8.4 | +14.0 | +1.0 |
+| render worker | +11.0 | -0.1 | +9.6 | +14.7 | +1.2 |

+Qualitatively: stage 1 is the descriptor data, the registry and the generated module's checks; stage 2 is the render hooks now
+reaching every registry bundle (the render worker is flat because it already carried `render.ts`); stage 3 is playback, song
+import and `sramSignature`, which reach the render worker too; stage 4 is the CC tables, `rolesForRom` and the embed (the control
+plane gains least because it already carried `parameterMap`'s tables); stage 5 is the generated checks, with no doors. No new
+package entered any bundle and the planner bundle is unchanged. The growth is the descriptors plus hook code that hangs on
+objects every registry-loading bundle already imports (section 10); it has not been attributed module by module.
+
+**What acceptance must run beyond tip-verify** (from the whole-prototype review):
+
+- **A module-by-module bundle diff.** Run `tools/build-session.js`'s `bundleInputs` for each bundle entry (cp, ui, cli, render

+  registry modules and the hook code, and no package may newly appear.

+- **The fixtures-present run with `RP_FAIL_ON_SKIP=1`** for parity, the render baseline, `render-cli`, `render-chunks`,
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f4apro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
The four doors are deleted and every importer names the owning package: a kit
caller imports @retroplug/lsdj/kitFormat or @retroplug/risa/kitFormat (and the
spec types from @retroplug/dsp), a tracker caller imports the cart catalog or
integration it wants, src/tracker's live-save helpers are ./tracker/liveSav,
trackerRegistry keeps only the generated list and its resolvers, and audioDriver
keeps its facade and drops its re-exports. The v2-to-v3 migration freezes the
five cart-owned enum lists beside the step, so projectConfig no longer imports
sameboy, mesen or lsdj: the shell's sources name no package but core, tracker,
dsp and launchpad.

Rule 9 of the boundary check holds the shell to an explicit list of contract
modules, each with its reason, and fails an entry no import uses; src/generated
is unjudged. A scanner test refuses a platform id or a ROM-extension literal in
packages/retroplug/src, read with TypeScript's own scanner rather than a regular
expression, so a comment or a template's text is told apart from a literal.

Tests follow their code into the packages' ts/test: the parameter tables to mgb
and bliptoaster, the .lsdprj planner and the song importer to lsdj (the importer
over a fake SongImportHost), each cart's render hooks to its cart, LSDj's
working-song signature to lsdj, BlipToaster's byte-level detection to bliptoaster
with the rolesForRom case staying in the shell. The shell tests that drive carts
end to end stay. One new case pins each importer's savPathOf refusal.

The docs catch up: AGENTS.md's package paragraph gains the consoles member, the
tracker hooks, loadEmbedded and compileKitFormat and rule 9; spec/00, 02, 03, 06,
07 and 13 and docs/package-split.md record the consoles and embeds contributions,
the capture field, the boundary rule, the scanner test, the package's own tests
and F4a's own bullet, with F4b and per-product bundles owed.
EOF
````

This task commits nothing (unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit of its own, named for what it fixes). It is the
phase's acceptance: the tree and a full build, every leg of `/tmp/f4apro/tip-verify.sh` (the 43 legs the baseline and
every stage ran), the three oracle families under their require flags, both device images and the pack's bytes, the SDL
legs, the two Reaper parameter runs and the whole Reaper suite, a fresh clone, the boundary and docs checks, both
consumer suites, and the four legs the whole-prototype review asked for beyond the script. It is run on the tree the five
tasks leave, from a state the build has not touched where a leg says so, and its figures are compared with the baseline
recorded at `96d748e5c` (`/tmp/f4apro/base-summary.txt` and `base-*.log`) and with the final verification at the
prototype's tip (`/tmp/f4apro/s5fv-summary.txt` and `s5fv-*.log`). **There is no hardware leg: no step may touch the NES,
the N8, the Pico box, the probe, the Zoom L6 or any MIDI interface, and the hardware safety rules in this plan's header
govern every step here too.**

The kit is `/tmp/f4apro/tip-verify.sh`, the baseline's and every stage's. Write it to a scratch path of its own (never

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cd /workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish
L=${TVL:-/tmp/f4apro/tv}
run() { local n=$1; shift; "$@" > $L-$n.log 2>&1; echo "$n exit $?" >> $L-summary.txt; }
: > $L-summary.txt
run build cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
run typecheck pnpm typecheck
run test pnpm test
run plugin pnpm test:plugin
run egfix env RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources build/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test
run parity env RP_FAIL_ON_SKIP=1 RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources pnpm test:native parity
run native env RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources pnpm test:native
run nativeci env RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/nonexistent-rp-resources RISA_SRC=/nonexistent-rp-risa pnpm test:native
run ui env RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources pnpm test:ui
run node pnpm test:node
run clits pnpm test:cli-ts
run docs pnpm check:docs
run n8 pnpm test:n8
S="suppressions=$PWD/packages/native/test/sanitizer/tsan.supp halt_on_error=1"
run tsanbuild cmake --build build-tsan --target retroplug-engine-graph-test retroplug-graph-test retroplug-n8-test -j$(nproc)
run tsaneg env TSAN_OPTIONS="$S" RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources build-tsan/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test "[host-io],[systems],[b2],[alloc],[devices],[capability],[n8-node],[n8-adapters],[providers],[launchpad],[offline],[engine-jobs]"
run tsang env TSAN_OPTIONS="$S" build-tsan/bin/retroplug-graph-test "[dsp],[dsp-nodes],[dsp-resample],[dsp-buffer-nodes],[resource],[resources]"
run tsann8 env TSAN_OPTIONS="$S" build-tsan/bin/retroplug-n8-test
run tsanlp bash -c 'cmake --build build-tsan --target retroplug-launchpad-test -j$(nproc) && TSAN_OPTIONS="suppressions=$PWD/packages/native/test/sanitizer/tsan.supp halt_on_error=1" build-tsan/bin/retroplug-launchpad-test' 
run tsandevmode bash -c 'cmake -S . -B build-tsan >/dev/null && cmake --build build-tsan --target retroplug-device-mode-test -j$(nproc) && TSAN_OPTIONS="suppressions=$PWD/packages/native/test/sanitizer/tsan.supp halt_on_error=1" build-tsan/bin/retroplug-device-mode-test "[script-pack]"'
run asanbuild cmake --build build-asan --target retroplug-engine-graph-test retroplug-graph-test retroplug-n8-test -j$(nproc)
run asaneg env ASAN_OPTIONS="abort_on_error=1 detect_leaks=1" RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources build-asan/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test "[host-io],[systems],[b2],[alloc],[devices],[capability],[n8-node],[n8-adapters],[providers],[launchpad],[offline],[engine-jobs]"
run asang env ASAN_OPTIONS="abort_on_error=1 detect_leaks=1" build-asan/bin/retroplug-graph-test
run asann8 env ASAN_OPTIONS="abort_on_error=1 detect_leaks=1" build-asan/bin/retroplug-n8-test
run asandevmode bash -c 'cmake --build build-asan --target retroplug-device-mode-test -j$(nproc) && ASAN_OPTIONS="abort_on_error=1 detect_leaks=1" build-asan/bin/retroplug-device-mode-test'
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f4apro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

list, and fails when a real port appears. **Run neither any other way.**

````text
  ok: nothing selected, nothing claimed; unclaimed, the device's notes reach the shared stream
  ok: reclaimed before MIDI opens and audio starts; its notes kept out of the shared stream; released at quit
  ok: Programmer mode first, LED traffic, the release last
  ok: a real scan found and confirmed the device, saved it, and claimed it mid-session - its notes stop, others' do not, the shared output steps aside
  ok: a second standalone leaves the first one's device alone, and does not hear its pads
````

- [ ] **Step 8: The legs the whole-prototype review asked for**

Four legs beyond `tip-verify.sh`, from the review's list in the design's section 11: a module-by-module bundle diff,
the two red proofs re-run over full archives, a v2 project load through the frozen lists, and `measure.sh`'s sizes
against the baseline. **(a) The bundle diff.** `tools/build-session.js`'s `bundleInputs(entry, format)` bundles in
memory and returns every module that went in and the output's size, which is the instrumentation the repo already has
(the planner bundle's `bundle-no-zod`/`bundle-protocol` tests use it), and it resolves its entry against the process's
working directory: the shell's entries are written `src/...` because the bundle-protocol test runs from
`packages/retroplug`, so the recorder changes there before it loads the tree's esbuild. The UI bundle is not a
build-session one: `tools/build-ui.js` builds it with its own options (the React aliases and the nodePaths of
`tools/esbuild-shared.js`), so the recorder runs that script and reads the depfile it writes from esbuild's metafile,
which is the module list. Run it in a checkout of the base and in this tree, and diff the module lists and sizes: the
growth must be the new contract and registry modules and the hook code, and no package's app, node or integration
module may newly appear. Do it from two clones so neither tree's generated modules leak into the other's answer.

Write the recorder to a scratch path (it is not part of the repository) and run it once per tree: it bundles each
entry with the tree's own esbuild and node modules, and prints every module that went in and the output's size, so two
runs diff cleanly. The base clone has no submodules: link each of its `.gitmodules` paths to this worktree's checkout
(the UI bundle reaches dpf.js and React through them), install offline, and run the base's generator first (its
sources import the generated `protocol.ts`, which a clone has none of).

````js
// Records, per bundle, the modules esbuild put in and the output's size: the module-by-module diff the final review
// asked for (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md section 11). Run it with the tree to record as its argument:
//
//   node /tmp/f4a-accept/bundle-modules.mjs <tree>
//
// The build-session entries resolve against packages/retroplug, which is where the repo's own bundle-protocol test runs
// (and where its entry strings are written), so the recorder changes there before it loads the tree's esbuild: the
// metafile's paths, and the `// <path>` comment esbuild writes above each module, are relative to the process's working
// directory. The UI bundle is not a build-session one: tools/build-ui.js builds it with its own options (the React
// aliases and nodePaths from tools/esbuild-shared.js), so the recorder runs that script and reads the depfile it writes
// from the metafile, which is the module list; the output's size is the file's.
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { chdir } from "node:process";
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";

if (!process.argv[2]) throw new Error("usage: node bundle-modules.mjs <tree>");
const tree = resolve(process.argv[2]);
const outDir = resolve(process.argv[3] ?? "/tmp/f4a-accept/bundles");
mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });

// The five build-session bundles: the entries and formats packages/native/CMakeLists.txt and cmake/bundles.cmake
// name (cp is the control plane's own script, which bundles with the same options).
const ENTRIES = [
  ["cp", "src/pluginControlPlane.ts", "esm"],
  ["cli", "cli/cli.ts", "esm"],
  ["worker", "src/render/worker.ts", "iife"],
  ["sdk", "cli/sdk.ts", "esm"],
  ["planner", "src/graph/buildGraph.ts", "esm"],
];

chdir(`${tree}/packages/retroplug`);
const require = createRequire(`${tree}/packages/retroplug/`);
const { bundleInputs } = require(`${tree}/tools/build-session.js`);
const norm = (p) => relative(tree, resolve(p)).split(sep).join("/");

const out = {};
for (const [name, entry, format] of ENTRIES) {
  const r = bundleInputs(entry, format);
  out[name] = { modules: r.inputs.length, bytes: r.bytes, inputs: r.inputs.map(norm).sort() };
}

const uiJs = resolve(outDir, "ui-bundle.js");
const uiD = `${uiJs}.d`;
execFileSync(process.execPath, [`${tree}/tools/build-ui.js`, uiJs, uiD, `${tree}/packages/retroplug/ui/main.tsx`], {
  cwd: tree,
  stdio: ["ignore", "ignore", "inherit"],
});
const dep = readFileSync(uiD, "utf8").replace(/\\\n\s*/g, " ");
const uiInputs = dep
  .slice(dep.indexOf(":") + 1)
  .trim()
  .split(/\s+/)
  .filter((p) => p !== "")
  .map((p) => p.replace(/\\ /g, " ").replace(/\\\\/g, "\\"))
  .map(norm)
  .sort();
out.ui = { modules: uiInputs.length, bytes: statSync(uiJs).size, inputs: uiInputs };

console.log(JSON.stringify(out, null, 1));
````

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# measure.sh: product binary sizes, the mesen library and its objects (recorded, never gated).
cd /workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish
for f in build/bin/retroplug build/bin/retroplug-cli build/bin/retroplug-host build/bin/retroplug-sdl \
         build/bin/retroplug-ui-test build/bin/retroplug-render-host-test build/bin/retroplug-vst2.so \
         build/bin/retroplug.clap build/bin/retroplug.vst3 build/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test build/bin/retroplug-audio-test; do
  if [ -d "$f" ]; then echo "$(du -sb "$f" | cut -f1) $f"; elif [ -e "$f" ]; then echo "$(stat -c %s "$f") $f"; fi
done
find build -name 'retroplug-node*.node' -exec stat -c '%s %n' {} \; 2>/dev/null
echo "libmesen $(stat -c %s build/deps/mesen/libmesen.a 2>/dev/null)"
echo "mesen objects $(ar t build/deps/mesen/libmesen.a | grep -c "\.o$") members, $(ar tv build/deps/mesen/libmesen.a | awk '{s+=$3} END {print s}') bytes (ar tv)"
echo "cli text: $(size build/bin/retroplug-cli | tail -1)"
echo "cli console symbols: SnesPpu $(nm -C build/bin/retroplug-cli | grep -c 'SnesPpu::') GbPpu $(nm -C build/bin/retroplug-cli | grep -c 'GbPpu::') PceVdc $(nm -C build/bin/retroplug-cli | grep -c 'PceVdc::') WsPpu $(nm -C build/bin/retroplug-cli | grep -c 'WsPpu::')"
for b in build/native/*-bundle.js build/cli-sdk/retroplug-cli.js; do [ -e "$b" ] && echo "$(stat -c %s "$b") $b"; done
````
